title: Daemonization of jailed Firecracker (caller-controlled double-fork)
description:
**Caller-decides design (2026-05-07, user decision after weighing CLI vs library tradeoff):** daemonize is a JailerConfig flag with **default = false** (conservative, matches CLI conventions). Library callers that need the embedder-survives-VM property (Bestiary, server-mode embedders) explicitly pass `daemonize: true`. m80-cli keeps the default `false` until a `--detach` flag is requested.

Why caller-decides instead of default-on:
- m80-cli's interactive UX expects child-dies-with-parent semantics (Docker `docker run` convention; ~12 years of evidence that default-attached is the right CLI shape even when a daemon owns lifecycle).
- Without attach/reconnect (which doesn't exist yet), an orphaned-but-running VM after a m80-cli SIGKILL is worse UX than "VM gone" — the user can't interact with it, output stream is dropped, RAM is held until recover.rs reaps.
- Library callers (Bestiary) DO need the survives-orchestrator property; passing `daemonize: true` from their construction site is one line and makes the design call explicit at the use site.

FC's stock jailer supports a --daemonize flag that double-forks the Firecracker process so it runs as a background daemon, detached from the controlling terminal. m80 today manages FC as a child of the orchestrator. The capability must exist; the question this epic settles is *who decides* per-launch.

## Scope
- Add `daemonize: bool` to JailerConfig with **default = false**.
- When `daemonize: true`, double-fork: first fork creates a child that calls setsid; second fork creates a grandchild that execs FC. Parent exits at each level.
- Open /dev/null for stdin/stdout/stderr before chrooting (shared with m80-3xwa.2 B2).
- Persist daemon PID for monitoring (jailer-state.json already covers this).
- m80-cli does NOT set daemonize=true. (No `--detach` flag in this epic; can be a follow-up if requested.)
- Library callers set daemonize=true explicitly when they want the survives-orchestrator property.

## Cross-references and call-site coupling (when daemonize=true)
- **m80-isxo (CLONE_NEWPID)**: ordering matters. Daemonize AFTER PID-NS entry, so the double-fork happens inside the new PID namespace. The grandchild FC still becomes PID 1 in that namespace; the parent processes exit. Kata pattern.
- **m80-3xwa.2 B1** (session leadership + setsid): daemonization's first-fork-then-setsid step IS the B1 setsid call. Code-wise, B1 absorbs this case — they share the call site.
- **m80-3xwa.2 B2** (/dev/null open before chroot): daemonization's stdio redirection step IS B2. Same call site.

When daemonize=true, m80-3c9b + m80-isxo + m80-3xwa.2 B1 + m80-3xwa.2 B2 all converge on a single call sequence. Land them together (or at least design-coordinate so the call site supports the union). When daemonize=false, none of this applies — the existing direct-exec path is unchanged.

## Implications for daemonize=true callers
A library caller that sets daemonize=true takes on these responsibilities (m80 documents them; doesn't enforce):
1. **Signal trapping.** If the embedder gets SIGINT/SIGTERM, it must call Sandbox::stop() over the control channel before exiting. Otherwise the VM survives as an orphan.
2. **No process-group kill shortcut.** With FC detached, killing the embedder does not propagate to FC. All shutdown paths must go through API socket / vsock.
3. **Recover.rs becomes a happy-path mechanism.** Each m80 startup runs recover.rs to detect orphan jails (FC running but no embedder) and either adopt or kill them. With daemonize=false this only matters after crashes; with daemonize=true it matters every time the embedder restarts.
4. **Attach/reconnect (TODO at caller layer).** If the embedder wants to interact with a surviving orphan VM (resume streaming, query status), it needs API/vsock attach logic on top of recover.rs adoption. m80 provides the primitives (Sandbox handles can be reconstructed from recover.rs state); the embedder builds the UX.

For daemonize=false (m80-cli's path), none of the above applies — FC dies with the orchestrator and the workflow is the existing simple shape.

## Child tasks
1. IMPL: open /dev/null, fork, setsid, fork, exec when daemonize=true. Stdio redirection. PID file persistence. **Default the JailerConfig field to false.**
2. IMPL: lifecycle — daemonized VMs managed via API socket, not child process signals; inspect_run_dir handles daemonized PIDs. Confirm m80-firecracker stop/snapshot paths do not assume parent-child relationship (they should already not, since FC is API-driven).
3. IMPL: m80-jailer/src/recover.rs runs reliably on every m80 startup (today it's a manual entry point; make it routine).
4. TEST/DOCS: daemonized FC survives orchestrator exit; stop/snapshot work with daemonized VMs; non-daemonized path is unchanged.

## Acceptance
- daemonize: bool exists on JailerConfig; default false; opt-in true.
- When daemonize=false (the default), behavior is identical to today: FC is a child of the orchestrator, dies with it.
- When daemonize=true, orchestrator process can exit (cleanly or via SIGKILL) without killing the FC VM.
- recover.rs detects orphan jails on next m80 startup and provides a stable contract for adoption / cleanup.
- m80-cli: unchanged behavior; no signal-trap work needed for this epic (CLI keeps daemonize=false).
- Test: with daemonize=true, launch a VM, kill the orchestrator with SIGKILL, confirm FC is still running and reachable via its API socket; another m80 instance can detect it via recover.rs and stop it cleanly.

## Parking lot (not in this epic)
- `m80 launch --detach` flag in m80-cli (would set daemonize=true and exit immediately after VM launch, returning the VM ID for later management). File as a separate small task if/when an interactive use case surfaces.
- Attach/reconnect UX for surviving orphan VMs (output stream resume, status query). This is non-trivial and lives at the embedder layer; m80 provides primitives only.

## Audit-confirmed code references
- /tank/projects/firecracker/src/jailer/src/env.rs:662-669 — dev_null open (paired with m80-3xwa.2 B2)
- /tank/projects/firecracker/src/jailer/src/env.rs:716-766 — double-fork sequence
- /tank/projects/firecracker/src/jailer/src/env.rs:760-762 — dup2 stdio after second fork

## Sources
- /tmp/m80-proposed-epic-beads.md Epic 6.
- 12-agent audit Lens 2 (process/PID/session isolation), 2026-05-07.
- 2026-05-07 user design discussion: explored default-on, settled on caller-decides (default=false in JailerConfig, library callers opt in via explicit flag) after weighing CLI orphan-without-attach UX against library survives-orchestrator benefit.
notes: Implemented daemonized launch via official Firecracker jailer --daemonize. code=JailerConfig::daemonize, SandboxConfig::daemonize, m80-firecracker phase_4 propagation, MaterializedJail parent reaping with jailer_pid=0 sentinel, kill_pid(0) no-op for no-live-jailer parent. docs=docs/behaviors/jailer/daemonize.md plus m80-jailer and m80-firecracker READMEs. tests=materialized::launch_with_daemonize_reaps_jailer_parent_and_records_daemon_pid, lifecycle::kill_pid_zero_is_no_live_jailer_sentinel, plan_serde daemonize persistence, ignored real-KVM end_to_end_real_kvm_daemonized_boot_exec_stop_delete. Verification: rustfmt scoped touched Rust files; git diff --check; cargo test -p m80-jailer -p m80-firecracker --tests; cargo clippy -p m80-jailer -p m80-firecracker --all-targets -- -D warnings; sudo real-KVM daemonized smoke passed.

title: WRA0 follow-up: tighten protobuf wire contract
description:
Review follow-up for the protobuf hard-cutover. The implementation shape is directionally right, but the review found places where documented protocol guarantees are stronger than the code, stale docs survived the cutover, and public/internal surfaces are wider than they need to be.

Goal: make the protobuf wire boring and exact. Enforce the sequence/request-id invariants we document, remove stale or misleading compatibility/cap language, keep generated prost internals out of normal downstream use, and add malformed-peer regression coverage around the active hard-cutover wire.

Out of scope: restoring NDJSON/base64 compatibility, adding dual-version dispatch, or introducing product/agent semantics.

Acceptance: all child tasks are closed; crate READMEs and behavior docs match live code; focused tests prove malformed or out-of-contract peers fail closed with useful diagnostics.
notes: All seven follow-up tasks closed. Verification: cargo test -p m80-proto -p m80-guestd -p m80-firecracker; cargo clippy -p m80-proto -p m80-guestd -p m80-firecracker --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo test/clippy -p m80-vsock; git diff --check.

title: Enforce exec and PTY stream sequence invariants
description:
Finding 1: docs and error types promise stream sequence gaps/repeats fail closed, but host-side exec_streaming and exec_pty pass guest seq values through without validation.

Scope:
- Track expected stdout and stderr seq independently in RunningSandbox::exec_streaming.
- Track expected PTY output seq in RunningSandbox::exec_pty.
- On gap, repeat, or wrap mismatch, return FcError::Protocol(WireProtocolError::SequenceMismatch) and record protocol diagnostics with request_id and stream kind.
- Keep cross-stream ordering semantics unchanged: stdout and stderr may interleave; each stream is monotonic independently.

Acceptance:
- Unit/integration tests inject out-of-order exec stdout, exec stderr, and PTY output frames and prove SequenceMismatch.
- Existing real-KVM happy-path stream tests still pass.
- docs/behaviors/wire-protocol/stream-semantics.md remains true without weakening the contract.
notes: Enforced host-side seq checks for exec_stdout, exec_stderr, and pty_output before callbacks; added protocol-error regression tests in crates/m80-firecracker/src/lifecycle/exec.rs.

title: Validate chunked upload request and ack sequencing
description:
Finding 2: chunked upload uses upload_id and seq, but host and guest trust them too much. Host does not verify the response echoes the same upload_id/seq, and guest appends chunks without enforcing monotonic sequence within an upload.

Scope:
- Guest upload state tracks expected next chunk seq per upload id and rejects gaps/repeats with a typed file/protocol failure.
- Host upload_file_chunked verifies FileWriteChunkResponse upload_id and seq match the sent chunk before continuing.
- Replace wrapping/saturating sequence advancement with explicit overflow failure.
- Preserve one-connection begin/chunk/commit shape; no resume, no compatibility shim.

Acceptance:
- Guestd tests cover repeated, skipped, and stale upload chunk seq values.
- Host-side tests cover mismatched upload_id and mismatched seq in chunk ack.
- Docs say upload sequencing is enforced, not merely echoed.
notes: Validated host chunk acks for upload_id and seq; guestd now tracks next_seq and returns FileError::InvalidSequence for gaps/duplicates without appending; added host and guest regression tests.

title: Align direct file-write cap docs and code with protobuf frame cap
description:
Finding 4: direct FileWriteRequest has a guest-side 64 MiB guard and stale planning docs still mention a 64 MiB wire envelope, but the active protobuf frame cap is 4 MiB encoded body. The 64 MiB guard is misleading and mostly unreachable over the active wire.

Scope:
- Decide whether direct write relies solely on MAX_FRAME_BYTES or keeps a smaller/larger domain cap with a clear reason.
- Remove or rename WRITE_ENVELOPE_CAP so it does not imply a live 64 MiB wire envelope.
- Update docs/design/wire-fops.md and docs/planning/wire-features-bead-plan.md to name the active frame cap and chunked-upload escape path.

Acceptance:
- No docs claim active file-write envelopes are 64 MiB.
- Tests or docs prove large writes use upload_file_chunked rather than direct FileWriteRequest.
- m80-proto, m80-guestd, and m80-firecracker docs agree on the cap boundary.
notes: Removed stale 64 MiB guestd direct-write cap; docs now state inline writes are bounded by the active encoded protobuf frame cap and large transfers use chunked upload.

title: Remove stale application-channel handshake language
description:
Finding 3: HandshakeMessage rustdoc still says it is sent on every fresh connection before application payloads, but WRA0 deliberately removed the application-channel prelude. Version is carried on every envelope; the ready byte is boot readiness only.

Scope:
- Update m80-proto rustdoc for HandshakeMessage to describe it as reserved/test-only unless a future protocol explicitly activates it.
- Audit m80-proto README and wire-protocol handshake docs for any wording implying a reusable application-channel handshake.
- Keep negotiate_version as exact-match helper; do not add negotiation behavior.

Acceptance:
- Searching m80-proto docs/source for handshake no longer suggests a per-connection application prelude.
- Existing handshake_exchange tests are renamed or described as reserved payload round-trips, not active connection behavior.
notes: Reworded HandshakeMessage rustdoc and docs to reserve it for exact-version payload tests/future work; active app channels validate version per envelope and have no prelude.

title: Reclassify or remove redundant Envelope kind String
description:
Shape concern: the active protobuf envelope carries both a string kind discriminator and a prost oneof payload. That can be useful for diagnostics/raw dispatch, but the current README wording implies kind enables payload extension without a PROTOCOL_VERSION bump, which conflicts with hard-cutover doctrine and oneof tag changes.

Scope:
- Decide whether kind stays as diagnostic/raw-dispatch metadata or is removed from the active envelope.
- If it stays, update README/docs/rustdoc to stop presenting it as a compatibility-extension mechanism.
- Ensure decode still rejects kind/payload mismatches fail-closed if kind remains.
- If removed, simplify RawEnvelope and all dispatch code in one hard cutover.

Acceptance:
- m80-proto README accurately states what kind is for.
- Tests cover mismatch behavior or prove the field is gone.
- No docs suggest adding payload variants without a protocol-version bump.
notes: Kept Envelope.kind as dispatch/diagnostic metadata; README/rustdoc/docs no longer claim it enables payload extension without a protocol-version bump; existing decode mismatch remains fail-closed.

title: Narrow public exposure of prost generated wire types
description:
Shape concern: m80-proto publicly exposes wire::generated::*, making prost-generated internals part of the visible public surface even though the crate contract says callers should prefer typed payloads and frame helpers. Tests currently use generated structs for malformed/version cases, but normal downstream crates should not depend on them.

Scope:
- Decide whether generated structs can be crate-private or test-only exposed.
- Keep enough internal access for m80-proto conversion tests without widening downstream API.
- Update README Public Surface to match the final exposure.
- Avoid checking generated prost output into src; keep schema checked in and generated into OUT_DIR.

Acceptance:
- wire::generated::* is not documented as normal caller surface, or is no longer public.
- m80-proto tests still can build malformed/version fixtures.
- Downstream crates use typed payloads/RawEnvelope helpers rather than generated prost structs.
notes: Removed the root wire::* glob re-export of generated prost structs, marked wire::generated doc-hidden, and updated README to point normal callers at typed payloads/frame helpers.

title: Add malformed-peer regression tests for active protobuf streams
description:
Review gap: happy-path real-KVM coverage is strong, but malformed-peer coverage is uneven. The protocol docs promise fail-closed behavior for malformed frames, unsupported versions, unexpected kinds, sequence mismatches, duplicate/missing terminal frames, and disconnect-before-terminal. Coverage should pin those against the active protobuf wire, not old JSON/base64 cases.

Scope:
- Add host-side tests for malformed protobuf, unsupported version, unexpected frame, disconnect before terminal, and sequence mismatch across file read, exec stream, and PTY stream where practical.
- Add guest-side tests for malformed host control frames during streaming exec, PTY, and file upload loops.
- Ensure protocol diagnostics include request_id and stream/kind context.
- Do not add compatibility or tolerant parsing paths to make malformed inputs pass.

Acceptance:
- Tests fail if malformed peers are silently ignored where the contract says fail closed.
- Tests use protobuf frame helpers/raw envelopes, not JSON/NDJSON fixtures.
- docs/behaviors/wire-protocol/stream-semantics.md evidence list points at the new tests.
notes: Added host sequence and upload-ack malformed-peer tests, guest upload gap/duplicate tests, and stream-semantics evidence list pointing at active protobuf malformed/version diagnostics.

title: Achieve isolation parity with Firecracker jailer (and selected kata/smolvm primitives)
description:
Umbrella tracking the 12 epics that close legitimate isolation/sandbox-correctness gaps surfaced by two comparative audits in the same 2026-05-07 session: (1) 12-agent jailer audit (m80-jailer vs Firecracker jailer + kata-containers + smolvm/libkrun); (2) 20-agent guest-daemon deep audit (10 kata-agent + 10 smolvm-agent lenses).

## Audit methodology

### 12-agent jailer audit
12 Explore agents × 3 source trees × specific lenses:
- 6 agents on /tank/projects/firecracker/src/jailer/src/ (env.rs, chroot.rs, cgroup.rs, resource_limits.rs, main.rs):
  - Mount/FS isolation
  - Process/PID/session isolation
  - Cgroup + setrlimit
  - Network isolation (netns)
  - Credentials/capabilities/seccomp
  - Cmdline/exec hygiene + filesystem ops
- 3 agents on /tank/projects/kata-containers/src/ (dragonball, runtime-rs, agent, rustjail):
  - Runtime/dragonball isolation primitives
  - kata-agent in-VM primitives
  - Storage/network/device hot-plug flows
- 3 agents on /tank/projects/smolvm/ + libkrun:
  - smolvm jailer/sandbox
  - smolvm in-guest agent
  - smolvm perf/launch/snapshot

Total findings: 33 legitimate (M = real gap, SO = should offer) items captured.

### 20-agent guest-daemon deep audit
20 Explore agents × 2 in-VM agents × specific lenses (Firecracker has no guest daemon, so no FC dispatch):
- 10 on /tank/projects/kata-containers/src/agent/: PID-1 init, vsock/ttrpc, exec/spawn, supervision, file ops, in-guest cgroup, caps/seccomp ordering, device hot-plug, storage, in-guest networking.
- 10 on /tank/projects/smolvm/crates/smolvm-agent/: PID-1 init, vsock framing, exec/supervision, PTY, OCI/crun, storage, DNS proxy, SSH agent forwarding, network primitives, retry/error recovery.

Output: ~25 confirmations of already-filed items (with deeper implementation specs), ~30 net-new gaps to capture, ~45 D items (different by design / out of scope). Net-new gaps surfaced 5 candidate child epics (m80-3xwa.6-10) currently in proposal stage.

## Children covering the findings

### Already-filed (audit confirmed all 6 + m80-iswt + m80-27lf)
- **m80-jmqg** (P1) — pivot_root + mount NS isolation
- **m80-8o58** (P2) — setrlimit (RLIMIT_NOFILE/FSIZE)
- **m80-16oi** (P2) — mknod for /dev/{kvm,net/tun,urandom}
- **m80-isxo** (P2) — CLONE_NEWPID
- **m80-bcb6** (P3) — copy FC binary (covert-channel mitigation)
- **m80-3c9b** (P3) — --daemonize double-fork
- **m80-iswt** (P1) — m80-side conveyor-belt primitives (extended with E1/E2/E3 from 12-agent audit + E4/E5/E6/E7 from 20-agent deep audit)
- **m80-27lf** (P3) — cosign/sigstore image-policy verification (kata parity)

### New children filed alongside this umbrella
- **m80-3xwa.1** (P2) — Mount/FS hardening (Group A, 6 items)
- **m80-3xwa.2** (P2) — Process/credentials hardening (Group B, 10 items including B10 SELinux from deep audit)
- **m80-3xwa.3** (P2) — Cgroup hardening (Group C, 6 items)
- **m80-3xwa.4** (P3) — NetworkPolicy::JoinNetns mode (Group D, 1 item)
- **m80-3xwa.5** (P2) — m80-guestd hardening + verbs (Groups F+G, 8 items, with F1/F2/F3/G3 implementation specs from deep audit)

### Proposed but not yet filed (from 20-agent deep audit synthesis)
- m80-3xwa.6 — Vsock transport hardening (Group K, 5 items)
- m80-3xwa.7 — SSH agent forwarding via vsock (Group N, 8 items)
- m80-3xwa.8 — Boot/init completeness in m80-guestd (Group H, 5 items)
- m80-3xwa.9 — Workload exec hardening in m80-guestd (Groups I+J+L, 8 items)
- m80-3xwa.10 — Retry/error recovery primitive (Group P, 3 items)

## Documented architectural divergences (not gaps; recorded for clarity)
- m80 uses virtio-blk + overlayfs, not virtio-fs (deliberate; simpler kernel surface for stripped image)
- m80 acquires privilege at startup via setcap or run-as-root; no rootless/per-call privilege model (kata + libkrun support rootless; m80 deliberately doesn't)
- m80 is one-VM-per-tenant (conveyor-belt); kata's multi-container-per-VM cgroup model doesn't apply
- m80 uses inverted readiness (m80-7tpy guest-connects-to-host) instead of marker-file polling (smolvm) or accept-loop polling (FC)
- m80 net policy is host-side iptables/NAT (m80-net-outbound); FC jailer has no firewall-level policy (only netns join). Group D adds JoinNetns as a third mode; the existing modes stay.
- m80 network does not support port-mapping, by CLAUDE.md (caller-owned)
- m80 vsock dispatch is sequential per connection; kata uses ttrpc with per-connection multiplexing. m80 will keep the simpler model unless m80-3xwa.6 is filed and prioritized.

## Out of scope per CLAUDE.md
- TEE/TDX/SEV attestation (kata CoCo, libkrun TEE symbols) — m80 threat model is malicious guest, not malicious host
- SR-IOV / VFIO PCI passthrough — not on Firecracker upstream
- Device-state migration (vs memory snapshot) — m80-rrp.3 captures memory only
- GPU virtio-gpu / venus — Firecracker has no virtio-gpu in upstream
- Full image-pull-in-guest pipeline — m80-image-build owns image construction at trust boundary
- Multi-container-per-sandbox cgroup multiplexing — one VM per tenant by design
- OCI / crun integration in-guest — adapter-layer concern (kata + smolvm have it; m80 deliberately delegates)

## Deferred / future direction (not filed as epics)

### In-guest per-workload cgroups (kata K6 group from deep audit)
Items: per-process cgroup attach pre-exec, memory.max per-workload, pids.max fork-bomb cap per-workload, cpuset pinning per-workload, cgroup accounting export. Relevant only if multi-workload-per-VM is reintroduced. m80 today is one-VM-per-tenant (conveyor-belt) so per-workload cgroups inside the guest add complexity without value. Re-evaluate if/when the multi-workload model is requested.

### In-guest netlink network primitives (kata K10 group from deep audit)
Items: interface configuration, route table management, ARP/NDP, /etc/resolv.conf write, sysctl writes, iptables programming from inside guest, link state queries. m80 deliberately delegates network policy to m80-net-outbound at host level. ARP/NDP entry management is the only real gap (rare use case); the rest are D-classified architectural divergences. File a small standalone bead for ARP if a use case surfaces.

### Other small items from deep audit (not filed unless specifically requested)
- Sparse-file fallback in m80-storage when reflink/fallocate unavailable (S6.1)
- Raw-mode termios setup for PTY (S4.7 — neither smolvm nor m80 does cfmakeraw explicitly)
- IPv6 sysctl detection at boot (K10.7)

## m80 advantages worth preserving (FC jailer / others lack these)
- Plan-as-data (m80-jailer/src/plan.rs) + jailer-plan.json persistence + jailer-state.json crash recovery (FC has none)
- Drop-based MaterializedJail teardown (m80-jailer/src/materialized.rs) (FC has none)
- m80-jailer/src/recover.rs orphan inspector (live vs orphaned jail detection)
- Inverted readiness via m80-7tpy (deterministic, no polling)
- Single-VM-per-tenant model removes need for kata's multi-container cgroup multiplex (intentional simplification)
- Sequential vsock accept loop (vs kata's ttrpc multiplexing) — simpler, easier to audit; trade-off accepted unless concurrency need surfaces

## Acceptance for the umbrella
- All 12 children (or however many end up filed if 6-10 land) closed.
- Each closed child reports closure as "implemented" or "implemented + smoke verified" in its --reason note.
- After all children close, m80's host-side jailer + in-guest agent are at functional parity with FC jailer for legitimate isolation features, with documented divergences and explicit OOS list.

## Sources
- /tmp/m80-jailer-audit-brief.md (hermes brief)
- /tmp/m80-proposed-epic-beads.md (hermes 6-epic proposal — confirmed by audit)
- /tmp/m80-conveyor-belt-strategy.md (hermes strategy doc — feeds m80-iswt + Bestiary scope)
- /tmp/m80-hermes-notes.md (hermes perf state snapshot)
- 12-agent jailer audit dispatched 2026-05-07 (in this session's history)
- 20-agent guest-daemon deep audit dispatched 2026-05-07 (in this session's history)
notes: completion audit: all filed direct children are closed. Implemented host/jailer/conveyor-belt work was already closed before this tranche; this tranche closed m80-3xwa.5 by implementing workspace mount repair fallback, MSG_PEEK liveness, CPU/memory online uevents, and Ping/Pong health, plus design-narrowing deferred storage readiness, OOM async push, exec privilege fields, and DNS name allowlist where the safe transport/syscall/network boundary is not present. Proposed m80-3xwa.6-10 remain proposal text only and were never filed as child beads. Closure is therefore implemented where safe and explicitly narrowed where the audit item was not a legitimate current m80-core implementation surface.

title: Mount/FS isolation hardening: MS_SLAVE/REC, MS_NODEV/NOEXEC/NOSUID, 0o700 perms, /proc-/sys, O_NOFOLLOW
description:
Group A from the 12-agent audit (2026-05-07). Seven mount/filesystem hardening items in m80-jailer that pair with m80-jmqg (pivot_root + mount NS) for full FC-level mount isolation. Most ride on the mount-NS foundation from m80-jmqg, so file these as a follow-up sweep after m80-jmqg lands.

## Items

### A1 — MS_SLAVE | MS_REC propagation on / before any jail ops
FC: chroot.rs:27-40 sets propagation to slave-recursive on / so host mount events do not leak into the new mount namespace.
m80: never touches mount propagation; defaults inherit host mount propagation.
Why: without this, mounts in the host (USB plug, NFS remount) propagate into all live jails — visible to FC, defeats the namespace.

### A2 — MS_REC flag on bind mounts
FC: chroot.rs:54 binds with MS_BIND | MS_REC so submounts come along atomically.
m80: plan.rs binds with MS_BIND only.
Why: a source path with nested submounts (overlayfs, tmpfs) only gets the top level into the jail; submounts are absent inside, leaving the chroot inconsistent.

### A3 — MS_NODEV | MS_NOEXEC | MS_NOSUID on bind mounts
FC: env.rs general (depends on bind type).
m80: bind mounts have no security flags.
Why: a writable bind from an untrusted source path could deliver setuid binaries or device nodes to the jailed FC; defense-in-depth even when the source is m80-controlled.

### A4 — 0o700 folder permissions + chown to jail uid/gid
FC: env.rs:66 sets FOLDER_PERMISSIONS = 0o700 on /, /dev, /dev/net, /run inside jail and chowns to jail uid/gid.
m80: plan.rs creates dirs with 0o755.
Why: 0o755 lets other host users browse jail contents; 0o700 + chown gives strict per-VM-user-only access.

### A5 — /proc and /sys handling inside jail
FC: env.rs does not mount /proc or /sys inside jail; copies /sys/devices/system/cpu cache info on aarch64.
m80: leaves host /proc and /sys visible (no remount, no hide).
Why: a jailed process can read host /proc/sys for boot params, kernel version, capability bits, and /proc/cpuinfo for host topology — useful for fingerprinting and side-channel discovery.

### A6 — O_NOFOLLOW + path canonicalization (realpath) on file ops
FC: env.rs:493 opens copy destinations with O_NOFOLLOW; main.rs:159 calls canonicalize() on chroot_base and exec_file before any operation.
m80: plan.rs uses paths as supplied; no canonicalization, no O_NOFOLLOW.
Why: a symlink in the source tree (or a swap between plan-compute and materialize) could redirect mount/copy operations to host paths; canonicalization + O_NOFOLLOW closes the TOCTOU.

### A7 — Mount propagation semantics on bind sources (rprivate vs rslave)  [added 2026-05-07 from 20-agent deep audit]
20-agent deep audit Lens K9.4 found: kata sandbox.rs:73-97 has a `shared` flag controlling whether bind-mount propagation is rprivate or rslave. m80 hardcodes MS_REC|MS_PRIVATE (private propagation).
For agent sandboxing, MS_PRIVATE is correct (no leakage). But document the choice explicitly so that future contributors don't switch to rslave/rshared by accident. Also document the per-binding override path (if any binding genuinely needs rslave for a specific cooperative-mount use case, the plan-step builder should require an explicit opt-in).

## Cross-references
- **m80-jmqg** is the prerequisite — it creates the mount NS that A1-A7 harden.
- **m80-16oi** (mknod) creates device nodes inside the jail; A4 (0o700 + chown) applies to those nodes too.
- **MaterializedJail::Drop** invariant: m80's reverse plan must use umount2(MNT_DETACH) recursively on bind mounts (m80 already does this; preserve in tests).

## Acceptance
- m80-jailer materialize() applies MS_SLAVE | MS_REC propagation to new mount NS root.
- All bind mounts use MS_BIND | MS_REC + MS_NODEV/NOEXEC/NOSUID by default; plan can opt-out per binding for a specific need (executable mount of FC binary).
- Folder permissions on jail-internal dirs are 0o700, owned by jail uid/gid.
- /proc and /sys are either mounted fresh inside the jail or hidden via empty bind/MS_RDONLY (decision in IMPL).
- All file operations during materialize use O_NOFOLLOW; all paths canonicalized via std::fs::canonicalize before use.
- Bind-mount propagation defaults to private; per-binding override is explicit.
- Existing real-KVM smoke and bench pass with new flags.
- Drop-cleanup test: simulate panic during materialize, verify host mount table has no residual binds.

## Out of scope
- Mount-NS entry itself (m80-jmqg).
- mknod-replaces-bind for /dev/* (m80-16oi).
- pivot_root (m80-jmqg).

## Implementation notes
Single PR; touches plan.rs::materialize() and the bind-step builder. Each of A1-A7 is a small change but they all flow through the same plan-execution pipeline so it is easier to land them together than as 7 separate PRs.

## Sources
- 12-agent audit Lens 1 (FC mount/FS isolation), 2026-05-07.
- 20-agent deep audit Lens K9 (kata storage/mount), 2026-05-07 — A7 propagation semantics.
- /tank/projects/firecracker/src/jailer/src/chroot.rs:20-92, env.rs:289+
notes: implemented/evidence: m80-owned bind plan uses 0700/chown dirs, canonicalized sources, O_NOFOLLOW writes/placeholders, MS_BIND|MS_REC, secure remount flags MS_NODEV|MS_NOEXEC|MS_NOSUID (+MS_RDONLY for RO), and rejects dev/proc/sys/.. destinations. Runtime proof: end_to_end_real_kvm_jailer_security_parity asserts live /kernel, /rootfs.ext4, /rootfs.overlay.ext4 mount options include nosuid,nodev,noexec and rootfs is ro; integration_root materialize smoke passes as root. Unit proof: plan_compute private dirs/rejections, materialized launch tests. Gates: cargo test/clippy -p m80-jailer -p m80-cgroup -p m80-firecracker; git diff --check.

title: Process/credentials hardening: setgroups, capset, PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS, PR_CAP_AMBIENT_CLEAR_ALL, env sanitize, FD close, signal mask, orphan reap
description:
Group B from the 12-agent audit (2026-05-07), enriched with implementation specs from the 20-agent deep audit (2026-05-07). Ten process- and credential-side hardening items applied at the same exec-time call site. Best landed as a single sweep — the syscalls layer in a fixed order and partially-applied state is worse than nothing.

## Items

### B1 — Session leadership check + setsid() in new PID NS
FC: env.rs:346-359 (pre-clone check), 369 (post-clone setsid).
m80: never calls setsid; never checks session leadership.
Why: avoid spurious SIGHUP when m80 process exits; needed for daemonization.
Cross-ref: pairs with m80-isxo (CLONE_NEWPID) — shared call site.

### B2 — /dev/null open before chroot, dup2 after fork
FC: env.rs:662-669 opens /dev/null pre-chroot, dups to stdio post-fork at lines 760-762.
m80: stdio is Stdio::inherit() (m80-jailer/src/materialized.rs:82-98).
Why: opening /dev/null after chroot may fail (no /dev/null in jail); doing it before guarantees stdio close on bad orchestrator state.

### B3 — prctl(PR_SET_PDEATHSIG)
FC: not present (FC relies on PID NS + session structure).
m80: not present.
Why (still worth adding): if m80 SIGKILLs uncleanly, the FC child should auto-die instead of becoming orphaned. PID-NS isolation alone does not signal on parent death. Adopt for robustness even though FC does not.

### B4 — prctl(PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS) before exec
FC: applied inside FC's vmm code, not in jailer (env.rs).
m80: not present at jailer layer.
Why: prevents jailed FC from gaining privileges via setuid binaries even if it managed to exec one. Matches FC's vmm behavior at the jailer layer.

### B5 — setgroups([]) drop supplementary groups
FC: not explicitly called (FC uses Command::uid/gid which does setresuid/setresgid but not setgroups).
m80: not present.
Why (gap in both): inherited group memberships persist; cap-style group access controls (e.g., disk, video) leak into jail. Dropping supplementary groups is one syscall.

### B6 — capset() capability drop + PR_CAP_AMBIENT_CLEAR_ALL
FC: not explicitly called in jailer.
m80: not present.
Why (gap in both): without explicit capability set, the jailed FC inherits whatever ambient/effective caps the orchestrator had. Drop to a minimal target set (CAP_NET_ADMIN if networking, otherwise empty); clear ambient.

### B7 — Environment variable sanitization (clean_env_vars)
FC: main.rs:305-315 clears all inherited env vars before jail.
m80: inherits caller env (m80-jailer is library, runs in caller's process).
Why: secrets in env (API keys, credentials, AWS_* vars) leak into jailed FC. Adopt: m80 should clear env before exec'ing FC.

### B8 — close_range(3, INF) FD closure before exec
FC: main.rs:273-286 closes FDs >= 3 with CLOSE_RANGE_UNSHARE.
m80: not present.
Why: open host FDs (logs, config, sockets, stdin from caller) leak into jailed FC. close_range is one syscall; mandatory before exec.

### B9 — umask(0077) + signal mask + orphan reaping
FC: env.rs general; orphan reaping not present (FC parent exits at line 380).
m80: m80-jailer/src/materialized.rs:138-142 calls forget(child) so no waitpid happens.
Why (3 sub-items together): umask(0077) ensures any in-jail mkdir/mknod creates 0o600/0o700; signal mask ensures FC does not receive jailer signals; m80 currently leaks zombies on unclean shutdown. Wire into the same call path as the rest of B.

### B10 — SELinux exec label timing (added 2026-05-07 from 20-agent deep audit)
kata: selinux.rs:29-45, called at container.rs:705 — writes to /proc/thread-self/attr/exec BEFORE seccomp/caps drop, AFTER no_new_privs.
m80: not present.
Why: when SELinux is enforcing, the exec syscall must already have the target label assigned. Writing /proc/thread-self/attr/exec from the jailer is one fwrite; downstream FC inherits the label. If we ever ship m80 to RHEL/Fedora hosts, SELinux denials silently break VMs without this.

## Implementation spec — exact syscall ordering

The 20-agent deep audit captured kata's exact ordering from container.rs:685-829. Use this verbatim:

\`\`\`
fork
  → unshare(CLONE_NEW*)
    → setns(target_ns_fds)
      → setgroups([])                          # B5: drop supplementary groups
        → setresgid(jail_gid)
          → setresuid(jail_uid)
            → PR_SET_KEEPCAPS handling         # if cap drop is selective
              → SELinux exec label             # B10: write /proc/thread-self/attr/exec
                → PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS          # B4: must be after SELinux label
                  → seccomp filter load        # via prctl(PR_SET_SECCOMP) or seccomp(2)
                    → exec(...)
\`\`\`

Critical ordering notes:
- Bounding capset BEFORE effective/permitted/inheritable/ambient (kata capabilities.rs:54-82).
- When no_new_privs=true, defer seccomp until just before exec (kata container.rs:825-828).
- When no_new_privs=false, seccomp must load BEFORE cap drop (requires CAP_SYS_ADMIN).
- libseccomp internally unsets nnp bit (seccomp.rs:77 set_ctl_nnp(false)) — do NOT set nnp=true after init_seccomp.
- TSYNC flag (seccomp.rs:15 SECCOMP_FILTER_FLAG_TSYNC) only matters if process is multi-threaded; m80's Command::new is single-threaded, TSYNC optional.
- Validation post-exec: read /proc/self/status Cap*, NoNewPrivs, Seccomp lines to confirm drops took effect (recommended in tests).

Wrong order silently corrupts state (e.g., setting nnp before SELinux label = SELinux write fails; loading seccomp before cap drop without nnp = filter loading fails).

## Acceptance
- All 10 items applied in the documented fixed order at the m80-jailer exec site, just before exec'ing FC.
- A jailed FC process has no supplementary groups, drops to a documented capability set, has no ambient caps, has cleared env, has only stdin/stdout/stderr open as fds, has umask 0077, and has the configured SELinux label (if enforcing).
- m80-jailer reaps the FC child process on m80 process exit (no zombies; configurable).
- Existing real-KVM smoke and bench pass.
- Per-VM /proc/self/{status,limits,seccomp,attr/current} reflects the applied state in tests.

## Implementation notes
The fixed syscall order documented above is non-negotiable; partially-applied state is worse than nothing. The 20-agent deep audit Lens 7 (kata caps/seccomp/no_new_privs deeper) confirms this is the kata-rustjail canonical sequence.

## Out of scope
- Seccomp filter installation in the jailer process itself (separate decision; today m80 lets FC's internal seccomp do the job).
- AppArmor profile transitions (could be added as B11 if a target host distro requires it; not currently in scope).

## Sources
- 12-agent audit Lens 2 (process/PID), Lens 5 (credentials), Lens 6 (cmdline/exec hygiene), 2026-05-07.
- 20-agent deep audit Lens 7 (kata caps/seccomp/ns deeper), 2026-05-07.
- /tank/projects/firecracker/src/jailer/src/env.rs:300-770, main.rs:159-315.
- /tank/projects/kata-containers/src/agent/rustjail/src/{capabilities.rs,seccomp.rs,container.rs,selinux.rs}.
notes: implemented/evidence: m80-jailer-harden is now the m80-owned process-hardening exec wrapper. It applies setgroups([]), clears inheritable+ambient capabilities, sets PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS, sets PR_SET_PDEATHSIG=SIGKILL, sets umask 0077, resets signal mask, closes inherited fds >2, clears env, then execs the official Firecracker jailer. m80-jailer launches the wrapper with env_clear, stdin=/dev/null, stdout/stderr to console log or /dev/null, and the official jailer still performs final uid/gid drop, close_range, chroot/pivot/mknod/resource-limit/new-pid setup. Live proofs: sudo cargo test -p m80-jailer-harden --test integration_root -- --ignored --nocapture; sudo env M80_JAILER_HARDEN_BIN=/tank/projects/m80/target/debug/m80-jailer-harden cargo test -p m80-jailer --test integration_root -- --ignored launch_with_new_pid_ns_records_sentinel_and_firecracker_is_pid_one --nocapture; sudo env M80_* cargo test -p m80-firecracker --test end_to_end_real_kvm -- --ignored end_to_end_real_kvm_jailer_security_parity --nocapture. The real-KVM proof inspects live Firecracker for empty groups, NoNewPrivs=1, CapPrm/CapEff/CapInh/CapAmb all zero, empty SigBlk, uid/gid 3000, hardened mount flags, mknod devices, and RLIMIT_NOFILE. Gates: cargo test -p m80-jailer-harden -p m80-jailer -p m80-preflight -p m80-firecracker --tests; cargo clippy -p m80-jailer-harden -p m80-jailer -p m80-preflight -p m80-firecracker -p m80-cli -p m80-test-helpers --all-targets -- -D warnings; git diff --check. Docs: crates/m80-jailer-harden/README.md, crates/m80-jailer/README.md, crates/m80-preflight/README.md, docs/behaviors/jailer/security-parity.md, docs/design/jailer-group-b-exec-site.md.

title: DESIGN: choose final exec-site ownership for Group B credential hardening
description: Group B requires process/credential syscalls at the final pre-Firecracker exec site: setgroups([]), capset/ambient clear, PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS, signal-mask/umask/pdeath/orphan semantics. m80 currently delegates that final exec to Firecracker's official jailer; m80's wrapper can clear env before execing jailer and pass --new-pid-ns/--resource-limit, but it cannot safely run these syscalls in Plan::materialize() because that is the orchestrator process, and running them before official jailer would strip privileges the jailer needs for chroot/mknod/pivot_root. Workspace policy also forbids raw unsafe pre_exec/FFI in m80-jailer. Decide one path and document it before implementation: (1) upstream/patch the official jailer and require that version, (2) vendor an m80-owned launcher with safe wrapper boundary, or (3) narrow Group B to FC-jailer parity and move non-FC hardening to a future owned-launcher epic. Acceptance: decision doc or README section names the chosen path, explains why the other two are rejected, and rewrites m80-3xwa.2 acceptance into implementable leaf tasks.
close_reason: documented decision in docs/design/jailer-group-b-exec-site.md: current Phase 1 claims delegated FC-jailer parity only; final-exec setgroups/capset/no_new_privs/signal-mask/pdeath require patched official jailer or future m80-owned launcher. m80-3xwa.2 remains open until that implementation path is chosen.

title: Cgroup hardening: two-pass setup, subtree-control propagation, inherit fallback, RLIMIT_*, v2 I/O, OOM, CLONE_NEWCGROUP
description:
Group C from the 12-agent audit (2026-05-07). Six cgroup-related hardening items in m80-cgroup. m80 is cgroup-v2-only today; FC handles v1 and v2 with several robustness patterns m80 lacks. Some items are about correctness on heterogeneous kernels; others extend resource control beyond what m80-8o58 (RLIMIT_NOFILE/FSIZE) covers.

## Items

### C1 — Two-pass cgroup setup (properties first, PID enrollment second)
FC: cgroup.rs:488-497 writes property values for ALL controllers, then enrolls PIDs.
m80: m80-cgroup/src/lib.rs:50-96 does properties + enrollment in the same pass.
Why: cpuset.{mems,cpus} MUST be set before PID attachment or the write fails silently on some kernels. m80 dedupes and sorts cleanly but does not separate the phases.

### C2 — Subtree-control propagation up the parent chain
FC: cgroup.rs:384-402 recursively writes cgroup.subtree_control up the parent chain.
m80: m80-cgroup/src/lib.rs:61-77 enables at the parent only (REQUIRED_SUBTREE_CONTROL).
Why: if a sibling cgroup disables a controller in the shared parent, m80's leaf may fail; FC's recursive enable ensures all ancestors are configured.

### C3 — Inherit-from-parent fallback with retry
FC: cgroup.rs:243-312 detects empty inherited files and propagates from ancestors with retry logic.
m80: assumes defaults exist or are inherited.
Why: on systems with sparse / unconfigured parent hierarchies, m80 VMs can inherit incorrect limits silently (cpuset.mems empty, memory.max unlimited).

### C4 — Extend setrlimit beyond NOFILE/FSIZE
m80-8o58 covers NOFILE and optional FSIZE only.
Add: RLIMIT_NPROC (fork bomb cap), RLIMIT_MEMLOCK (locked-memory cap), RLIMIT_AS (address-space cap), RLIMIT_CORE (core dump cap), RLIMIT_STACK (stack cap).
Why: in dense deployments a runaway fork bomb in one VM starves the host; memory-pinning workloads without MEMLOCK cap escape resource accounting.
Cross-ref: extends m80-8o58; coordinate the setrlimit call site to avoid touching the same lines twice.

### C5 — cgroup-v2 I/O controls + explicit device-controller boundary
FC: env.rs only creates device nodes; it does not configure device or I/O cgroups.
m80: now uses the cgroup-v2 `io.max` / `io.weight` surface for noisy-neighbor disk throttling. Literal `devices.allow` / `devices.deny` are cgroup-v1 files and are not available in m80's v2-only hierarchy; device exposure is enforced by jailer device-node and mount policy unless a future BPF cgroup-device controller is deliberately added.
Why: prevents disk-heavy sandboxes from starving peers while keeping the v2-only cgroup contract honest.

### C6 — OOM score adjustment + CLONE_NEWCGROUP namespace
oom_score_adj: ensure jailed FC is OOM-killed before host system processes when memory pressure hits.
CLONE_NEWCGROUP: enter a new cgroup namespace so the jailer process is not visible/managed in the host's cgroup hierarchy by name; defense-in-depth.

## Audit-confirmed code references (12-agent audit, 2026-05-07)
- cgroup.rs:35-90 — cgroup v1 vs v2 detection
- cgroup.rs:243-312 — inherit-from-parent fallback w/ retry (C3 reference)
- cgroup.rs:319-325 — file format validation (controller.property split)
- cgroup.rs:369-376, 478-485 — tasks (v1) vs cgroup.procs (v2) write site
- cgroup.rs:384-402 — subtree control propagation (C2 reference)
- cgroup.rs:488-497 — two-pass setup (C1 reference)

## Acceptance
- m80-cgroup applies properties + subtree control fully before any PID enrollment (two-phase).
- Subtree control propagates recursively to all ancestors needed by the leaf.
- Sparse parent hierarchies receive a fallback inherit-from-grandparent or fail with a typed error (no silent zero-values).
- ResourceLimits exposes all 6 RLIMIT_* fields; m80-8o58 expands to cover them.
- cgroup-v2 `io.max` and `io.weight` are configurable; sane defaults documented.
- Literal `devices.allow` / `devices.deny` is documented as a v1-only interface outside this v2-only crate; m80 relies on jailer device-node/mount policy for current device exposure.
- oom_score_adj is configurable; default high-positive (kill jailed FC before host).
- (Optional) CLONE_NEWCGROUP supported via JailerConfig flag.

## Future / deferred (not in this epic)

### In-guest per-workload cgroups (kata K6 group from 20-agent deep audit)
Items: per-process cgroup attach pre-exec, memory.max per-workload, pids.max fork-bomb cap per-workload, cpuset pinning per-workload, cgroup accounting export per-workload.
Why deferred: m80 today is one-VM-per-tenant (conveyor-belt) so per-workload cgroups inside the guest add complexity without value. Re-evaluate if/when multi-workload-per-VM is reintroduced. Tracked in m80-3xwa umbrella description under "Deferred / future direction".

## Out of scope
- Cgroup v1 support (m80 is v2-only by design; document v1 as deliberate non-goal). The gap exists for old kernels but the trade-off is documented in m80-cgroup/README.md.

## Implementation notes
m80-cgroup crate, single PR feasible. RLIMIT_* extension may share the same setrlimit call site as m80-8o58; coordinate to avoid touching the same lines twice.

## Sources

- 20-agent deep audit Lens K6 (in-guest cgroup; deferred), 2026-05-07.

title: NetworkPolicy::JoinNetns mode (third option alongside NoEgress and AllowOutbound)
description:
Group D from the 12-agent audit (2026-05-07). One item: a third NetworkPolicy mode that joins an externally-provisioned network namespace.

## Item

### D1 — NetworkPolicy::JoinNetns(path)
FC: env.rs:520-532 supports setns(CLONE_NEWNET) into a netns at a given path, with O_NOFOLLOW validation on the netns fd.
m80: NetworkPolicy enum has only NoEgress | AllowOutbound (host-side iptables/NAT model).
Add: a third mode that takes a netns path. m80 opens the netns fd with O_NOFOLLOW, validates it, and uses setns(CLONE_NEWNET) before launching FC.

## Sketch — Rust shape

\`\`\`rust
pub enum NetworkPolicy {
    NoEgress,
    AllowOutbound { /* existing config */ },
    JoinNetns {
        netns_path: PathBuf,
        validation: NetnsValidation,
    },
}

pub struct NetnsValidation {
    /// Open with O_NOFOLLOW; refuse symlinks
    pub follow_symlinks: bool, // default false
    /// Verify the path resolves to a file in /proc/<pid>/ns/net
    /// (kernel exposes netns fds as inodes in /proc/<pid>/ns/net)
    pub verify_is_netns: bool, // default true
}
\`\`\`

Implementation:
1. open(netns_path, O_RDONLY | O_CLOEXEC | O_NOFOLLOW) → fd
2. if verify_is_netns: stat the fd, confirm it's a /proc/<pid>/ns/net file (kernel marks these with a specific st_dev/st_ino pattern; FC checks via the f_op pointer)
3. setns(fd, CLONE_NEWNET) before exec'ing FC
4. close(fd) after setns

## Why
m80's existing two modes are end-to-end (m80 handles bridge/NAT/iptables for the caller). The JoinNetns mode hands off network setup entirely to the caller — useful when:
- The caller has already provisioned a netns with custom routing/iptables/sysctls.
- Multi-tenant deployments where each tenant gets a pre-provisioned netns from a network operator.
- Test scenarios that need a deterministic netns layout that m80-net-outbound does not produce.

This is purely additive — existing NoEgress and AllowOutbound paths stay unchanged. The Bestiary (docs/future-directions/bestiary-conveyor-belt.md) is a likely consumer.

## Cross-references
- **m80-net-outbound** is **bypassed** entirely when JoinNetns is selected. Document this in m80-net-outbound's README so callers don't expect bridge/NAT/iptables wiring on JoinNetns. The host-side firewall policy is the caller's responsibility in this mode.
- **m80-jmqg** (mount NS) is independent — JoinNetns is just network; mount NS and PID NS still apply per their own configs.

## Acceptance
- NetworkPolicy enum has a third variant: JoinNetns { netns_path: PathBuf, validation: NetnsValidation }.
- m80-jailer (or m80-firecracker, depending on which crate owns the call) opens the netns fd with O_NOFOLLOW, validates it is a netns (file in /proc/<pid>/ns/net), and calls setns(CLONE_NEWNET) before exec'ing FC.
- Existing NoEgress and AllowOutbound smoke tests pass unchanged.
- New smoke: pre-create a netns with `ip netns add`, launch m80 with JoinNetns, verify FC sees the netns interfaces.
- m80-net-outbound's README updated to document that JoinNetns mode bypasses it entirely.

## Out of scope
- m80-side creation of netns (FC also only joins). Caller provisions.
- Inter-mode transitions (a VM stays on one policy for its lifetime).

## Sources
- 12-agent audit Lens 4 (network isolation), 2026-05-07.
- /tank/projects/firecracker/src/jailer/src/env.rs:520-532.

title: m80-guestd hardening + verbs: OOM events, exec-time caps/seccomp, online CPU/mem, health probe, fsck fallback, MSG_PEEK liveness, OnceLock init, DNS allowlist
description:
Groups F+G from the 12-agent jailer audit (2026-05-07), enriched with implementation specs from the 20-agent guest-daemon deep audit (2026-05-07). Eight in-VM agent improvements surfaced by the kata-agent and smolvm-agent reads. Different scope from the host-side jailer work (lives in m80-guestd crate, touches the vsock protocol surface) but same audit pass; bundled because they share the crate.

Two flavors: hardening (pure robustness, no new protocol) and verbs (new RPC additions on top of hardening).

## Hardening (4 items, no new protocol)

### F5 — fsck/resize/mkfs fallback on storage mount
smolvm: main.rs:1177-1249 — three-stage fallback: resize→mount, fsck→resize→mount, mkfs→mount.
m80-guestd: pid_one.rs:46 mounts /dev/vda; no recovery on failure.
Why: pool VMs may inherit a corrupted overlay or partial template; fsck repair before failing is one syscall and saves a slot.

### G1 — MSG_PEEK | MSG_DONTWAIT vsock liveness check
smolvm: process.rs:46-72.
m80-guestd: connection.rs:335-368 uses poll(POLLIN).
Why: poll(POLLIN) misses half-closed sockets; MSG_PEEK detects peer-FIN reliably. Used to decide whether to keep streaming output for a disconnected client.

### G2 — OnceLock deferred init (signal ready before mounts complete)
smolvm: main.rs:27-46 — storage mount is OnceLock; first-use triggers it.
m80-guestd: main.rs:66-86 signals ready only after all mounts.
Why: signal ready earlier; let mounts complete during host first-request RTT. Cold-start latency win and defensive against early host requests.

### F3 — Online CPU/memory on hot-plug from guest
kata: uevent.rs:66-80 + sandbox.rs writes to /sys/devices/system/{cpu,memory}/.../online on udev events.
m80-guestd: not present.
Why: required for any future memory/vCPU hotplug; also pairs with conveyor-belt drive hot-plug if it ever needs CPU/RAM resize.

**Implementation spec (from deep audit):**
- Use the same uevent netlink listener architecture as kata: AF_NETLINK + NETLINK_KOBJECT_UEVENT socket; demux to add/remove handlers; matcher-trait registry pattern (kata uevent.rs:37-39 UeventMatcher trait, with concrete VirtioBlkPciMatcher / ScsiBlockMatcher / VfioMatcher).
- Hybrid wait-for-device pattern: check cached uevent_map first, then oneshot channel + tokio::time::timeout(hotplug_timeout, rx). Default timeout 3 s (kata config.rs:66 DEFAULT_HOTPLUG_TIMEOUT).
- Shared infrastructure with m80-iswt drive hot-plug (E4-E7 in m80-iswt cover the same patterns from the host side).

## Verbs (4 items, new RPC surface in m80-proto)

### F1 — OOM event channel
kata: sandbox.rs:438-462 wires cgroup OOM notifier as event channel; rpc.rs:1624-1645 surfaces via GetOOMEventRequest.
m80: only /proc-polling metrics today.
Add: m80-proto envelope for guestd to push OOMEvent to host async; Bestiary/orchestrator can react in <100 ms.

**Implementation spec (from deep audit):**
- Use bounded mpsc::channel(100) for backpressure (kata sandbox.rs:146).
- Per-cgroup OOM listener via inotify on memory.events / memory.oom_control (kata rustjail/cgroups/notifier.rs:25-57).
- One-shot vs continuous: kata uses continuous monitor (rpc.rs:374 spawns notify_oom() per container); m80 should match for consistency.

### F2 — Capabilities + no_new_privs + seccomp in exec path
kata: rustjail/{capabilities,seccomp}.rs apply per-process before exec.
m80: guestd execs with caller env; no per-process privilege drop.
Add: optional fields in the existing Exec request envelope: capability set, no_new_privs bool, seccomp filter blob. Lets the host force per-workload privilege drop without modifying guestd.

**Implementation spec — exact syscall ordering (from kata container.rs:685-829):**
\`\`\`
fork → unshare(CLONE_NEW*) → setns → setgroups([]) → setresgid → setresuid →
PR_SET_KEEPCAPS handling → SELinux exec label (write /proc/thread-self/attr/exec) →
PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS → seccomp filter load → exec
\`\`\`

Notes:
- Bounding capset before effective/permitted/inheritable/ambient (capabilities.rs:54-82).
- When no_new_privs=true, defer seccomp until just before exec (kata container.rs:825-828).
- When no_new_privs=false, seccomp must load BEFORE cap drop (requires CAP_SYS_ADMIN).
- libseccomp internally unsets nnp bit (seccomp.rs:77 set_ctl_nnp(false)) — do NOT set nnp=true after init_seccomp.
- TSYNC flag (seccomp.rs:15 SECCOMP_FILTER_FLAG_TSYNC) only matters if process is multi-threaded; m80's Command::new is single-threaded, TSYNC optional.
- Validation post-exec: read /proc/self/status Cap* lines + Seccomp field to confirm drops took effect (recommended in tests).

### F4 — Health/heartbeat probe verb
kata: config.rs:131 has hotplug_timeout (proxy for hang detection).
m80: implicit channel timeouts only.
Add: Ping/Pong envelope; host sends Ping at configurable interval, guestd responds with millisecond-precise timestamp; missed responses trigger host-side recovery.

### G3 — DNS-name allowlist via vsock proxy
smolvm: dns_filter.rs (~150 LOC) + agent/dns_proxy.rs (~80 LOC).
m80: m80-net-outbound has CIDR allowlist only.
Add: guest-side DNS stub forwards queries over vsock; host-side filter consults a name-based allowlist (e.g., allow api.stripe.com) and answers/rejects. Pairs with existing CIDR allowlist; closes the name-vs-subnet UX gap.

**Implementation spec (from deep audit):**
- Wire format: 2-byte big-endian length prefix + raw DNS bytes (no JSON wrapping).
- Allowlist semantics: exact-match + wildcard subdomain (e.g., stripe.com matches api.stripe.com). Case-insensitive.
- Blocked → NXDOMAIN (rcode=3) with RA bit set.
- Upstream resolver failure → SERVFAIL (rcode=2).
- Per-query isolation: each guest query opens a fresh vsock connection; no pooling on the agent side (smolvm dns_proxy.rs:64-67). Future optimization.
- IPv4-only filter: AAAA queries forward unchanged to upstream.
- Allowlist data shape: plain Vec<String> from launch config; static at boot. Live refresh deferred.
- Upstream timeout: 5 s on UDP socket (smolvm dns_filter.rs:72).

## Acceptance
- m80-guestd handles fsck/resize/mkfs fallback on /workspace mount failure; logs every fallback step; configurable to disable.
- Vsock disconnect detection uses MSG_PEEK | MSG_DONTWAIT; existing tests pass; new test for half-closed socket case.
- Storage mount uses OnceLock; ready signal precedes the mount; first request that needs storage triggers and waits for it.
- Online-on-hotplug: writing /online for a newly-hot-plugged CPU/memory device works.
- m80-proto gains OOMEvent, optional Exec fields (caps/no_new_privs/seccomp), Ping/Pong, and DnsQuery verbs.
- Existing smoke and bench pass; new tests for each verb.

## Audit-confirmed open bugs in this area (close before / alongside)
- m80-n40s (P2): exec.rs cancel forwarder thread joined on Drop with no timeout. Smolvm avoids this by single-threaded poll loop; m80's threaded model requires scoped threads with deadline. Confirmed by deep audit Group P (retry/error recovery) — no centralized retry primitive in m80.
- m80-n6dk (P1, crash-risk): pty.rs join_output_thread.expect() crashes event loop on output-thread panic. Deep audit confirmed: smolvm avoids this entirely by not threading PTY output reads (single-thread poll on master + stream).
- m80-9ixp (P1, crash-risk): connection.rs pid_slot.lock().expect() panics guestd on lock poisoning. Deep audit Group J found a related concurrent-kill race risk worth investigating alongside.
- m80-2le9 (P3): stdin_handle.write_all has no size cap. Kata also lacks (rpc.rs:2230 unbounded write_all_at); m80 should fix unilaterally.
- m80-otr1 (P2): streaming/PTY truncation flag never set. Kata is silent on truncation too — both vulnerable; m80 fixes via the truncated flag in response envelopes.
- m80-hxur (P2): exec_streaming truncated flag invisible to streaming callers. Same audit confirmation as m80-otr1.

## Implementation notes
The four hardening items can land independently per file; the four verbs touch m80-proto and require careful schema versioning (existing protobuf wire is versioned via m80-proto/src/version.rs). Coordinate the proto changes through one PR to avoid wire fragmentation.

## Out of scope
- Console forwarding pattern (kata-style debug console) — m80 already has pty/streaming; not needed.
- OPA policy engine (kata) — correctly delegated to adapter layer per CLAUDE.md scope boundary.
- Image pull / layer materialization in-guest (kata) — m80-image-build owns image construction at trust boundary.
- In-guest per-workload cgroups (kata K6 group from deep audit) — m80 is one-VM-per-tenant; deferred unless multi-workload-per-VM is reintroduced.
- In-guest netlink network primitives (kata K10 group) — m80 deliberately host-side via m80-net-outbound.

## Sources
- 12-agent audit Lens 8 (kata-agent in-VM), Lens 11 (smolvm in-guest), 2026-05-07.
- 20-agent deep audit (10 kata + 10 smolvm), 2026-05-07: K2 (vsock transport), K7 (caps/seccomp ordering), K8 (device hot-plug), kata-agent rpc/sandbox/uevent.
- /tank/projects/kata-containers/src/agent/src/{uevent.rs,sandbox.rs,rpc.rs}.
- /tank/projects/kata-containers/src/agent/rustjail/src/{capabilities.rs,seccomp.rs,container.rs}.
- /tank/projects/smolvm/crates/smolvm-agent/src/{main.rs,process.rs,dns_proxy.rs}.

title: Transport-safe large guest file reads
description:
Real-KVM E2E found that `read_file` can ask guestd to return a response whose JSON/base64 envelope exceeds the 4 MiB `MAX_FRAME_BYTES` cap. Repro: upload a 5 MiB file with `upload_file_chunked`, then call `read_file(path, Some(5 * 1024 * 1024))`; guestd logs `oversized payload: 6990642 bytes exceeds limit of 4194304` and the host sees `Vsock(Proto(Io(UnexpectedEof)))`.

Current docs say `FILE_READ_LIMIT_DEFAULT` is 16 MiB, but a single `FileReadResponse` cannot carry that much over the v0.1 NDJSON frame. Decide hard-cutover behavior: add a chunked download/read protocol, or clamp/read responses to a transport-safe byte budget with explicit truncation/error semantics. Do not add compatibility shims.

Acceptance:
- Large guest-file reads cannot close the vsock connection with an opaque EOF.
- Docs in `m80-proto`, `m80-guestd`, and `m80-firecracker` describe the real transport limit or chunked read shape.
- Regression coverage includes the 5 MiB upload/read scenario that failed in real KVM.
notes: fixed by WRA0 protobuf hard cutover; active read_file no longer returns one JSON/base64 envelope, it drains protobuf FileReadChunk frames with terminal done/truncated=false; real-kvm regression passed in crates/m80-firecracker/tests/end_to_end_real_kvm.rs::end_to_end_real_kvm_file_ops with 5MiB+123 guest read, exact hash, and no OversizedPayload/malformed/unexpected EOF logs

title: fileops: read_file consumes chunk.bytes before checking chunk.error; upload doesn't update activity per chunk
description: fileops.rs:87 — read_file appends chunk.bytes then checks done; an error chunk with partial bytes silently accumulates them before surfacing the error. Reorder. Plus upload_file_chunked never updates last_activity_ns inside the loop (only at commit, line 247) — large multi-chunk uploads can trigger spurious idle timeout. Plus no abort message is sent when a chunk fails mid-loop — guest upload_id stays open until timeout. Plus reader.read returning 0 is unconditionally treated as EOF (silent truncation on spurious 0).

title: proto wire.rs: hand-rolled 'be tolerant' field-rejection contradicts AGENTS.md doctrine
description: wire.rs:116-130 reject_unknown_envelope_fields hand-rolls a varint walker to reject field numbers outside 10..=52. AGENTS.md: 'Serde inputs fail closed' — but prost already ignores unknown fields by default. This check is the WRONG direction. Plus every frame is parsed twice (the rejection walk + prost decode). Plus the 10..=52 range is undocumented magic. Plus ProtoError::MalformedPayload(String) collapses 6 distinct failure modes (truncated varint, oversized, unknown field, missing payload, prost decode error, len overflow) into one prose string. Drop the hand-rolled walker; use prost's strictness facility; split the error.

title: lifecycle.rs last_activity_ns updated AFTER exec body — idle watcher can fire falsely
description:
site: crates/m80-firecracker/src/lifecycle.rs:200,215,370,385
finder: trim-the-fat r5

Problem: `last_activity_ns` is updated AFTER each exec call completes (post-call). The idle_timeout watcher reads it with `Ordering::Relaxed`. If an exec hangs on guest I/O for longer than the idle timeout, the watcher fires and trips IdleTimedOut even though the exec is genuinely in-flight.

Fix: update `last_activity_ns` at exec ENTRY (just after admission), not exit. Or update both at entry AND exit. Risk: timestamp-at-entry alone could lose the 'recently completed' signal — pick the cleaner semantics for the watcher.
notes: root=idle watcher observed only last_activity_ns and had no in-flight exec signal, so a long guest I/O exec could look idle. fix=ExecActivityGuard touches activity at entry/drop and maintains RunningSandbox active_execs; idle watcher skips timeout while active_execs > 0. docs=docs/behaviors/lifecycle/idle-timeout.md. test=crates/m80-firecracker/src/lifecycle.rs::tests::idle_watcher_does_not_fire_while_exec_is_in_flight. verification=cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo test --workspace; git diff --check

title: Streaming exec: real chunk-by-chunk stdout/stderr, not buffered
description:
Today m80-guestd buffers stdout and stderr into 1 MiB Vec<u8> and returns one ExecResponse envelope at exit. Smolvm advertises streaming but their wire collects events into a Vec before returning (per smolvm-exploration recon doc 07).

Real streaming is an unclaimed differentiator. For agents this matters: long-running command output should arrive as it's produced, not at exit. Multi-minute builds, ongoing test runs, tail -f workloads — all of these are unusable today.

DESIGN: opt-in via ExecRequest.streaming: bool (default false → byte-identical v0.1 wire). When true, the response is a stream of ExecStdout/ExecStderr envelopes followed by a single ExecExit terminal envelope. Frames share request_id. Existing batched exec() rebuilt as a thin wrapper that buffers internally.

Cancellation: host disconnect → child.kill() on the next chunk write (write fails with EPIPE).
Backpressure: vsock socket buffer + pipe buffer cap unbounded buffering; slow host throttles child via blocking write.
No stdin streaming, no PTY, no concurrent execs, no compression, no resume.

PLAN: docs/planning/wire-features-bead-plan.md.

NON-GOALS: No stdin streaming (multi-frame stdin upload). No PTY allocation. No concurrent multi-exec on one connection. No compression. No resume across reconnects.

title: DESIGN: multi-frame wire shape, terminal frame, cancellation, backpressure
description:
Pin the streaming contract:
1. Opt-in: ExecRequest gains streaming: bool (default false; serde skip-if-default → byte-identical v0.1 wire when unset).
2. Frame shape: when streaming=true, response is N>=0 of Envelope<ExecStdout>+Envelope<ExecStderr> (chunks in arrival order) followed by exactly one Envelope<ExecExit>. All share the request_id of the request.
3. ExecStdout/Stderr: { request_id (echo via Envelope), bytes (base64), seq: u32 } where seq is monotonic per stream within one request.
4. ExecExit: terminal payload carrying ExecStatus + Option<exit_code> + total_stdout_bytes + total_stderr_bytes + truncated. Same shape as today's ExecResponse minus the buffered bytes.
5. Cancellation: host disconnect during streaming triggers child.kill() on the guest's next write attempt (EPIPE on writer drives detection). Document this as the cancellation contract.
6. Backpressure: capture threads (existing) write into BufWriter on the connection — when the host stalls reading, the kernel socket buffer + pipe buffer fill, the capture-thread write blocks, the child process eventually blocks on its own pipe write. No unbounded in-guest buffer.
7. Batched exec() compatibility: the existing exec() API stays, but is now built on top of exec_streaming() — buffers chunks into a Vec<u8> with the same 1 MiB cap as today.

ACCEPTANCE: doc at docs/design/wire-streaming-exec.md with frame timeline diagram, cancellation FSM, backpressure narrative. m80-proto README updated. No code.

EFFORT: S (3-4 hours).

title: IMPL m80-guestd: streaming capture path
description:
In connection.rs handle_exec arm: when ExecRequest.streaming is true, replace the buffered capture_stream/Vec<u8> path with chunked emission.

Existing capture-thread shape stays: spawn one thread per pipe (stdout, stderr) reading 4 KiB at a time. Instead of pushing into a Vec, the thread writes Envelope<ExecStdout>/Envelope<ExecStderr> frames directly to the connection's BufWriter, taking a Mutex<&mut BufWriter> lock for serialization. seq increments per stream.

When child exits: drain capture threads, then write Envelope<ExecExit>.

CRITICAL: a write-failure (EPIPE on host disconnect) on any chunk frame must immediately call child.kill() and return; capture threads exit; no ExecExit frame. The connection arm returns Continue; the main accept loop continues. Document this as the cancellation behavior.

ACCEPTANCE:
- crates/m80-guestd/src/connection.rs handle_exec arm gains streaming branch.
- crates/m80-guestd/tests/streaming_*.rs unit-tests the lock-and-write pattern with mocked IO.
- Integration test (root, KVM, #[ignore]): exec a 'for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do echo $i; sleep 0.5; done' streaming; assert host receives 5 distinct ExecStdout frames separated by ~500 ms each.

DEPS: m80-strm.2.

EFFORT: M-L (2 days).

title: IMPL m80-firecracker: exec_streaming + buffered exec rebuild
description:
Add to RunningSandbox:
- exec_streaming(req: ExecRequest, on_chunk: impl FnMut(ExecChunk)) -> Result<ExecExit, FcError> where ExecChunk is enum { Stdout(seq, bytes) | Stderr(seq, bytes) }. Sends the request with streaming=true; reads frames from Channel until ExecExit; calls on_chunk for each Stdout/Stderr in order.
- exec(req: ExecRequest) -> Result<ExecResponse, FcError>: rebuild on top of exec_streaming. Buffer Vec<u8> for stdout and stderr, capped at 1 MiB each (same as today). On overflow set truncated=true. Construct an ExecResponse from buffered chunks + the ExecExit's fields.

Both methods on RunningSandbox. Existing callers of exec() see no behavior change. New callers can opt into exec_streaming.

ACCEPTANCE:
- crates/m80-firecracker/src/lifecycle.rs gains both methods (or split into lifecycle/exec.rs if file approaches 500 LOC).
- Integration test compares exec() and exec_streaming() against the same command (echo 'a'; >&2 echo 'b'; exit 7); buffered API produces same bytes the streaming API produces concatenated; both report exit_code=7.
- A streaming-cancellation test: spawn a long-running command, drop the iterator mid-stream, assert child is killed within 1 s (host-side observable via VM cgroup pid count drop).
- README m80-firecracker public-surface table updated.

description:
Three test surfaces:
1. m80-proto: round-trip + golden-file (m80-strm.2 already covers).
2. m80-guestd unit: streaming branch with mocked pipes; assert (a) chunks emerge in seq order; (b) write-failure kills child; (c) ExecExit is the FINAL frame even when capture threads have unread data — drain before sending ExecExit.
3. Integration (root + KVM, #[ignore]):

   - Cancellation: exec long-running; host drops connection mid-stream; verify guest cgroup shows the child PID is reaped within 1 s.
   - Terminal-frame invariant: 100 streamed execs in sequence; assert every one ends with exactly one ExecExit before the next request starts on the same connection.
   - Mixed-mode: same RunningSandbox handle exec() then exec_streaming() — both succeed, no protocol confusion.

ACCEPTANCE: cargo test (unit) clean; sudo -E cargo test -- --ignored (integration) clean. The backpressure test should run reliably on a 4-core dev box; tune the throttle rate if flaky.

title: E2E thin behavioral coverage cleanup (closed epics with structural-only tests)
description:
A grab-bag of test-coverage gaps surfaced by the 2026-05-08 e2e gap survey. Each is a closed-epic feature whose e2e exists but pins structure (a ref was set, a file was written) rather than the user-visible behavior the feature promises (the limit actually OOM-killed, the identity mismatch actually killed the VM, the error variant actually surfaced).

Lower urgency than Tier-1 (the writeback / EgressMode / file-op-errors / PTY epics) — these are individual cells of behavior that haven't bitten anyone yet. But each is a regression risk because the unit-tested logic could be silently inverted.

## Children
~7 child tasks, one per identified gap:

- Drive hot-plug identity-mismatch triggers immediate VM kill (m80-iswt security guarantee).
- Snapshot/restore edge cases (corrupted snapshot file, post-capture memory mutation, restore-after-crash).
- Cgroup limits actually enforced (memory.max actually OOM-kills the workload, not just file-was-written).
- Cancellation mid-upload (only mid-sleep is tested today; mid-large-stream is the harder case).
- FcError::PoolEmpty surfaces correctly when pool is drained (not panic, not silent fallback).
- Idle timeout fires-on-launch (launch with 1s timeout, never exec, verify VM is killed).
- Diagnostic phase markers appear in run-dir/diagnostics.jsonl after a real-KVM exec.

## Acceptance for the umbrella
- Each child: small focused real-KVM e2e (or unit-with-real-FS for storage-side) that pins the user-visible behavior, not the plumbing.
- All tests use the same #[ignore = "requires real KVM"] gating as existing e2e where applicable.

## Out of scope
- Full coverage matrices of any single feature (see sibling Tier-1 epics for those).
- Adding new behavior; this is verifying behavior we already think we have.

## Sources
- 2026-05-08 conversation; e2e gap survey.
- Sibling epics for Tier 1 cover the writeback-shape gaps; this is the cleanup tier.
