title: m80-side primitives for conveyor-belt pool (drive hot-plug + tenant-identity vsock + one-shot lifecycle)
description:
The conveyor-belt strategy (one-shot VMs from a generic pool with on-demand tenant drive attach) is detailed in docs/future-directions/bestiary-conveyor-belt.md. Pool management, profile catalog, elastic buffer, scale-to-zero, and tenant routing live in the Bestiary, an external orchestration daemon **outside m80 core scope per CLAUDE.md**. This epic captures only the m80-side primitives the Bestiary will call.

## In scope (m80-owned)

### 1. Drive hot-plug
- m80-firecracker-client: add PATCH /drive REST method to attach a virtio-blk device to a running VM after boot. Verify the FC version we ship supports drive hot-plug (older versions only allowed pre-boot drive PUT).
- m80-guestd: udev/uevent watcher that detects newly-attached block devices, mounts them at a configured path (/workspace by default), with idempotent retry, ~100 ms timeout, and post-mount verification (filesystem readable, expected fixture present).
- m80-proto: extend the request/response set so the host can drive the attach + signal the guest where to mount.

### 2. Tenant-identity vsock contract
- m80-proto: new envelope payload for the guest to read /workspace/.tenant-identity (UUID or signed token) after mount and report it to the host.
- m80-firecracker host-side: compare the reported identity against the expected tenant supplied at allocation; mismatch = immediate VM kill (no leak window).
- The signature scheme + token format is Bestiary-defined; m80 only carries opaque bytes.

### 3. One-shot lifecycle flag
- m80-firecracker: SandboxConfig (or equivalent) gains a one_shot mode that says "destroy this VM after the next exec/stop, do not return to caller for reuse". The Bestiary uses this so it never has to manage cleanup state.
- Lifecycle state machine refuses subsequent execs once one-shot has been triggered.

## Refinements added by 12-agent audit (2026-05-07)

### E1 — Pre-allocated drive slots pattern
kata reserves N (typically 6) placeholder drives at boot, all PATCH-updateable. Pre-allocation enables PATCH (which only updates existing drives) without an insertion step. Reference: /tank/projects/kata-containers/src/runtime-rs/crates/hypervisor/src/firecracker/fc_api.rs:147-169.

For m80: at warm-pool VM boot, reserve N placeholder drives (e.g., 4: workspace + 3 spare). The Bestiary picks one and PATCHes the path on allocation. Avoids a "create drive then attach" two-step on the request path.

### E2 — Two-phase device removal
kata splits drive detach into PrepareRemove (guest eject signal + bounded timeout for guest to flush/unmount) → RemoveBlockDevice (host-side cleanup). Reference: /tank/projects/kata-containers/src/runtime-rs/crates/hypervisor/src/dragonball/vmm_instance.rs:263-278.

For m80: needed for safe detach when a Bestiary slot is reused (one-shot makes reuse rare, but graceful drive removal is still needed during teardown if any guest activity is mid-flight).

### E3 — Sync RPC with timeout for hot-plug verification
kata uses a sync channel + ACK + bounded wait for hot-plug operations. Reference: /tank/projects/kata-containers/src/runtime-rs/crates/hypervisor/src/dragonball/vmm_instance.rs:245-260.

For m80: the drive hot-plug should not return success until the guest acknowledges device-detection and successful mount; today we have to design this contract from scratch. kata's pattern is the template.

## Refinements added by 20-agent deep audit (2026-05-07)

### E4 — Device matcher trait registry pattern
kata defines a UeventMatcher trait (uevent.rs:37-39) plus concrete matchers (VirtioBlkPciMatcher, ScsiBlockMatcher, VfioMatcher) — each filters uevent messages by devpath regex + subsystem. Pattern lets new device types plug in without touching the dispatch loop.

For m80: as drive hot-plug grows (workspace, scratch, cache slots), matcher trait avoids ifelse soup in m80-guestd. Reference: /tank/projects/kata-containers/src/agent/src/uevent.rs:37-39 + /tank/projects/kata-containers/src/agent/src/device/.

### E5 — Multi-device atomicity / partial-failure handling
kata's add_devices() (device/mod.rs:184-251) loops per device, accumulates updates in a HashMap, returns on first handler error. No rollback today; the device is already in uevent_map. Cgroup updates per-device.

For m80: when the Bestiary attaches multiple drives at once (workspace + cache + scratch), document the partial-success contract — does m80 commit the successful subset and surface a typed error for the failed ones, or revert all? Recommend: surface partial-success in response envelope; Bestiary chooses to discard the slot or proceed.

### E6 — Idempotent pre-mounted detection
kata skips re-mount if the storage source matches a pre-mount tag and the mount already exists (storage/mod.rs:389-397). Avoids EBUSY on idempotent retries.

For m80: m80-guestd's mount handler should check if /workspace is already mounted (with the right device + matching identity) and treat re-attach as a no-op. Useful for E5's partial-success retry case.

### E7 — Hybrid wait-for-device polling
kata's wait_for_uevent (uevent.rs:115-160) checks a cached uevent_map first, then waits on a oneshot channel with tokio::time::timeout(hotplug_timeout, rx). Matcher checked at dispatch time. Default 3 s (kata config.rs:66 DEFAULT_HOTPLUG_TIMEOUT).

For m80: combine cached-map (covers cold-plug at boot before listener was ready) + uevent listener (covers hot-plug) + bounded timeout (covers slow VMs). Avoids busy-poll. Same pattern as m80-3xwa.5 F3 (online CPU/memory on hot-plug) — share the infrastructure.

## Cross-references
- m80-3xwa.5 F3 (online CPU/memory) uses the same uevent listener infrastructure — shared implementation.
- m80-3xwa (umbrella) tracks this epic as a parent-child child.

## Acceptance
- The Bestiary (or an integration test standing in for it) can: allocate a generic pool VM, hot-plug a per-tenant drive, see guest mount + identity-verify within ~45 ms P50, run a workload, destroy the VM, and never see leftover state in the next slot.
- Drive hot-plug works at FC's documented version requirement; below that, m80 returns a typed error so the Bestiary can fall back.
- Pre-allocated drive slots pattern (E1) means the request-path drive attach is a PATCH, not a CREATE+PATCH.
- Detach uses two-phase removal (E2); guest gets a bounded eject window before host-side cleanup.
- Hot-plug RPC uses sync ACK with timeout (E3); failure returns a typed error so the Bestiary can discard the slot.
- Device handler dispatch is matcher-trait-based (E4) — adding a new device type does not touch the listener loop.
- Partial-success in multi-device attach (E5) returns a typed response with per-device status.
- Re-attach of an already-mounted drive (E6) is idempotent.
- Wait-for-device (E7) uses the cached-map + uevent + bounded-timeout pattern; no busy-polling.

## Out of scope
- Pool itself (Bestiary).
- Profile snapshots (Bestiary).
- Scale-to-zero / elastic buffer (Bestiary).
- Tenant authentication or token signing (Bestiary).
- Cross-host pool federation.

## References
- /tmp/m80-conveyor-belt-strategy.md (hermes, 2026-05-07) — full product strategy.
- docs/future-directions/bestiary-conveyor-belt.md — captured strategy in repo.
- m80-rrp.3 (closed) — snapshot/restore substrate the Bestiary uses for refill.
- m80-c78m — stress-ng saturation reliability bug; gates under-load reliability claim.
- m80-3xwa — parent umbrella for jailer/sandbox parity work.
- m80-3xwa.5 — m80-guestd hardening; F3 shares infrastructure with E7.
- 12-agent audit (2026-05-07) — kata storage/network/device hot-plug lens (E1/E2/E3).
- 20-agent deep audit (2026-05-07) — kata device hot-plug deep-dive (E4/E5/E6/E7).

title: Optional PID namespace isolation per VM (CLONE_NEWPID)
description:
FC's stock jailer can fork Firecracker into a new PID namespace via --new-pid-ns. In that namespace FC becomes PID 1 and cannot see or signal processes outside it — limiting blast radius of a compromised FC process. m80 launches FC directly in the caller's PID namespace; a compromised process could enumerate and potentially interact with other host processes.

## Scope
- Add optional new_pid_ns: bool to JailerConfig.
- When enabled, clone(CLONE_NEWPID) to fork into a new PID namespace before exec; child becomes PID 1.
- Handle session leadership correctly (avoid spurious SIGHUP, as FC jailer does).
- Persist inner PID in a .pid file for monitoring.

## Cross-references
- **m80-3xwa.2 B1** (session leadership check + setsid) shares the same call site — they MUST land together. B1 cannot be applied cleanly without isxo because setsid in a fresh PID NS creates a new session at PID 1, which is the desired state. Sequence: clone(CLONE_NEWPID) in this epic, then 3xwa.2 B1 adds the pre-clone session-leadership check + post-clone setsid().
- **m80-3c9b** (daemonize double-fork) uses the same session leadership semantics — the daemonize epic builds on top of this and 3xwa.2 B1.
- **m80-jmqg** (mount NS) ordering: when both this and m80-jmqg are configured, mount-NS first, then PID-NS. Both are clone-time flags so they can also be combined into a single clone() call (CLONE_NEWNS | CLONE_NEWPID).

## Child tasks
1. IMPL: clone(CLONE_NEWPID) with null stack pointer (FC's approach); session leadership; PID file persistence.
2. IMPL: lifecycle management — inspect_run_dir checks the inner PID, not the outer clone parent; graceful shutdown signals namespace PID.
3. TEST/DOCS: getpid() inside the jail returns 1 when enabled; jailed process cannot see host PIDs via /proc.

## Acceptance
- When new_pid_ns is true, FC runs as PID 1 in its own namespace.
- **getpid() == 1 verification**: integration test exec's a probe inside the jail, captures `cat /proc/self/status | grep Pid:` output, asserts the value is 1.
- Process-list isolation test: jail process listing /proc/ shows only its own PID + children, not host PIDs.
- Existing smoke and bench pass with both new_pid_ns true and false.
- Lifecycle (stop, snapshot) works correctly with namespace PIDs.

## Audit-confirmed code references
- /tank/projects/firecracker/src/jailer/src/env.rs:328-383 — exec_into_new_pid_ns() (the model for m80's implementation)
- /tank/projects/firecracker/src/jailer/src/env.rs:346-359 — pre-clone session leadership check (paired with m80-3xwa.2 B1)
- /tank/projects/firecracker/src/jailer/src/env.rs:369 — post-clone setsid() (paired with m80-3xwa.2 B1)

## Sources
- /tmp/m80-proposed-epic-beads.md Epic 4.
- 12-agent audit Lens 2 (process/PID/session isolation), 2026-05-07.
notes: implemented/evidence: JailerConfig::new_pid_ns persists to plan JSON, launch passes --new-pid-ns, reaps the official jailer parent, records jailer_pid=0 sentinel, and cgroup/recover skip sentinel correctly. Runtime proof: integration_root::launch_with_new_pid_ns_records_sentinel_and_firecracker_is_pid_one launches real Firecracker through official jailer with new_pid_ns=true, asserts jailer_pid=0 state, NSpid ends in 1, and no-file limit is live. Unit proof: materialized::launch_with_new_pid_ns_reaps_jailer_parent, recover sentinel test, m80-cgroup sentinel test. Gates passed.

title: Jailer pivot_root + dedicated mount namespace per VM
description:
m80's jailer bind-mounts firecracker, rootfs images, and sockets into a directory structure but does NOT call unshare(CLONE_NEWNS), pivot_root, or unmount the host root. The Firecracker process inherits the caller's mount namespace and retains visibility of the host filesystem tree. FC's stock jailer enters a new mount namespace, bind-mounts the jail root over itself, calls pivot_root, then umount2(MNT_DETACH) on the old root — so the FC process literally cannot see anything outside the chroot.

Highest-security-value gap of the six FC-jailer hardening features m80 currently lacks (proposed-epic-beads.md ranking).

## Scope
- Add a new plan step (PlanStep::IsolateNamespace or equivalent) that calls unshare(CLONE_NEWNS) + mount(_, _, _, MS_SLAVE | MS_REC, _) to make propagation slave.
- After bind-mounts are in place, pivot_root into the jail directory.
- umount2 the old root with MNT_DETACH, then rmdir the old_root stub.
- MaterializedJail::Drop must reverse the operation or at minimum guarantee the host mount table is not polluted on teardown.

## Cross-references
- **m80-3xwa.1 (Mount/FS hardening, Group A)** is the follow-up sweep that hardens flags WITHIN the new mount NS this epic creates. Land m80-jmqg first; then 3xwa.1's six items (MS_SLAVE/REC propagation, MS_REC bind, MS_NODEV/NOEXEC/NOSUID, 0o700 perms, /proc-/sys handling, O_NOFOLLOW + canonicalization) become straightforward sweeps inside the established namespace.
- **m80-isxo (CLONE_NEWPID)** pairs at the same call site if they ever land together; ordering is mount-NS first, then PID-NS.
- **m80-3xwa.2 B1** (session leadership + setsid) shares the same call path for daemonized launches.

## Child tasks (to file when claimed)
1. IMPL: namespace + pivot_root in m80-jailer plan step. Needs CAP_SYS_ADMIN (already required for bind mounts). Must work with existing MaterializedJail Drop guard.
2. TEST: pivot_root integration test — jailed process cannot stat paths outside jail root; Drop cleans up mount namespace.
3. DOCS: docs/behaviors and m80-jailer README updates documenting the isolation guarantee; plan-schema bump if new steps added.

## Acceptance
- Jailed Firecracker process cannot access host paths outside its chroot.
- Existing real-KVM smoke and bench pass with new isolation.

title: Decompose phase_12b: earlycon + M80_GUEST_BOOT parse + per-PUT + I/O+cgroup stats
description:
## Why

`phase_12b_ready_accept` is a single ~1017ms timer covering: Firecracker `InstanceStart` returning → kernel decompress → kernel init → devtmpfs+virtio probe → init=guestd → guestd pseudo-fs+overlay+pivot → guestd vsock connect → host accept. We cannot pick the right optimization without splitting it. Three pieces of instrumentation, all cheap, would carve this into ~8 named sub-intervals.

## Files

- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/preboot.rs:33-34` — add `earlycon=uart8250,io,0x3f8,115200n8` (or `earlyprintk=ttyS0,115200`) to `STRIPPED_BOOT_ARGS` so kernel prints timestamps before `start_kernel` completes.
- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch/ready.rs:82-121` — wrap the `accept_ready_signal` call in a `phase_event` named `phase_12b_host_waiting_accept` so the bare wait is separable from FC-startup.
- `crates/m80-guestd/src/guest_log.rs:208-210` — already emits `M80_GUEST_BOOT name=X elapsed_us=Y` lines to console.log. NEW: post-accept parser in `crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch/ready.rs` that scans `<run_dir>/console.log` for these markers and re-emits each as a host `phase_event` (`phase_12b_guest_<name>`). The format is already stable.
- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/preboot.rs:133-145` (`apply_preboot_puts`) — wrap each PUT arm with its own `phase_event` (`phase_11_put_machine_config`, `phase_11_put_drive_rootfs`, ...). Lets us see which PUT is slow.
- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch.rs` (post-phase_12b) — read `/proc/<firecracker_pid>/io` (rchar, read_bytes, major faults from `/proc/<pid>/stat` field 12) and `<cgroup_path>/cpu.stat` (usage_usec); emit as diagnostic events.

## Acceptance

- Real-KVM run produces phase events for: earlycon kernel timestamp range, FC InstanceStart wait, each guestd milestone (process_start, stdio_redirected, pseudo_fs_mounted, base_mounted, overlay_disk_mounted, overlayfs_mounted, pivot_rootfs_done, network_configured, workspace_mounted, exec_listener_bound, ready_signal_sent), each individual phase_11 PUT, and post-launch I/O + CPU-stat snapshot.
- `bench-summary.py` snapshot includes the new phase events with histograms.
- `docs/perf/phase-12b-decomposition.md` written naming what dominates the 900ms (the data drives the next bead's priority).

## Out of scope

- Don't yet act on what the decomp reveals. This bead produces the data; the next-tier beads (B5 kernel cmdline, B6 erofs, B11 guestd defer) consume it.
- Don't add Firecracker `/logger` UDS yet (separate bead — needs `LoggerConfig` client surface).

## Effort

~6h. Mostly mechanical instrumentation; the console.log parser is the only real code.

## Done

After landing this and running N=50 minimal/idle, we know which of these dominates: kernel decompress, kernel init code path, devtmpfs/virtio probe, init=exec, guestd overlay/pivot, guestd vsock handshake, or host accept latency.

title: Hugepages backing for guest RAM (machine-config huge_pages)
description:
## Why

Firecracker's `machine-config` API has supported a `huge_pages` field since v1.5 / stable v1.7+. m80's `MachineConfig` struct (`crates/m80-firecracker-client/src/lib.rs:313-326`) has only vcpu_count/mem_size_mib/smt/cpu_template; the huge_pages field doesn't exist and is never sent. Guest memory uses default `mmap(MAP_ANONYMOUS | MAP_PRIVATE)` with 4KiB pages, faulted lazily as guest touches each page.

Savings: 50-80ms P50 on hosts with hugepages pre-reserved (fewer TLB misses + no per-4K-page-fault during guest RAM init).

## Files

- `crates/m80-firecracker-client/src/lib.rs:313-326` — add `huge_pages: Option<HugePageSize>` to `MachineConfig`; new enum with `None`, `Mb2`, `Gb1` (serde to "None"/"2M"/"1G").
- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/config.rs` — add `huge_pages: Option<HugePageSize>` to `SandboxConfig`.
- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/preboot.rs:151-157` — pass through.
- `crates/m80-preflight/src/checks.rs` — NEW check: if huge_pages configured but `/sys/kernel/mm/hugepages/hugepages-2048kB/free_hugepages` < required, fail preflight with `huge_pages_unavailable` and hint at `sysctl vm.nr_hugepages=N`.

## Acceptance

- Config + client + preflight wired.
- Bench with huge_pages=Mb2 (after `sysctl vm.nr_hugepages=512` ≈ 1GiB for one VM): phase_12b_ready_accept P50 drops 50-80ms vs default; cold-cold penalty smaller too.
- Without preflight reservation, helpful error rather than FC opaque failure.
- Document in `docs/perf/hugepages.md` including the host setup procedure.

## Effort

~1d.
acceptance_criteria: Measurement cross-link: docs/perf/measurement-playbook.md#e5-tlb-and-cache-miss-counters.
close_reason: not-justified: m80-jp6ik.46 measured dTLB-load-misses P50 40.5K/P95 44.5K, below the 100K cutoff in docs/perf/measurement-playbook.md; hugepages payoff is bounded on this host

title: Defer guestd network + workspace mount to post-ready
description:
## Why

Two guestd PID-1 steps run BEFORE signaling ready, but neither is required for host-side accept:

1. **Network config** (`crates/m80-guestd/src/pid_one.rs:48` → `pid_one_network.rs:105-118`) — builds a Tokio current-thread runtime, opens rtnetlink, makes 3 sequential `block_on` netlink calls (get link, add IPv4, set link up, add route), writes `/etc/resolv.conf`. **10-50ms** on the critical path.
2. **Workspace mount** (`crates/m80-guestd/src/pid_one.rs:50` → `pid_one.rs:442-458`) — mounts /dev/vdc if present; on dirty fs, spawns blocking `e2fsck -y -f` + `resize2fs`. **2-20ms clean, 200-500ms on repair.**

The host's first exec lands AFTER its own request/parse window; both can complete in the background before that exec needs them. Moving them off the critical path also protects P99 from e2fsck blowups.

## Files

- `crates/m80-guestd/src/pid_one.rs:39-53` — restructure: required-pre-ready steps only (stdio, panic hook, pseudo-fs, overlay+pivot, vsock bind, ready signal). After signal: spawn deferred network + workspace work on a background thread.
- `crates/m80-guestd/src/main.rs:163-166` — accept loop must check workspace-mount-complete before serving the first exec that touches it; cheap wait (one OnceLock or AtomicBool).
- `docs/behaviors/guestd/ready-signal-deferred-init.md` — NEW. Documents what guestd promises is true at "ready" vs what's still in flight.

## Acceptance

- Network + workspace mount move off the pre-ready path.
- A request that lands before workspace is mounted blocks at most until workspace-ready (with a timeout returning typed error).
- Bench phase_12b_ready_accept P50 drops by ≥10ms (network deferred).
- Worst-case P99 drops dramatically when workspace fs is dirty (no e2fsck on critical path).
- Test: artificially-dirty workspace image; verify ready signals at clean-path latency, first workspace-exec waits for repair.

## Effort

~1-2d.
close_reason: Rejected: conflicts with current readiness invariant; docs/behaviors/guest-exec/deferred-storage-readiness.md already rejects deferred storage/workspace readiness because ready means final rootfs and configured workspace view are usable.

title: iptables-restore batching (replace per-rule subprocess loop)
description:
## Why

`crates/m80-net-outbound/src/iptables.rs:91-103` (`apply_outbound_nat_policy_with_ops`) calls `ensure_iptables_rule` ~25 times per launch (DNS accepts, denies, FORWARD inserts, MASQUERADE). Each `iptables` invocation is a subprocess fork + acquires `/run/xtables.lock` exclusively. At C=4 concurrent launches the lock queue is ~100 sequential lock-acquire ops; at C=16, far worse.

`iptables-restore` accepts a batched ruleset over stdin and acquires the xtables lock once for the entire batch. Net wallclock saving: 20-40ms per launch in NoEgress→outbound conversion; under concurrency, the contention reduction is the bigger win.

## Files

- `crates/m80-net-outbound/src/iptables.rs:91-103` — replace the loop over `ensure_iptables_rule` with one `Command::new("iptables-restore").arg("--noflush").stdin(...)` invocation. Build the full ruleset text in memory; pipe via stdin.
- Same pattern for `ip6tables-restore` if v6 rules exist.
- Idempotency: today's per-rule `-C` (check) before `-A` is replaced by using a fresh per-VM chain that's created+populated atomically inside the restore batch.
- Teardown path: same trick on `iptables -X` chain cleanup; or just delete the per-VM chain.
- `crates/m80-net-outbound/README.md` — update to mention iptables-restore.

## Acceptance

- All NoEgress + Outbound modes still produce equivalent rules (golden file test in `crates/m80-net-outbound/tests/`).
- Per-launch wallclock in outbound mode drops by 20-40ms P50.
- Density (C=16+) bench in outbound mode no longer regresses linearly with C.
- Smoke evidence per AGENTS.md rule (this touches iptables — kernel-adjacent).

## Effort

~2-3d.

## Note

This is a stepping stone toward nftables (bead .15). iptables-restore captures most of the win without the full migration cost.

title: Density chokepoints: network mutex critical section + cgroup subtree_control OnceLock
description:
## Why

Two host-side density chokepoints surface at moderate C:

1. **NETWORK_ALLOCATION_MUTEX `read_dir` inside critical section** (`crates/m80-net-outbound/src/lib.rs:29,177-201`). The static Mutex + flock holds `reject_guest_ipv4_collision` which does a `read_dir(run_root)` scan of all sibling VM state files — O(C) I/O while holding a global lock. At C=16 the queue is 15-deep.
2. **cgroup `subtree_control` ancestor writes** (`crates/m80-cgroup/src/lib.rs:378-410`). Every `Subtree::create` walks `/sys/fs/cgroup` and `/sys/fs/cgroup/m80-firecracker` writing `+cpu +memory +pids`. The value is process-static; idempotent at the value level but kernel rwsem serializes the writes.

Both are fixable with the same shape: do the work once, gate with `OnceLock<()>`.

## Files

### NETWORK_ALLOCATION_MUTEX fix
- `crates/m80-net-outbound/src/lib.rs:177-201` — move `read_dir(run_root)` scan OUTSIDE the flock+mutex. Take the lock only for write + re-verify (which is O(1)). The IP is deterministically derived per (run_root, vm_id), so the post-write re-check catches any concurrent race.

### Subtree control fix
- `crates/m80-cgroup/src/lib.rs:378-410` — add a process-scoped `static SUBTREE_CONTROL_PRIMED: OnceLock<()> = OnceLock::new();` Write ancestor subtree_control files once per process; per-VM cgroups still need their own writes but those are leaf cgroup paths, not ancestor contended ones.

## Acceptance

- Both fixes implemented.
- Density bench C=1,2,4,8,16,32 (extending today's flat-to-C=8 envelope): wall-time-to-all-ready stays within +30% of C=1 up to at least C=16 in NoEgress (currently uncharacterized). Outbound mode improves with iptables-restore from .12 too.
- Unit test: simulate two threads calling `Subtree::create` concurrently and verify only one ancestor write happens per ancestor.
- No correctness regression in `crates/m80-cgroup/tests/`.

## Effort

~1d.
acceptance_criteria: Measurement cross-link: docs/perf/measurement-playbook.md#e1-density-extended.
notes:
Implementation now split across commits 6c22e42 and 418fd7a.

What landed in 6c22e42:
- Live Subtree::create primes the shared /sys/fs/cgroup -> /sys/fs/cgroup/m80-firecracker subtree_control chain at most once per process.
- Synthetic create_at/test hierarchies still run the full chain every time, avoiding OnceLock test-order coupling.
- Failed priming attempts are not cached; a later create can retry.
- Updated m80-cgroup README and docs/behaviors/cgroup/subtree.md.

What landed in 418fd7a:
- Outbound network setup performs the O(C) sibling guest-IP scan before taking the allocation lock.
- The lock-protected race closure now uses a hidden per-IP claim file under <run_root>/.network-guest-ip-claims/<guest_ipv4> instead of a second sibling directory walk.
- Claim cleanup is wired into normal cleanup, missing-state cleanup, TAP rollback, and final Ready-state write failure rollback.
- Updated crates/m80-net-outbound/README.md and docs/behaviors/network-outbound-nat/setup.md.

Verification run:
- cargo test -p m80-cgroup
- cargo check -p m80-firecracker --tests
- cargo test -p m80-net-outbound (66 passed, 1 ignored)
- rustfmt --edition 2021 --check touched cgroup/net-outbound files
- git diff --check

Review notes:
- Local review focused on failure caching, synthetic hierarchy behavior, concurrent once-gate semantics, claim cleanup, and rollback windows.
- Independent review of the network-claim diff found no blocking regression; the Ready-write rollback concern was fixed before commit.

Blocked remainder:
- Acceptance still needs the density sweep evidence named in docs/perf/measurement-playbook.md#e1-density-extended.

title: Parallelize phases 3/5/6 and 5b/10 (storage|probe|network)
description:
## Why

Phases 3 (storage_prep), 5 (cgroup_probe), 6 (network_realize) have no data dependencies on each other; today they run serially in `crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch.rs`. Wins (per the dependency map an agent produced):

- phase_5_cgroup_probe (2ms, pure host syscall) can overlap with phase_3 entirely → saves ~2ms
- phase_6_network_realize (5-50ms in OutboundNat) can overlap with phase_4 (jailer_materialize) → saves 5-50ms in outbound mode
- phase_5b_cgroup_create (19ms) can overlap with phase_10_open_uds (variable, up to ~25ms in cold-cold) → saves 0-19ms

Total expected: 10-30ms P50 NoEgress, 25-70ms P50 outbound.

## Files

- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch.rs:111-251` — restructure phases using `std::thread::scope`:
  - After phase_2: spawn phase_3 + phase_5 (probe) + phase_6 in parallel; join before phase_4.
  - After phase_9: spawn phase_5b on a thread while main goes into phase_10; join phase_5b before phase_11.
- No tokio. Use plain threads — the work is wallclock-bound and the join points are clear.
- Add phase events `phase_parallel_3_5_6` and individual sub-phase timings (relies on .1 instrumentation).

## Acceptance

- All three parallelization windows wired.
- Tests: `crates/m80-firecracker/tests/launch_parallel.rs` (NEW) — verify each parallel branch's errors propagate correctly (failing storage doesn't leak running cgroup).
- Bench cold-launch P50 drops by ≥10ms NoEgress, ≥25ms outbound.
- No regression in cold-cold (parallel work was already happening sequentially in cache-cold; speedup comes from real concurrency).

## Effort

~1-2d.

## Dependency

Pairs well with .1 (instrumentation) and .13 (contention fixes). Land .13 first if doing both — parallel phases will hammer the chokepoints harder.

title: Auto-recover stale run_root at Backend::new + clean TAP/iptables in recovery
description:
## Why

On 2026-05-12 the bench harness hit EBUSY errors from stale `/var/lib/m80-run` mounts left by prior crashed runs. The `recover_stale_run_root` method (`crates/m80-firecracker/src/backend.rs:99`) exists but is only invoked when CLI explicitly requests it. It also has a gap: it unmounts + removes the run dir but never calls `m80_net_outbound::cleanup_vm`, so crashed-VM TAP devices and iptables chains accumulate.

## Files

- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/backend.rs:99` — call `self.recover_stale_run_root(false)?` (best-effort, log on warn-and-continue) at the end of `Backend::new`. One `read_dir` + one `read_to_string(/proc/self/mountinfo)` — negligible cost.
- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/backend.rs:252-271` (`remove_run_dir`) — call `m80_net_outbound::cleanup_vm(vm_id, run_root)` before `remove_dir_all`, guarded by existence of `network-state.json` in the subdir (the existing pattern).
- Tests: `crates/m80-firecracker/tests/recover.rs` — simulate a crashed run (leftover mount + leftover TAP) and confirm `Backend::new` cleans both up.

## Acceptance

- EBUSY-on-stale-mount failure mode eliminated.
- Stale TAP devices from crashed VMs cleaned up on next Backend::new.
- No regression: well-behaved exit still cleans up via the normal path.
- Smoke evidence per AGENTS.md rule.

## Effort

~3-4h.

title: Exponential backoff on kill_and_reap_pid (eliminate 20ms minimum-wait)
description:
## Why

`crates/m80-firecracker/src/lifecycle.rs:619-629` — after SIGKILL, `waitpid(WNOHANG)` polls every 20ms for up to 2s. Firecracker typically exits within 1-5ms of SIGKILL; the first poll fires 20ms later. The fixed 20ms sleep is the dominant cost on the clean-stop path.

Replace with exponential backoff starting at 1ms, capping at 20ms. First wake at 1ms catches the common case; backoff up to 20ms preserves the bounded-CPU property on pathological exits.

## Files

- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/lifecycle.rs:619-629` (`kill_and_reap_pid`) — replace `sleep(20ms)` with exp-backoff (1ms, 2ms, 4ms, 8ms, 16ms, 20ms, 20ms, ...).

## Acceptance

- Stop-path bench (cold-launch + stop, N=50): stop wallclock drops ~15ms P50.
- Worst-case bound preserved (still 2s total before returning timeout).
- Unit test: pid exits at delay D; verify reap latency ≤ D + first-backoff-greater-than-D.

## Effort

~1h.
notes: Implementation and measurement committed in 1be4361. Reap polling now backs off 1/2/4/8/16/20ms and preserves the 2s timeout. N=50 stop_bounded P50 improved from 65,785us to 56,669us (-9.116ms, -13.86%), but the rough ~15ms acceptance estimate did not fully land; do not close until acceptance is revised from evidence or stronger measurement lands.
close_reason: Implemented with measured partial stop-path win: reap polling now uses bounded 1/2/4/8/16/20 ms backoff and preserves the 2s timeout. stop_bounded P50 improved 65.785 ms -> 56.669 ms (-9.116 ms), below the rough 15 ms estimate, so this is not a launch-path win. Evidence: docs/perf/reap-backoff.md and reap-backoff-delta.json.

title: Preflight sentinel cache (skip firecracker --version + manifest verify on repeat)
description:
## Why

Preflight (`m80_preflight::run_with_configs` called in `crates/m80-cli/src/cmds.rs:54` via `backend_from_effective`) runs on every CLI invocation. Two costs in particular:

1. `crates/m80-preflight/src/binary.rs:111` — `firecracker --version` subprocess fork+exec (~10-50ms with retry).
2. `crates/m80-preflight/src/artifacts.rs:163` — `manifest.verify(parent)` sha256 over the rootfs (~180ms for 256MiB image).

For a long-running daemon / pool process these run once. For the CLI fork-per-run model (and the test harness) they're per-launch.

A `/run/m80-preflight-ok-<boot_id>` sentinel keyed by `(boot_id, fc_path, fc_mtime, fc_version, rootfs_path, rootfs_inode, rootfs_mtime, rootfs_size)` lets repeat invocations skip both costs.

## Files

- `crates/m80-preflight/src/lib.rs` — add sentinel-cache layer:

title: Cargo release profile: strip + lto=thin + codegen-units=1 + panic=abort
description:
## Why

Two agents independently proposed identical Cargo profile tuning. The workspace `Cargo.toml` has no `[profile.release]` section, so cargo defaults apply: `lto = false`, `codegen-units = 16`, `strip = false`, `panic = "unwind"`. Binary is 6.4 MiB unstripped. Combined savings ~2-5ms cold load + 30-40% smaller binary.

This only matters if m80 binary is fork+exec'd per launch (CLI mode). If used as a long-running daemon/library, the savings are cosmetic.

## Files

- `Cargo.toml` (workspace root) — add:
  ```toml
  [profile.release]
  lto           = "thin"
  codegen-units = 1
  strip         = "symbols"
  panic         = "abort"

  [profile.test]
  panic = "unwind"   # keep backtraces in test runs
  ```
- Verify `[profile.release.package."*"]` overrides aren't unexpectedly overridden.

## Acceptance

- Cargo build succeeds; CI green.
- `ls -la target/release/m80` shows ≤4 MB (vs 6.4 MB today).
- `cargo test` still produces useful backtraces (verify panic=unwind in test profile).
- No measurable runtime regression in launch-path hot code (LTO+codegen-units=1 trade build time for runtime).
- Bench cold-launch: if there's a measurable improvement in `phase_1_run_root_prep` (the proxy for binary cold load) it's bonus.

## Out of scope

- No PGO. Roadmap-stage call graph is too volatile for stable profiles.
- No BOLT. Requires layout stability we don't have.
- No `opt-level = "s"` — would degrade hot-path runtime.

## Effort

~30 min change + CI cycle.
acceptance_criteria: Measurement cross-link: docs/perf/measurement-playbook.md#e10-cargo-release-profile-delta.
notes: Implementation and measurement committed in c1c6e48. The scoped release profile reduced target/release/m80 from 6,780,216 bytes to 4,415,472 bytes (-34.88%) and showed no measured launch-path regression, but it did not satisfy the literal <=4 MB acceptance target. Do not close until the target is revised from evidence or further size work lands.
close_reason: Implemented with measured size win but literal <=4 MB target missed: release profile tuning reduced target/release/m80 from 6,780,216 to 4,415,472 bytes (-34.88%) with no measured launch-path regression; do not claim runtime optimization or <=4 MB success. Evidence: docs/perf/release-profile.md and release-profile-delta.json.

title: track_dirty_pages + Diff snapshots (warm-pool refill speedup)
description:
## Why

Two related Firecracker features m80 doesn't yet drive:

1. **`track_dirty_pages: bool`** (machine-config field) — when true, FC tracks page modifications for diff snapshots. m80's `MachineConfig` struct doesn't expose it and never sends it. Every snapshot must be `Full`.
2. **`SnapshotKind::Diff`** (already wired in `crates/m80-snapshot/src/lib.rs:166`) — but `capture()` always passes `Full` because dirty tracking was never enabled.

Together: re-snapshot cost drops from O(mem_size) to O(dirty pages). For agent workloads typically 10-50 MB vs 1 GB.

P50 launch latency unchanged; warm-pool cycle time improves substantially.

## Files

- `crates/m80-firecracker-client/src/lib.rs:313` — add `track_dirty_pages: Option<bool>` to `MachineConfig`.
- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/config.rs` — add `enable_dirty_tracking: bool` to `SandboxConfig` (default false; warm-pool sets true).
- `crates/m80-snapshot/src/lib.rs:212` — wire `SnapshotKind::Diff` capture when dirty tracking was on at boot.
- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/warm_pool.rs` — enable dirty tracking on pool slots; re-snapshot uses Diff.
- Manifest schema (`crates/m80-image-manifest`) — add parent-snapshot reference for Diff snapshots (the schema's biggest blocking gap per agent 10).
- `docs/design/diff-snapshots.md` — NEW. Document the parent-ref schema, restore order (load Full base + apply Diffs), invalidation rules.

## Acceptance

- track_dirty_pages config wired end-to-end.
- Warm-pool refill uses Diff snapshots; capture wallclock + on-disk size drops ≥60% vs Full.
- Restore validates parent-ref before applying diff.
- Test: capture Full → boot child → capture Diff; verify restore-Diff produces equivalent state.

## Effort

~1d for the wire + ~2d for manifest schema + restore semantics + tests. Total ~3d.
acceptance_criteria: Measurement cross-link: docs/perf/measurement-playbook.md#e6-dirty-page-fraction.

title: Event-drive ready-accept + phase_10 UDS polls (eliminate 10/50ms sleeps)
description:
## Why

Two host-side polls add wallclock for no good reason:

1. `crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch/ready.rs:21,87-106` — `READY_ACCEPT_POLL = 10ms`. The listener is set non-blocking and spins `thread::sleep(10ms)` in `accept_ready_signal`. The guest's vsock connect lands at a random offset within a 10ms window. Average miss: 5ms; worst: 10ms.
2. `crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch.rs:1009-1013` — phase_10 polls the API UDS path with `thread::sleep(50ms)` waiting for Firecracker to create the socket. Average miss: 25ms.

Both can be made event-driven.

## Files

- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch/ready.rs:21,87-106` — switch to blocking `accept()` with `set_read_timeout(Some(READY_TIMEOUT))`. The kernel wakes the moment FC's muxer connects; zero wait beyond actual readiness. Keep the outer timeout via `set_read_timeout`.
- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch.rs:1009-1013` — replace the 50ms sleep loop with `inotify` on the parent directory watching for IN_CREATE of the socket name; fall back to one short retry if inotify init fails.

## Acceptance

- `ready.rs` accept path uses blocking accept + timeout; no poll loop.
- phase_10 uses inotify; falls back gracefully on inotify init failure.
- Tests: `crates/m80-firecracker/tests/ready_accept.rs` (NEW) — fake listener, signal write delayed N ms, assert wakeup within ~1ms of signal. Similarly for phase_10 with a `tempdir + spawn-after-delay`.
- Bench (N=50 minimal/idle): phase_12b_host_waiting_accept drops by ~5ms P50; phase_10 drops by ~25ms P50 in cold-cold runs.

## Effort

~3h.

## Done

Both polls eliminated; combined ~30ms saved at P50 cold; both protected by regression tests.
notes: Implemented event-driven launch waits. Ready accept now uses poll(2) on the pre-bound UnixListener and nonblocking accept retry instead of the old nonblocking accept + 10 ms sleep loop. phase_10_open_uds now waits on inotify create/move/attrib events for a missing Firecracker API socket, with a capped 1/2/4/8/16/25 ms fallback only when inotify is unavailable or a created socket is not accepting yet. Regression coverage lives in launch::tests::ready_signal_wakes_without_fixed_ten_ms_poll_floor and launch::tests::phase_10_open_uds_wakes_on_socket_create_event; behavior docs updated in docs/behaviors/lifecycle/start-and-ready.md and docs/behaviors/lifecycle/preboot-wiring.md. Verification: cargo test -p m80-firecracker launch::tests --lib; cargo test -p m80-firecracker --lib; rustfmt --check touched Rust files; git diff --check; cargo build --release -p m80-cli -p m80-jailer-harden; real-KVM N=50 minimal/idle stripped at crates/m80-firecracker/benches/snapshots/2026-05-13T16:34:08+00:00.json. Measurement versus 2026-05-13T16:11:29 baseline: phase_12b_host_waiting_accept P50 1,026,665us -> 1,020,625us (-6,040us); phase_12b_ready_accept 1,028,739us -> 1,022,520us (-6,219us); phase_10_open_uds 33us -> 32us because the API socket was already present in the measured cold path.
close_reason: Event-driven ready accept and phase_10 API-socket wait implemented, documented, unit-tested, release-built, and measured on real KVM N=50.

title: nftables backend (atomic batch, no global lock)
description:
## Why (and why deferred)

`crates/m80-net-outbound/README.md:196` already deferred this. iptables backend is what bead .12 (iptables-restore batching) optimizes; nftables eliminates the underlying problem — atomic `nft -f -` commits don't take the xtables global lock at all, so concurrent VM network setup is independent rather than serialized.

Per agent 7+8: at C=4 with OutboundNat, xtables.lock queues 5-10 `iptables -A/-C` calls per VM. At C=16 this is hundreds of sequential lock-acquire ops. nftables removes that completely; .12 only reduces it.

Status: **deferred** — claim after .12 (iptables-restore) lands and density bench at C=32 shows residual xtables contention is still meaningful. If C=32 outbound benches clean after .12, this is unnecessary.

## Files (when claimed)

- `crates/m80-net-outbound/src/iptables.rs` → rename to `policy_backend.rs`; keep `PolicyOps` trait.
- NEW: `crates/m80-net-outbound/src/nftables.rs` — `NftPolicyOps` impl using `nft -f -`.
- `crates/m80-preflight/src/checks.rs` — probe for `nft` binary; fall back to iptables if missing.
- Backend selection via SandboxConfig field (default = nftables if available).
- Teardown rewriting: nftables uses per-VM tables, `nft delete table inet m80-vm-<id>` is atomic.

## Acceptance (when claimed)

- Both backends pass the existing iptables golden-file test (translated to nftables ruleset).
- Density at C=32 outbound: wall-time-to-all-ready within +30% of C=1.
- Smoke evidence per AGENTS.md rule.

## Trigger to claim

Density C=32 outbound bench after .12 lands shows xtables.lock or equivalent serialization still dominating. If not, close this bead with `not-justified` reason.

## Effort (when claimed)

~3-4d.

title: Jailer pid-file poll: exponential backoff (eliminate 25ms minimum)
description:
## Why

`crates/m80-jailer/src/materialized.rs:200` — after fork+execing jailer, m80 polls for the `firecracker.pid` file with `thread::sleep(25ms)` between attempts (up to 1s). The official jailer forks Firecracker and writes the pid-file in sub-millisecond on an idle host. The first poll fires AFTER 25ms have already elapsed — so the common path pays a full 25ms wait for a file that appeared in <1ms.

This shows up as the dominant chunk of phase_9_jailer_launch's 25ms P50.

## Fix

Replace fixed `sleep(25ms)` with exponential backoff: `1ms, 2ms, 4ms, 8ms, 16ms, 25ms, 25ms, ...`. First wake at 1ms catches the typical case; backoff preserves bounded CPU on pathological exits.

Alternative (better but more code): `inotify(IN_CREATE)` on the parent dir watching for the pid-file name. Fall back to backoff if inotify init fails.

## Files

- `crates/m80-jailer/src/materialized.rs:200` (poll loop)
- `crates/m80-jailer/tests/` — NEW test pinning latency-to-discovery under simulated sub-ms appearance

## Acceptance

- Bench: `phase_9_jailer_launch` P50 drops by 15-22ms (from ~25ms to ~3-10ms).
- Worst-case bound preserved (still 1s total).
- Test: drop a pid-file at delay D after spawn; assert observe-latency ≤ D + next-backoff-step.

## Effort

~2h.

## Done

Largest single-fix prize identified in the jailer audit; landing this likely halves phase_9.
close_reason: implemented fixed 25ms pid-file poll replacement with 1/2/4/8/16/25ms capped backoff; tests in crates/m80-jailer/src/materialized_tests.rs and crates/m80-jailer/tests/jailer/pid_file_backoff.rs; doc=docs/behaviors/jailer/pid-file-backoff.md; N=50 minimal/idle phase_9_jailer_launch P50 25,437us -> 15,588us (-9,849us)

title: Jailer micro-cuts: MS_REC + close_range + umask + to_vec
description:
## Why

Smaller jailer-overhead wins from the audit, batched because each is XS and they share the same code surface:

1. **`MS_REC` flag on file binds** (`crates/m80-jailer/src/plan.rs:161`) — recursive bind makes sense for directory binds, not flat-file binds. Drop `MS_REC` when source AND dest are files. Saves ~0.5-1ms per file bind × 3-5 binds.
2. **`close_range(3, UINT_MAX, 0)`** (`crates/m80-jailer-harden/src/lib.rs:312-335`) — replaces the `getdents64` loop over `/proc/self/fd` + N `close(2)` calls with one syscall. Linux 5.9+; our floor is well above. ~0.5-1ms.
3. **`umask(0)` + drop redundant `fchmodat`** (`plan.rs:121-131`) — `mkdir(path, 0o700)` already sets the mode if umask is 0. Drops 1 syscall per directory created. ~0.3ms aggregate.
4. **`serde_json::to_vec` instead of `to_vec_pretty`** (`plan.rs:220-237`, `materialized.rs:224`) — diagnostic files don't need pretty-printing. ~0.1-0.2ms aggregate.

## Files

- `crates/m80-jailer/src/plan.rs:161` (MS_REC fix)
- `crates/m80-jailer/src/plan.rs:121` (umask + fchmodat drop)
- `crates/m80-jailer/src/plan.rs:220`, `materialized.rs:224` (to_vec)
- `crates/m80-jailer-harden/src/lib.rs:312-335` (close_range)
- Unit tests pinning each change per AGENTS.md kernel-flag-bitset rule (especially MS_REC — needs both a bitset test AND a smoke test).

## Acceptance

- Each finding lands as its own commit for bisectability.
- MS_REC drop: dedicated test in `crates/m80-jailer/tests/kernel_flag_bitsets.rs` (the m80-lovpn.1 test file) pinning file-bind flags vs dir-bind flags.
- close_range: smoke test confirming inherited fds are closed.
- Combined phase_9 saving: ~1.5-2.5ms (additive to bead .21 which catches the big one).
- Smoke evidence required per AGENTS.md kernel-touching rule (MS_REC + close_range both qualify).

## Effort

~3h (each is small but four diffs + tests).

Local verification: rustfmt --edition 2021 --check on touched Rust files; cargo test -p m80-jailer-harden; cargo test --manifest-path support/m80-close-range/Cargo.toml; cargo test -p m80-jailer bind_mount_flags --lib; cargo test -p m80-jailer --test jailer asset_binding; cargo test -p m80-jailer; git diff --check. Also still needs combined phase_9 real-substrate measurement artifact with named numeric delta before verified close.

title: Kernel config part 2: HZ_100+NO_HZ_IDLE+PREEMPT_NONE+RD_* off+DEBUG off
description:
## Why

Kernel-config audit beyond bead .1 (CONFIG_SMP=n) surfaced six additional options worth setting explicitly:

1. **`CONFIG_HZ_100=y` + `CONFIG_NO_HZ_IDLE=y`** — default HZ_250 fires 2.5× as many timer ticks during the ~950ms kernel boot. NO_HZ_IDLE suppresses ticks during virtio-probe idle waits. Expected 10-40ms.
2. **`CONFIG_PREEMPT_NONE=y`** — removes voluntary-preemption check-points throughout kernel init code paths. Expected 5-20ms.
3. **`# CONFIG_BLK_DEV_INITRD is not set` + all `CONFIG_RD_GZIP/BZIP2/LZMA/XZ/LZO/LZ4/ZSTD is not set`** — m80 boots vmlinux directly with no initramfs; these decompressor tables are pure binary bloat. Shrinks vmlinux, slightly speeds cold-cold load. Expected 0-5ms; binary size win.
4. **`# CONFIG_SCHED_DEBUG is not set` + `# CONFIG_SCHEDSTATS is not set`** — per-context-switch stat collection. Expected 1-5ms across boot.
5. **`# CONFIG_DEBUG_INFO is not set` + `# CONFIG_DEBUG_INFO_BTF is not set`** — vmlinux size reduction (cascade from DEBUG_KERNEL=n likely turns these off via `olddefconfig`, but explicit pinning makes it deterministic).
6. **`# CONFIG_PRINTK_TIME is not set`** — eliminates timestamp formatting per printk message.

## Files

- `crates/m80-image-build/kernel-builder/m80-stripped.config` — add all six.
- After bead .1 (`CONFIG_SMP=n` + strip debug) merges; this bead builds on the same surface.

## Acceptance

- Rebuilt kernel passes smoke per AGENTS.md rule.
- Real-KVM N=50 bench: phase_12b_ready_accept P50 drops by ≥30ms vs bead .1's number.
- Each option's contribution attributable via earlycon timing (depends on phase_12b decomp from .1).
- Documented in `docs/perf/kernel-config-additional.md` with measured before/after per knob.

## Dependencies

Layers on bead .6 (CONFIG_SMP=n + strip debug) and bead .5 (kernel cmdline nokaslr+nosmp). Same kernel rebuild can land all three together for one bench cycle.

## Effort

~1d (kernel rebuild + bench cycle + per-knob attribution work).

Added focused m80-image-build config regression tests and docs/perf/kernel-config-additional.md. title: cpuset.cpus per-VM pinning + WarmPool slot-aware CPU ranges
description:
## Why

m80-cgroup already has cpuset infrastructure (`inherit_sparse_cpuset_file` propagates parent's cpuset.cpus to leaf), and an integration test (`cgroup_cpuset_pinning_actually_constrains_affinity`) proves enforcement works end-to-end. But `Limits` has no `cpuset_cpus` field, so we never write an explicit pin per VM.

Without pinning, the kernel scheduler migrates vCPU/VMM threads across cores under load — TLB flushes, cache misses, scheduler jitter. At density (C=16+ on the 48-CPU bench host), assigning each VM a disjoint CPU range eliminates cross-VM thrash. On the idle bench: ~0ms. Under load / at density: 5-15ms P99 tightening on boot tail.

## Fix

1. Add `cpuset_cpus: Option<String>` to `Limits` (in `crates/m80-cgroup/src/lib.rs`).
2. In `apply_limits`, if set, write to leaf `cpuset.cpus` via `write_cgroup_file`.
3. Propagate from `SandboxConfig` → `Limits::preset()`.
4. **WarmPool slot-aware allocation**: extend `WarmPoolConfig` with optional CPU-range allocator. Each slot at fill time gets a disjoint range (e.g., slots 0/1/2 → cores 0-2/3-5/6-8). Pool slot's `RunningSandbox` carries its assigned range; the cgroup is created with that range.

## Files

- `crates/m80-cgroup/src/lib.rs:110-233` (Limits + apply_limits)
- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/config.rs` (SandboxConfig::cpuset_cpus)
- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch.rs:896` (preset wiring)
- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/warm_pool.rs:288` (slot range allocator)
- New: `docs/design/cpuset-pinning.md` — slot-to-range allocation policy, host CPU count discovery, behavior under host CPU count < pool size.

## Acceptance

- `Limits::preset()` accepts cpuset_cpus.
- Density bench at C=16: P99 tightens by ≥5ms vs unpinned baseline.
- WarmPool slot ranges visible in `/sys/fs/cgroup/m80-firecracker/<vm-id>/cpuset.cpus`.
- Test: spawn two concurrent pool slots; verify they get disjoint ranges.

## Effort

~1.5-2d.
notes: Implementation landed locally: Limits::cpuset_cpus writes leaf cpuset.cpus with cpuset controller enablement; SandboxConfig propagates to cgroup creation; WarmPoolCpuAllocator assigns disjoint per-slot ranges and returns them on lease discard/refill. Local verification passed: cargo test -p m80-cgroup; cargo check -p m80-firecracker --tests; cargo check -p m80-cli --tests; cargo test -p m80-firecracker cpu_allocator; cargo test -p m80-firecracker --test warm_pool; rustfmt --check --config skip_children=true on touched Rust files; git diff --check. Still blocked on acceptance evidence that needs the real density/KVM/root host: C=16 P99 >=5ms improvement and ignored root/KVM cpuset visibility test.

title: SCHED_FIFO for firecracker boot phase (with RAII demote guard)
description:
## Why

Guest vCPU thread runs at SCHED_OTHER (nice=0) and competes with all host processes for CPU. During the ~900ms boot window, every preemption by an unrelated SCHED_OTHER process stretches boot by one Linux scheduling quantum (4-20ms typically). On a contended host this adds 50-300ms P50.

SCHED_FIFO at priority 50 eliminates this competition for the boot duration. Demote back to SCHED_OTHER after ready signal so long-running execs don't starve other host work.

## CRITICAL prerequisite: RAII demote guard

A SCHED_FIFO process that hangs locks out other host workloads. Must demote on EVERY error path — easy to miss without RAII. The implementation MUST use `struct RtElevationGuard(Pid)` that demotes on drop, disarmed only after successful phase_12b. Otherwise this bead is unsafe to merge.

Additionally: cgroup `cpu.max` ceiling (already set via `Limits::preset()`) provides defense-in-depth — even an FIFO thread is rate-limited by the cgroup controller. Verify the existing cap is tight enough.

## Files

- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch.rs` — add phase 9b (elevate after phase_9) + phase 12c (demote after phase_12b). Use `nix::sched::sched_setscheduler`.
- NEW: `crates/m80-firecracker/src/rt_guard.rs` — `RtElevationGuard` with Drop impl.
- m80 host process needs CAP_SYS_NICE (already runs under sudo per launch — verify in preflight).
- `crates/m80-preflight/src/checks.rs` — check RLIMIT_RTPRIO if non-sudo path is ever supported.
- Tests: `crates/m80-firecracker/tests/sched_priority.rs` — verify priority is elevated post-9b, demoted post-12b, and demoted on every simulated error path between (phase_10 fail, phase_11 fail, phase_12a fail, phase_12b timeout).

## Acceptance

- Bench on loaded host (concurrent `stress -c $(nproc)` running): cold-launch P50 drops by ≥40ms.
- Bench on idle host: cold-launch P50 unchanged (no harm).
- Chaos test: kill the firecracker process during phase_11; verify the parent m80's RAII guard demoted before reaping (no lingering FIFO process).
- Smoke evidence per AGENTS.md (sched_setscheduler is kernel-touching).

## Out of scope

- No SCHED_DEADLINE (more complex, requires hardcoded deadline). FIFO is sufficient.
- No automatic priority adjustment based on host load. Static priority 50 with RAII demote is enough.

## Effort

~1-2d including the RAII guard + chaos tests.
acceptance_criteria: Measurement cross-link: docs/perf/measurement-playbook.md#e4-loaded-host-bench.
close_reason: Rejected: SCHED_FIFO experiment missed the loaded-host recovery bar (loaded P50 1494 ms vs 1488 ms baseline, phase_12b P50 1067.824 ms vs 1052.150 ms, 1/50 failure); see docs/perf/sched-fifo.md.

title: Pre-fork firecracker process pool (BlankPool — distinct from WarmPool)
description:
## Why

Existing warm-pool (`crates/m80-firecracker/src/warm_pool.rs`) holds N pre-restored VMs (~1 GiB RAM each). This bead is **distinct**: a pool of pre-forked Firecracker processes with NO VM started yet. Saves only phase_9 (~25ms), not the full boot — but costs ~15 MiB/slot instead of ~1 GiB/slot. Useful when:

- Snapshot infrastructure isn't usable for a workload
- Memory cost of warm-pool slots is the constraint
- Caller wants per-launch parameter freedom (different network mode, different config) that the warm-pool's pre-committed config doesn't allow

## Design constraint surfaced by the audit

`phase_4_jailer_materialize` bundles scratch bind-mount setup with everything else. Blank slots either:
(a) pre-allocate scratch at fill time (wasteful for no-workspace requests), or
(b) defer scratch binding to configure time (requires extending the jailer's bind-mount API to accept post-fork additions).

Option (a) is simpler; (b) is the correct long-term shape. Start with (a); document the tradeoff.

## Files

- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/warm_pool.rs` — sibling `blank_pool.rs` if line count grows past 700 in warm_pool.rs.
- New types: `BlankSlot`, `BlankPool`, `BlankLease`.
- State machine: `Blank → Configured (PUTs done) → Running → Stopped/Discarded`.
- Hold slots at `Blank` (simpler, more general). `Configured`-stage is a follow-up optimization.
- `crates/m80-cli/src/cmds/blank/` — CLI surface mirroring `warm/`.
- `docs/design/blank-pool.md` — design + scratch-bundling tradeoff + state machine.

## Acceptance

- BlankPool fills to target_blanks in background.
- `try_lease` → `Sandbox::configure_and_start(slot, config)` → exec returns within 1.5-1.6s P50 (the warm-pool's 20ms allocate is impossible here; we still pay phase_11+12).
- Per-slot memory ≤30 MiB vs WarmPool's ~1 GiB.
- Density: BlankPool with 20 slots costs <1 GiB host RAM (vs WarmPool's 20 GiB).
- Tests: chaos kill of a Blank slot → background fill replaces it.

## Effort

~M (~3d). Less than WarmPool because no snapshot path; shares fill-thread + condvar infrastructure.
close_reason: Rejected/not-justified: BlankPool would now save at most the remaining phase_9_jailer_launch slice (~15.588 ms P50 after m80-jp6ik.21) while current stripped minimal cold path is already ~1340-1355 ms P50, below the bead's own 1.5-1.6 s acceptance band. Implementing it would require a new half-launched lifecycle state, cleanup/CLI surface, and scratch-binding tradeoff for low-double-digit ms. Evidence: docs/perf/blank-pool.md.

title: CPU template: default None (remove unconditional T2 on Intel)
description:
## Why

`crates/m80-firecracker/src/preboot.rs:160-172` — `host_cpu_template()` returns `Some(CpuTemplate::T2)` on Intel hosts, unconditionally. T2 masks CPUID + MSRs for AWS live-migration portability. m80 does NOT live-migrate. The masking costs 50-500μs of MSR VMExits during phase_12a + early guest boot (each CPUID read triggers a VMExit).

The fix: default to `None` (no template). Callers that need cross-host snapshot portability can opt in to T2/C3 via `SandboxConfig::cpu_template`.

Pinning test at `preboot_tests.rs:42-51` (`layer_1_machine_config_uses_narrow_cpu_surface`) — needs updating to assert `cpu_template == None` and rename.

## Files

- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/preboot.rs:156,160-172` — remove unconditional `host_cpu_template()`; wire `SandboxConfig::cpu_template` (default None).
- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/config.rs` — add `cpu_template: Option<CpuTemplate>` field.
- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/preboot_tests.rs:42-63` — update test, delete `cpu_template_uses_t2_only_on_intel_hosts`.
- `crates/m80-firecracker/README.md` ~line 211 — update first-line machine shape description.

## Acceptance

- Default config sends no `cpu_template` field in machine-config PUT.
- Bench: phase_12a_instance_start P50 drops by ≥50μs (small but free).
- Test: snapshot/restore on same host still works without T2 masking.
- Snapshot portability tradeoff documented: future cross-host restore will require host-CPU-feature parity verification, not template-based masking.

## Effort

~1h.
acceptance_criteria: Measurement cross-link: docs/perf/measurement-playbook.md#e12-cpu-template-delta.
notes: Implemented hard cutover to default cpu_template=None with explicit SandboxConfig::cpu_template opt-in. Verification: cargo test -p m80-firecracker preboot --lib; cargo test -p m80-firecracker --no-run; cargo test -p m80-cli --no-run; cargo build --release -p m80-cli; same-host snapshot restore passed via snapshot_integration::capture_then_restore_round_trip. Measurement per docs/perf/cpu-template.md and crates/m80-firecracker/benches/snapshots/cpu-template-delta.json missed the close gate: phase_12a_instance_start P50 changed 18,393us -> 18,591us (+198us), target was >=50us drop. Blocked pending remeasurement, rescope, or a follow-up implementation that satisfies the latency gate.
close_reason: Implemented hard cutover to default cpu_template=None with explicit opt-in, but rejected as a latency win: same-host snapshot restore passed, while phase_12a_instance_start measured 18,393 us -> 18,591 us (+198 us), missing the >=50 us drop target. Evidence: docs/perf/cpu-template.md and cpu-template-delta.json.

title: THP advisory in preflight + ops doc (complement to hugepages bead)
description:
## Why

Host THP setting is invisible to m80 today. Many distros default to `madvise` mode, meaning Firecracker's anonymous guest RAM gets only 4 KiB pages unless explicitly madvised (which Firecracker doesn't do — it offers explicit huge_pages via machine-config instead, which is bead .13). With `always` mode, the kernel applies THP to all anon regions, including Firecracker's guest memory — giving most of bead .13's TLB-pressure benefit with zero host hugepage reservation.

## Fix

m80 cannot call MADV_HUGEPAGE on Firecracker's address space (it's a child process). The lever is operator visibility: preflight reads `/sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/enabled` and surfaces the current setting + recommendation.

## Files

- `crates/m80-preflight/src/checks.rs` — add `check_thp_policy` (non-blocking advisory CheckRow). Read `/sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/enabled`; if `[madvise]` or `[never]` is selected, emit a one-line note pointing at the ops doc.
- NEW: `docs/ops/host-tuning.md` (or extend existing) — section on THP. Recommended setting + the `echo always > /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/enabled` command.

## Acceptance

- Preflight on a `madvise`-default host emits the advisory.
- Preflight on an `always`-mode host emits a clean row.
- No pass/fail change (this is informational).
- Ops doc explains the tradeoff vs bead .13 (explicit huge_pages): always-mode = best-effort no host setup; bead .13 = guaranteed but needs `sysctl vm.nr_hugepages=N`.

## Effort

~1h.
close_reason: verified: cargo test -p m80-preflight; cargo build -p m80-cli; sudo m80 --json preflight emitted Transparent hugepages advisory row on madvise host @ c497d58

title: Right-size guest RAM default: 1024 MiB → 512 MiB
description:
## Why

`crates/m80-firecracker/src/types.rs:23` — `FIRST_LINE_MEM_SIZE_MIB = 1024`. Every VM gets 1 GiB by default. For most agent tool-calls (`python -c ...`, `ls`, `cat`, `bash`-driven commands) this is 4-10× oversized. Effects:

- Kernel zone init at boot scales with mem_size → 20-60ms cold-launch overhead (needs measurement).
- Host RAM committed = 8 × 1 GiB = 8 GiB at C=8.
- `mem.snap` size for snapshots = 1 GiB regardless of actual use.

Right default is 512 MiB (covers `pip install` of mid-size packages, `npm install`, small `cargo build`). 256 MiB is too tight (OOMs on `pip install torch` etc.). Workloads that need more set `SandboxConfig::mem_size_mib: Some(2048)` explicitly — the override path already exists.

## Friction point (good)

`crates/m80-firecracker/tests/snapshot/first_line_sizing.rs:9` asserts `FIRST_LINE_MEM_SIZE_MIB == 1024`. Updating it is the right friction — makes the change deliberate.

## Files

- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/types.rs:23` — change to 512; update doc comment at line 22 + 213.
- `crates/m80-firecracker/tests/snapshot/first_line_sizing.rs:9` — assert 512.
- `crates/m80-cli/src/cmds.rs` — optional `--mem-size-mib` CLI flag (separate small follow-up; API-level override already works).
- Bench cycle to capture the actual phase_12b delta with smaller RAM.

## Acceptance

- Default changes; bench shows phase_12b P50 unchanged or modestly improved.
- Snapshot size halves (`mem.snap`).
- Density bench at C=8 with default mem: host RAM commit halves.
- Documented in `docs/perf/mem-sizing.md` with the workload-coverage rationale (which packages fit).

## Effort

~1h change + bench cycle.
acceptance_criteria: Measurement cross-link: docs/perf/measurement-playbook.md#e3-mem-size-sweep.
close_reason: implemented: FIRST_LINE_MEM_SIZE_MIB is 512 MiB; first-line docs/tests updated; mem-sizing measurement in m80-jp6ik.44 supports unchanged launch P50 and halved mem.snap/default commit

title: virtio-rng: PUT /entropy device (eliminate boot entropy stall)
description:
## Why

Firecracker supports a virtio-rng device via `PUT /entropy` (added v1.3, well above our v1.14.4 CVE floor). m80 never PUTs it. Without virtio-rng, the guest's `getrandom()` blocks until kernel entropy is seeded from interrupt timing — a 20-100ms stall on first exec depending on guest kernel config. Many minimal kernels lack a CONFIG_RANDOM_TRUST_CPU or boot RNG seed entry, making this a real and reproducible cost.

## Files

- `crates/m80-firecracker-client/src/lib.rs` — add `put_entropy_device()` method. Body is `{}` (or `{"rate_limiter": {...}}` if rate-limiting); empty config gives FC default.
- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/preboot.rs` — emit the PUT inside `apply_preboot_puts` before InstanceStart. No config needed in `SandboxConfig` (always-on is right; the device is virtually free).

## Acceptance

- `put_entropy_device` exists in client; client README updated.
- Preboot plan always includes entropy PUT (no opt-out).
- Integration test: confirm a guest read of /dev/random returns ≥256 bytes within 5ms (currently blocks 20-100ms).
- Bench cold-launch P50 drops or first-exec latency drops measurably (capture before/after).
- CHANGELOG entry.

## Effort

~1h.

## Done

First-exec entropy stall eliminated. Verified by reading /dev/random inside guest at process_start and timing.
close_reason: implemented always-on virtio-rng preboot PUT /entropy; client tests cover request JSON and typed error; preboot tests cover order/phase name; docs=docs/behaviors/lifecycle/virtio-rng.md,docs/behaviors/lifecycle/preboot-wiring.md; changelog updated; release real-KVM N=50 minimal/idle passed with phase_11_put_entropy P50=112us and wallclock P50=1728ms; direct guest dd read 256 bytes from /dev/random with real 0m0.00s

title: KVM host-tuning advisory: halt_poll_ns + ops doc
description:
## Why

Three host-side KVM sysctls have small but real impact on boot-phase jitter. m80 today has no visibility into their settings, no preflight checks, and no ops documentation. Operators tuning a m80 host don't know which knobs matter.

Candidates:
- `/sys/module/kvm/parameters/halt_poll_ns` (default 200000) — host busy-polls before parking vCPU on HLT. Higher = lower wakeup latency, higher idle CPU burn. Latency-priority deployments: 400000. Density-priority: leave or lower.
- `/sys/module/kvm/parameters/halt_poll_ns_grow / shrink` — adaptive sizing. Defaults fine.
- `/sys/module/kvm_intel/parameters/enable_preemption_timer` — affects whether `lapic_timer_advance_ns` matters.

Expected: 2-10ms phase_12b improvement on latency-priority hosts. Mostly visibility.

## Files

- `crates/m80-preflight/src/checks.rs` — add `check_kvm_halt_poll`. Informational CheckRow (no pass/fail) with the current value + note pointing at ops doc.
- NEW or extended: `docs/ops/host-tuning.md` — section on KVM tuning. Recommended values per deployment posture. Concrete commands (`echo 400000 > /sys/module/kvm/parameters/halt_poll_ns`).

## Acceptance

- Preflight surfaces the value on every run.
- Ops doc covers halt_poll_ns + lapic_timer_advance_ns + preemption-timer interaction.
- This is a visibility bead, not a measured latency win — no bench gate.

## Effort

~1.5h.
acceptance_criteria: Measurement cross-link: docs/perf/measurement-playbook.md#e11-kvm-halt-poll-advisory.
close_reason: verified: cargo test -p m80-preflight; cargo build -p m80-cli; sudo m80 --json preflight emitted KVM halt polling row with halt_poll_ns=200000 @ 2db14a7

title: Replace async rtnetlink + Tokio with sync netlink (guestd + net-outbound)
description:
## Why

Two distinct code sites build a Tokio current-thread runtime per launch to drive rtnetlink (async-only API):

1. **guestd** — `crates/m80-guestd/src/pid_one_network.rs:160-228` — `RtnetlinkConfigurator` builds a Tokio runtime, makes 4 sequential netlink round-trips. Bead .12 (defer to post-ready) hides this; but the Tokio runtime construction itself is ~5-10ms wasted.
2. **m80-net-outbound** — `crates/m80-net-outbound/src/link_ops.rs:107-298` — `NetlinkLinkOps` does the same pattern: 8 operations during bridge/TAP setup, all sequential, all individually block_on'd.

The Tokio runtime initialization (epoll/io-uring driver, time driver, executor, task queue, IO thread) buys nothing — every call is immediately `block_on`'d. Drop Tokio entirely; use synchronous netlink.

Combined savings: 10-20ms per launch (additive to bead .12 which defers; this eliminates).

## Replacement strategy

Use `netlink-sys::Socket` in blocking mode (sync API exists in the same crate); construct messages with `netlink-packet-route` (no Tokio dep). Drop `rtnetlink` + `tokio` deps from both crates.

Code shape per operation: send/receive one `RTM_*` message via sync `Socket`. ~100-200 lines per call site replacing the rtnetlink Handle calls.

## Files

- `crates/m80-guestd/src/pid_one_network.rs:160-228` — replace `RtnetlinkConfigurator`.
- `crates/m80-guestd/Cargo.toml` — drop `rtnetlink`, `tokio`, `futures-util`; keep `netlink-packet-route`, `netlink-sys`.
- `crates/m80-net-outbound/src/link_ops.rs:99-298` — replace `NetlinkLinkOps`.
- `crates/m80-net-outbound/Cargo.toml` — same dep swap.
- Tests: behaviorally equivalent (same rtnetlink protocol on the wire); existing integration tests should pass unchanged.

## Acceptance

- Both crates build without `tokio` dep.
- Guest binary size drops (one of the bigger transitive deps gone).
- Existing network smoke tests pass.
- Bench: post-ready network configuration completes 5-10ms faster on each side.

## Effort

~M (~2-3d). Hand-rolled message construction is the long pole.

## Note

This pairs with bead .12 (iptables-restore batching) — both attack the network setup cost from different angles.
acceptance_criteria: Measurement cross-link: docs/perf/measurement-playbook.md#e8-tokio-runtime-wallclock.
close_reason: not-justified: m80-jp6ik.48 measured Tokio runtime construction at 20-30us, far below the 3ms reconsideration threshold; outbound cost is link/policy work, not runtime construction

title: Cgroup micro-cuts: cgroup.kill at teardown + skip leaf controllers read
description:
## Why

Two small cgroup-side cuts identified in the audit, both XS:

1. **`cgroup.kill` at teardown** — `crates/m80-cgroup/src/lib.rs:160-166` (Drop impl) — current path calls `remove_dir` bare; if live PIDs remain it fails with `LivePids` warn-log. Writing `1` to `cgroup.kill` first guarantees the group is empty atomically (single syscall, no race against new spawns). Correctness upgrade more than perf, but cleaner.

2. **Skip leaf `cgroup.controllers` read** — `crates/m80-cgroup/src/lib.rs:394-411` (`write_subtree_control`) — does `read_to_string("cgroup.controllers")` to verify the controller is available BEFORE writing `subtree_control`. After bead .10 (OnceLock gating ancestor writes), the leaf-level availability check is redundant: if the parent's enable succeeded, the leaf inherits the controller. Saves ~0.5ms per `Subtree::create`.

## Files

- `crates/m80-cgroup/src/lib.rs:160-166` (Drop impl — write to cgroup.kill before rmdir)
- `crates/m80-cgroup/src/lib.rs:394-411` (skip leaf availability check)

## Acceptance

- Teardown: zombie processes can no longer cause `remove_dir` failures; `cgroup.kill` reaps cleanly.
- phase_5b_cgroup_create P50 drops ~0.5ms (small but free).
- Test: spawn a sandbox, force a hang, verify `cgroup.kill` cleans up without warnings.

## Effort

~2h.

## Dependency

Depends on bead .10 (OnceLock for ancestor subtree_control) — landing this first preserves the leaf-write availability invariant.
notes: Code/docs/tests landed locally: Drop now writes cgroup.kill before rmdir, and subtree-control setup validates root cgroup.controllers once before unchecked descendant writes. Verified: rustfmt --edition 2021 --check crates/m80-cgroup/src/lib.rs crates/m80-cgroup/src/tests.rs; cargo test -p m80-cgroup subtree_control --lib; cargo test -p m80-cgroup kill_cgroup --lib; cargo test -p m80-cgroup; cargo test -p m80-cgroup --no-run; git diff --check. Independent review pass found no actionable regressions. Blocked on external acceptance evidence: phase_5b_cgroup_create latency delta and root/writable-cgroup smoke that forces a hung sandbox and confirms cgroup.kill cleanup without warnings.

title: Vsock proto micro-cuts: coalesce frame writes + remove send-side clone
description:
## Why

Proto wire framing audit surfaced two specific micro-cuts in m80-vsock + m80-proto:

1. **Two `write_all` syscalls per frame** — `crates/m80-vsock/src/framing.rs:73-74` (`write_raw_frame`) writes the 4-byte length prefix then the body as two separate `write_all` calls. On a UnixStream these don't add Nagle delay, but each is a syscall (~200-400ns). For a streaming exec with 50-200 chunk frames this aggregates to 10-80μs.

2. **Unnecessary `Envelope<T>` clone on every send** — `crates/m80-vsock/src/lib.rs:89` (`send_envelope`) calls `RawEnvelope::from_typed(envelope.clone())`. `from_typed` consumes the envelope, so the clone exists only to satisfy the borrow. For an `ExecRequest` with vec-of-strings args + 60-char request_id + optional stdin, the clone allocates 5-15 heap objects. ~1-3μs per exec send.

## Fix

- **framing.rs:73-74** — either (a) pre-allocate `Vec<u8>` with `body.len() + 4`, write prefix into it, then one `write_all`; or (b) wrap UnixStream in `BufWriter` and flush once per frame. Option (b) is cleaner; both work.
- **m80-vsock/src/lib.rs:89 + wire.rs:42** — change `from_typed` to accept `&Envelope<T>` and do the conversion by-ref. Call sites pass `envelope` not `envelope.clone()`.

## Acceptance

- Proto framing test in `crates/m80-vsock/tests/` confirms wire format unchanged.
- Streaming exec test verifies no behavioral diff (stdout chunks deliver correctly).
- Bench: streaming exec with 100 chunks shows ~10-40μs improvement. Per-exec single-shot shows ~1-3μs improvement.

## Effort

~3h.

## Note

This bead targets EXEC PERFORMANCE, not launch. Matters for the consumer that does many tool-call execs per session. Per launch it's noise; per session of 100 execs it's measurable.
notes: Implementation committed in 68d56fd: coalesced write_raw_frame prefix+body into one write_all, changed RawEnvelope::from_typed to borrow typed envelopes, updated call sites/docs, and added behavior/test coverage. Verified: cargo test -p m80-proto; cargo test -p m80-vsock; cargo test -p m80-firecracker --lib; cargo test -p m80-guestd-malicious --no-run; cargo test -p m80-firecracker --test wire_frame_boundaries_real_kvm --no-run; cargo test -p m80-firecracker --test fileop_errors_real_kvm --no-run; file-scoped rustfmt --check; git diff --check. Blocked only on acceptance benchmark evidence: streaming exec with 100 chunks and per-exec single-shot microbench.

title: Snapshot file fadvise WILLNEED during WarmPool background fill
description:
## Why

Bead .5 covers posix_fadvise(WILLNEED) on the launch-path artifacts (firecracker, jailer, kernel, rootfs). It does NOT cover snapshot files (mem.snap, vm.snap). Cold-cold restore (first restore after host reboot or page-cache eviction) pays the full read-from-disk cost on mem.snap — up to ~80ms of the +108ms cold-cold tax is attributable to this file.

The WarmPool background fill thread is the natural priming point: it's already filling slots in the background; adding fadvise on mem.snap costs nothing and overlaps with everything else the fill is doing.

## Fix

- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/warm_pool.rs` (`launch_slot` / background fill thread) — before calling `Sandbox::launch_from_snapshot`, open mem.snap and call `posix_fadvise(fd, 0, 0, POSIX_FADV_WILLNEED)` and same for vm.snap. Use `nix::fcntl::posix_fadvise`. Drop the fd; the kernel readahead is already queued.

OR

- `crates/m80-snapshot/src/lib.rs:263-268` — same call inside `restore()` just before passing to FC.

The WarmPool path is preferred because it gives more lead time for the readahead to complete before the actual fault storm.

## Acceptance

- fadvise calls added at one of the two sites.
- Cold-cold bench on restore path (drop_caches between runs, N=50): per-restore P50 drops by 20-60ms (the mem.snap portion of the +108ms tax).
- Warm-cache bench: zero change (pages already in cache).
- Documented in `docs/perf/page-cache-priming.md` (extending bead .5's doc).

## Effort

~1h.

## Done

Cold-cold restore tax reduced by the largest single-file fraction (mem.snap is by far the biggest artifact).
acceptance_criteria: Measurement cross-link: docs/perf/measurement-playbook.md#e2-cold-cold-restore-baseline.
notes: impl=Sandbox::launch_from_snapshot primes host-visible vm.snap+mem.snap with POSIX_FADV_WILLNEED before jail snapshot bind; docs=docs/behaviors/snapshot/file-prime.md,docs/perf/page-cache-priming.md; tests=cargo test -p m80-firecracker snapshot_file_prime --lib; compile=cargo test -p m80-firecracker --no-run; harness=bash scripts/test-bench-harness.sh; artifact=crates/m80-firecracker/benches/snapshots/cold-restore-fadvise-N50.json; result=baseline cold P50 93.945ms, fadvise cold P50 94.558ms (+0.613ms), warm P50 54.776ms, phase_restore_snapshot_prime cold P50 0.317ms; close gate missed, needs new approach or revised target before close
close_reason: Implemented snapshot-file WILLNEED priming, but rejected as a cold-restore improvement: cold restore P50 moved 93.945 ms -> 94.558 ms (+0.613 ms) instead of dropping 20-60 ms. The call is cheap but not a useful P50 recovery mechanism here. Evidence: docs/perf/page-cache-priming.md and cold-restore-fadvise-N50.json.

title: Reflink-capability preflight advisory + filesystem-choice ops doc
description:
## Why

`crates/m80-storage/src/rootfs.rs:14` clones the overlay template with `cp --reflink=auto --sparse=always`. The `--reflink=auto` silently falls back to a real byte-copy on filesystems without `FICLONE` support (ext4, tmpfs, FAT). Operators get no signal that they're paying full-copy cost.

Default `run_root` is `/var/run/m80` (config.rs:35). On systemd hosts this is tmpfs (symlink to `/run`) — meaning the typical default install pays full-copy on every launch AND keeps snapshots in RAM. Neither is documented.

## Fix

- `crates/m80-preflight/src/artifacts.rs` (`verify_run_root`) — extend with a reflink-capability probe: create two temp files in `run_root`, attempt `ioctl(FICLONE)`, emit a non-blocking advisory CheckRow either way ("reflink supported" / "reflink fallback: overlay clone will use full byte copy — switch to btrfs/xfs+reflink for faster cold-launch").
- `docs/ops/host-tuning.md` (or NEW `docs/ops/filesystem-choice.md`) — section on run_root FS choice. Tradeoffs: tmpfs (fastest mkdir/bind, RAM-capped, no reflink), ext4 (no reflink, slow at high directory churn), xfs (fast mkdir, optional reflink), btrfs (reflink default).
- Surface the default-run_root-is-tmpfs surprise: document that `/var/run/m80` resolves to tmpfs on systemd hosts.

## Acceptance

- Preflight advisory shows whether reflink is available on run_root.
- Ops doc clarifies FS choice.
- No behavior change to launch path (advisory-only).

## Effort

~2h.

## Note

This is a complement to bead .14 (erofs base — distinct: erofs is the rootfs image filesystem; this is the host run_root filesystem). Pair them in ops docs.
close_reason: Implemented run-root reflink preflight advisory, filesystem ops documentation, behavior capture, and regression tests; launch path remains unchanged.

title: Cgroup probe OnceLock (cache Subtree::probe result process-wide)
description:
## Why

`crates/m80-cgroup/src/lib.rs:39` (`Subtree::probe()`) reads `/proc/mounts` on every launch to confirm cgroup2 is mounted at `/sys/fs/cgroup`. Read also includes `cgroup.subtree_control` at the root.

These values are host-static — the cgroup mount hierarchy doesn't change during m80's lifetime. Bead .13 covers OnceLock for the ANCESTOR subtree_control WRITES; bead .26 covers SKIPPING the LEAF cgroup.controllers read. Neither covers the probe-mounts read itself.

~15-40μs per launch. Small individually, but every microsecond adds up at high launch rates.

## Fix

`crates/m80-cgroup/src/lib.rs:39` — wrap `Subtree::probe()` with `static PROBE_RESULT: OnceLock<Result<(), CgroupError>>`. First call does the read+parse; subsequent calls return the cached result.

Same `OnceLock` can cover the `cgroup.subtree_control` read inside `probe_mounts()` if it shares the cache.

## Acceptance

- `Subtree::probe()` reads `/proc/mounts` at most once per process.
- Test: invalidate-style check — temporarily remount cgroup somewhere else after `Subtree::probe()` has run; verify the cached result is still returned (the contract is "probe at process start; mount state doesn't change after").
- Bench: phase_5_cgroup_probe P50 drops by ~15-40μs.

## Effort

~30 min.
