title: Cache cpu_vendor in Discovery (eliminate per-launch /proc/cpuinfo read)
description:
## Why

`/proc/cpuinfo` is read in TWO places per launch:
1. `crates/m80-preflight/src/checks.rs:239` (`check_kvm_cpu_extensions`) — checks for vmx/svm.
2. `crates/m80-firecracker/src/preboot.rs:161` (`host_cpu_template`) — checks for `GenuineIntel` to apply T2 template.

The vendor + virt-flag info is process-static. The preflight read already has the cpuinfo string in memory; extracting the vendor at that point and stashing it in `Discovery` (which is threaded into `Backend`) eliminates the per-launch read in `host_cpu_template`.

~30-80μs per launch saved. Smaller in CLI mode, accumulates in daemon mode.

Bead .12 (CPU template default None) is the larger fix here — removes the unconditional T2 application entirely. But even with bead .12 landed, callers who explicitly opt INTO T2 should not pay the per-launch /proc/cpuinfo read.

## Fix

- `crates/m80-preflight/src/lib.rs` — add `cpu_vendor: CpuVendor` field to `Discovery` (enum: Intel, Amd, Other).
- `crates/m80-preflight/src/checks.rs:239` — extract vendor from the already-loaded cpuinfo string; populate `Discovery.cpu_vendor`.
- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/preboot.rs:161` — `host_cpu_template` becomes `host_cpu_template(discovery: &Discovery)`; reads `discovery.cpu_vendor` instead of `/proc/cpuinfo`.
- Delete the `cpu_template_for_cpuinfo` helper if it becomes unused after bead .12.

## Acceptance

- `/proc/cpuinfo` read only once per process (in preflight).
- Tests: `host_cpu_template(intel) == Some(T2)`; `host_cpu_template(amd) == None`.
- Bench: phase_11_rest_puts P50 drops by ~30-80μs.

## Dependency

Pairs with bead .12. If .12 lands first (default None), this becomes a smaller optimization (only matters when callers explicitly request T2). Land both together.

## Effort

~1h.
notes: Source-verified after m80-jp6ik.27: preboot no longer reads /proc/cpuinfo or infers T2 from host vendor. Machine config forwards SandboxConfig::cpu_template directly, defaulting to None; explicit T2 callers pass the typed CpuTemplate value without host probing. Remaining /proc/cpuinfo reads are preflight KVM capability checks and CLI env reporting, not per-launch REST PUT planning. Closing as superseded by the CPU-template hard cutover rather than adding an unused Discovery.cpu_vendor field.
close_reason: superseded by m80-jp6ik.27 CPU-template hard cutover; no per-launch cpuinfo read remains in preboot

title: DriveConfig cache_type=Unsafe for ephemeral overlay + workspace drives
description:
## Why

`crates/m80-firecracker-client/src/lib.rs:329-340` — `DriveConfig` has no `cache_type` field. Firecracker defaults to `cache_type: "Writeback"` (the more conservative setting), which means FC issues barriers/sync to the host filesystem on guest `fsync(2)` / `sync(2)` calls. For agent tool-call workloads (one-shot, ephemeral, throw away on teardown), this barrier cost is wasted — the data dies with the VM.

`cache_type: "Unsafe"` tells FC to skip the host-side sync. Guest writes are fast; host risks data loss on crash. For ephemeral workloads this is the correct tradeoff.

**Important caveat: this is an EXEC-PHASE win, not launch-phase.** Bench cold-launch P50 won't change. But every guest `fsync` or `sync` (e.g. `apt install`, `cargo build`, `pip install`) inside the VM benefits — typically 10-200ms saved per exec.

## Fix

- `crates/m80-firecracker-client/src/lib.rs:329-340` — add `cache_type: Option<CacheType>` to `DriveConfig`; new enum with `Writeback`/`Unsafe` variants. `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`.
- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/preboot.rs` — pass `cache_type: Some(CacheType::Unsafe)` on the overlay (`vdb`) and workspace (`vdc`) drives. NOT on base (`vda`) — read-only, irrelevant.
- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/config.rs` — optional `SandboxConfig::cache_type_override` for callers that need durability.
- README: document the ephemeral-default policy and how to override.

## Acceptance

- Preboot plan emits `cache_type: "Unsafe"` for vdb/vdc by default.
- Test: exec a script that does `sync` 100 times; assert wallclock drops vs Writeback baseline by ≥50%.
- Cold-launch bench: unchanged (this isn't a launch-path win).
- Smoke evidence per AGENTS.md (kernel-touching: changes FC durability semantics).

## Effort

~3h.
notes: Implementation committed in 23493d0: added typed Firecracker CacheType/DriveConfig cache_type support, defaulted preboot rootfs_overlay and workspace drives to CacheType::Unsafe, kept rootfs and hotplug placeholders unspecified, added SandboxConfig::drive_cache_type override for Writeback, propagated explicit constructors, and updated docs/behavior capture. Verified: cargo test -p m80-firecracker-client; cargo test -p m80-firecracker --lib; cargo check -p m80-firecracker --tests; cargo check -p m80-cli --tests; focused preboot/client tests; git diff --check. Blocked only on real acceptance evidence: sync-heavy exec benchmark, cold-launch unchanged note, and kernel-touching smoke evidence.

title: FC client HTTP: coalesce header+body write + drop json! macro intermediaries
description:
## Why

`crates/m80-firecracker-client/src/http.rs:18-31` (`send_json`) writes the HTTP request header and body as TWO separate `write_all` calls + `flush`. Each is a syscall. Over phase_11's 7 PUTs that's 14 write syscalls instead of 7. ~3-8μs/PUT × 7 = 21-56μs savings.

## Fix

`crates/m80-firecracker-client/src/http.rs:18-31` — either:
(a) wrap the UnixStream in `BufWriter`, do two `write_all` then one `flush` — coalesces in userspace then issues `writev`-equivalent on flush.
(b) Pre-assemble header + body into a single `Vec<u8>` and do one `write_all`.

Option (a) is one line; option (b) is two. Both fine.

Also: two call sites in `lib.rs:118` (`patch_vm_state`) and `lib.rs:168` (`instance_action`) build a `serde_json::Value` via the `json!{}` macro then serialize it. Switching to one-field private structs serialized directly saves ~2-5μs each. Small but right.

## Acceptance

- One `write_all` syscall per PUT instead of two.
- Bench phase_11_rest_puts P50 drops by 20-50μs.
- HTTP correctness unchanged (FC accepts the requests identically).

## Effort

~1h.

## Note

Small but cleanest cut in this round. Pairs with bead .15 (preflight sentinel) — both reduce FC client overhead.
notes: Code/docs/tests landed locally: HTTP send_json now assembles header+body into one request buffer and performs one write_all per REST request; patch_vm_state and instance_action use private typed payload structs instead of serde_json::Value/json! intermediates. Verified: rustfmt --edition 2021 --check crates/m80-firecracker-client/src/http.rs crates/m80-firecracker-client/src/lib.rs crates/m80-firecracker-client/tests/instance_action_serialization.rs; cargo test -p m80-firecracker-client send_json_writes_header_and_body_in_one_call --lib; cargo test -p m80-firecracker-client instance_action --test instance_action_serialization; cargo test -p m80-firecracker-client patch_vm_state --test snapshot; cargo test -p m80-firecracker-client; cargo test -p m80-firecracker-client --no-run; cargo check -p m80-firecracker --tests; git diff --check. Independent review pass found no issues. Blocked on phase_11_rest_puts benchmark evidence and existing graph gate m80-jp6ik.8.

title: Page-cache priming: posix_fadvise WILLNEED on FC+jailer+kernel+rootfs in preflight
description:
## Why

Cold-cold benchmark on 2026-05-12 measured a uniform +108ms penalty when page caches are dropped between runs. That's the cost of faulting kernel image + rootfs + firecracker binary + jailer binary back into memory. The penalty is deterministic (low jitter) — page-fault cost, not stochastic. `posix_fadvise(WILLNEED)` issued on these four files during preflight (which already holds all four paths) triggers async readahead overlapping with the rest of the launch.

## Files

- `crates/m80-preflight/src/binary.rs:99` — after `BinaryPreflight` is populated, open each binary and `nix::fcntl::posix_fadvise(fd, 0, 0, POSIX_FADV_WILLNEED)`. Two fadvise calls (firecracker, jailer).
- `crates/m80-preflight/src/artifacts.rs:80` — after `ArtifactPreflight.kernel` resolves, fadvise the kernel path.
- `crates/m80-storage/src/rootfs.rs:40` — top of `Rootfs::prepare`, fadvise the base rootfs path before `ensure_template`.

All four calls are async (no wait) and overlap with subsequent host-side work.

## Acceptance

- Four `posix_fadvise(WILLNEED)` call sites added; each behind a `#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]` or platform-gated helper.
- No new dependency (use `nix` already in workspace).
- Bench cold-cold (drop_caches between runs, N=50): +108ms penalty drops to ≤30ms.
- Document the mechanism in `docs/perf/page-cache-priming.md`.

## Out of scope

- Don't mlock anything. `mlock` pins pages in m80's address space, not Firecracker's. Wrong primitive.
- No background pinning daemon (separate deferred bead if cold-cold ever matters more than +108ms).

## Effort

~2h.

## Done

Cold-cold penalty reduced from ~108ms to ≤30ms at P50.
notes: Attempted the specified POSIX_FADV_WILLNEED implementation on 2026-05-13 and backed it out because the required cold-cold win did not materialize. Trial implementation primed Firecracker, jailer, m80-jailer-harden, kernel, and rootfs; moved rootfs priming before manifest verification; and primed base rootfs at Rootfs::prepare. Verification before backout: cargo test -p m80-preflight; cargo test -p m80-storage; cargo build --release -p m80-cli -p m80-jailer-harden; cold-isolated real-KVM N=50 minimal/idle stripped. Results: warm-cache reference 2026-05-13T16:34:08 P50 1728ms; cold-isolated with priming 2026-05-13T16:48:57 P50 1846ms (n=49, 1 failure); second cold-isolated with harden + pre-verify rootfs priming 2026-05-13T16:53:23 P50 1848ms (n=50). Earlier cold-cold baseline 2026-05-13T05:55:03 P50 1837ms. The cold tax remains roughly 110-120ms, mostly outside instrumented launch phases; WILLNEED is not sufficient here. Blocked pending a redesigned approach, likely preflight sentinel/cache work rather than this bead.
close_reason: Rejected: attempted POSIX_FADV_WILLNEED artifact priming for Firecracker, jailer, m80-jailer-harden, kernel, and rootfs, then backed it out because cold-isolated launch did not improve. Warm reference P50 1728 ms; prior cold baseline P50 1837 ms; primed cold runs were 1846 ms with 1 failure and 1848 ms. Evidence: docs/perf/page-cache-priming.md.

title: CPU governor preflight advisory + ops doc (acpi-cpufreq aware)
description:
## Why

CPU governor on the host (powersave/ondemand/performance/schedutil) affects cold-launch ramp-up. On `ondemand` with `acpi-cpufreq` driver, the host CPU can sit at idle frequency until launch starts, then takes 1-50ms to ramp — adding directly to phase_12b.

m80 has no preflight visibility. The pattern from beads .26 (KVM halt_poll), .27 (THP), .28 (BlankPool docs) is: non-blocking advisory CheckRow + ops doc section.

Driver matters: `intel_pstate`/`amd_pstate` with `powersave` is hardware-managed (HWP) — ramps in microseconds, no advisory needed. `acpi-cpufreq` with `ondemand` is software-managed — real cost. The check must distinguish.

## Fix

- `crates/m80-preflight/src/checks.rs` — add `check_cpu_governor`:
  - Read `/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu0/cpufreq/scaling_driver` and `scaling_governor`.
  - If driver = `intel_pstate` or `amd_pstate`: emit a clean CheckRow (HWP handles it).
  - If driver = `acpi-cpufreq` AND governor != `performance`: emit advisory "consider `cpupower frequency-set -g performance` for tighter launch tail — see docs/ops/host-tuning.md".
- `docs/ops/host-tuning.md` — extend with CPU governor section. Concrete commands per driver type.

Note: bench harness already exposes `CPU_GOVERNOR=performance` — that's a measurement knob, not a prod recommendation. Keep that scoping.

## Acceptance

- Preflight advisory fires only on acpi-cpufreq + non-performance.
- Stays silent on intel_pstate/amd_pstate (which is the majority of recent server hardware).
- Ops doc covers the driver distinction.

## Effort

~1.5h.

## Note

This is the third "host-tuning advisory" bead (sibling to .26 KVM and .27 THP). All three feed into the same `docs/ops/host-tuning.md` file — co-author them or land the doc once and append.
acceptance_criteria: Measurement cross-link: docs/perf/measurement-playbook.md#e7-cpu-governor-sweep.

title: Measurement: density sweep C={16,32,48,64} NoEgress + Outbound
description:
## Why

Current density data: flat from C=1 to C=8 (1726ms → 1754ms — +28ms over 8× concurrency). C>8 uncharacterized. The current gated density beads need data beyond C=8 before they can claim a real-substrate win:
- .13 chokepoints (network mutex, cgroup subtree_control): expected to bite C=12-16
- .20 nftables: claim trigger is "C=32 outbound still shows xtables.lock dominating after the iptables batching work lands"

This bead runs the density ladder at C={16, 32, 48, 64} for NoEgress AND Outbound modes, capturing wall-time-to-all-ready P50/P95/P99 + per-VM tail at each cell.

## Files

- `scripts/bench-cold-launch.sh` — already supports CONCURRENT; just invoke at higher Cs.
- `scripts/bench-density-extended.sh` (NEW or extend bench-extras.sh --density) — runs the sweep and aggregates.
- NEW: `crates/m80-firecracker/benches/density-extended.csv` + `snapshots/density-extended.json`.
- NEW or extended: `docs/perf/density-extended.md` — table of C × {NoEgress, Outbound} → wall-time + per-VM P99. Identifies first-contention-wall.

## Procedure

```sh
for C in 1 2 4 8 16 32 48 64; do
  CONCURRENT=$C ./scripts/bench-cold-launch.sh N=20 SKIP_LOADED=1
done
# Then again with outbound using the harness/network-mode knob current at implementation time:
for C in 1 2 4 8 16 32; do
  M80_NETWORK_POLICY=outbound CONCURRENT=$C ./scripts/bench-cold-launch.sh N=20 SKIP_LOADED=1
done
```

(C=64 only for NoEgress on a 48-CPU host — past 48 we're explicit-oversubscribe; valuable signal but flag as not-recommended-prod.)

## Acceptance

- Snapshot committed with N≥20 per cell for C∈{1,2,4,8,16,32,48} NoEgress + C∈{1,2,4,8,16,32} Outbound.
- `docs/perf/density-extended.md` documents first-wall location with annotated metric (e.g. "wall-time-to-all-ready P50 climbs >2× from C=16 to C=32 in outbound mode — xtables.lock candidate").
- The wall location + attribution feeds .13/.20 acceptance criteria.

## Effort

title: Measurement: TLB + cache-miss perf counters during phase_12b
description:
## Why

Bead .10 (hugepages backing) targets TLB pressure during guest boot. The expected gain is a guess without per-launch dTLB/iTLB miss counts. CPU-template work is tracked separately because it targets CPUID/MSR VMExits rather than TLB pressure.

`perf stat -e dTLB-load-misses,iTLB-load-misses,cache-misses` attached to the firecracker process during phase_12b gives the data. This is a measurement add-on that extends bead .1 (phase_12b decomp) — fits inside the same observability mode.

## Procedure

```sh
PERF_STAT=1 ./scripts/bench-cold-launch.sh N=20 SKIP_LOADED=1
```

In PERF_STAT mode, the bench script wraps the firecracker invocation with `perf stat -p $PID -e dTLB-load-misses:u,iTLB-load-misses:u,cache-misses:u --interval-print 100`. Output captured per launch into `crates/m80-firecracker/benches/perf-counters.csv`.

Requires `perf` binary installed + `kernel.perf_event_paranoid <= 1` on host.

## Files

- `scripts/bench-cold-launch.sh` — add PERF_STAT mode.
- NEW: `crates/m80-firecracker/benches/perf-counters.csv`.
- NEW or extended: `docs/perf/tlb-pressure.md` — baseline TLB miss counts during phase_12b. The bigger the count, the more bead .10 hugepages have to gain.

## Acceptance

- Baseline TLB-miss histogram committed.
- If dTLB-load-misses < 100K per launch: bead .10 hugepages payoff is bounded (TLB is already lightly pressured) — close .10 with notes.
- If dTLB-load-misses > 1M per launch: hugepages have meaningful headroom.

## Effort

~3h.
acceptance_criteria: Verified per docs/perf/measurement-playbook.md#e5-tlb-and-cache-miss-counters: docs/perf/tlb-pressure.md plus committed perf-counter artifacts.
close_reason: verified: docs/perf/tlb-pressure.md plus crates/m80-firecracker/benches/perf-counters.csv; N=20 minimal idle, sudo perf intervals, dTLB-load-misses P50 40.5K/P95 44.5K

title: Measurement: dirty-page fraction baseline (post-pristine + post-exec)
description:
## Why

Bead .19 (track_dirty_pages + Diff snapshots) requires knowing the dirty-page fraction after pristine boot to size the win. Without measurement, "Diff is N% smaller than Full" is a guess.

## Procedure

1. Enable `track_dirty_pages: true` in `MachineConfig` at boot (this requires bead .19's machine-config field to exist; chicken-and-egg, so this measurement work is partially part of .19 scaffolding).
2. After ready signal, query FC's internal dirty-page bitmap via PUT /snapshot/create with type=Diff after a no-op exec, measure file size, compare to a Full snapshot.
3. Repeat after a representative tool-call exec (e.g., `pip install requests`) — measures dirty fraction with workload.

## Files

- `scripts/bench-dirty-page-fraction.sh` (NEW).
- NEW: `crates/m80-firecracker/benches/dirty-fraction.csv` (rows: workload, dirty_pages, total_pages, dirty_fraction).
- NEW: `docs/perf/dirty-page-baseline.md`.

## Acceptance

- For a pristine post-ready VM with no workload: dirty fraction documented (likely <5%).
- For a VM after one representative exec: dirty fraction documented (likely 5-30%).
- These numbers gate .19 acceptance — if pristine dirty is already ~50%, Diff snapshots aren't much smaller than Full and .19's value drops.

## Dependency

Depends on partial scaffolding from .19 (machine-config field for track_dirty_pages). Sequence: scaffold .19's MachineConfig field → run this measurement → use results to inform .19 acceptance gate.

## Effort

~4h (depends on .19 prep).
acceptance_criteria: Verified per docs/perf/measurement-playbook.md#e6-dirty-page-fraction: docs/perf/dirty-page-baseline.md plus committed dirty-fraction artifacts.

title: Measurement: Tokio runtime construction wallclock (guestd + net-outbound)
description:
## Why

Bead .31 (sync rtnetlink, drop Tokio) claims 5-10ms saved per call site (guestd + net-outbound). The number is a literature estimate of Tokio current_thread runtime construction. Should be measured before committing to a M-effort dep swap.

## Procedure

Add temporary instrumentation (this is the measurement; gets removed/finalized when .31 lands):

- `crates/m80-guestd/src/pid_one_network.rs:160` — wrap `Builder::new_current_thread()...build()` with `Instant::now()` pair, log via guest_log's M80_GUEST_BOOT mechanism so the host parser (per .1 decomp) sees it.
- `crates/m80-net-outbound/src/link_ops.rs:107` — same.

Run N=20 cold launches with `M80_PHASE_TRACE=1`. Extract `tokio_runtime_build_us` from the phase-event stream.

## Files

- `crates/m80-guestd/src/pid_one_network.rs` — temp instrument.
- `crates/m80-net-outbound/src/link_ops.rs` — temp instrument.
- Bench harness consumes the M80_GUEST_BOOT line (via .1 decomp).
- NEW: `docs/perf/tokio-runtime-cost.md` — measured P50/P95 of runtime build on this host. ~5-10ms expected.

## Acceptance

- Measurement committed.
- If runtime build is <3ms: .31's payoff is smaller than estimated; reconsider effort/benefit. Maybe close as `not-justified`.
- If runtime build is >7ms: .31 is well-justified; proceed.

## Dependency

Depends on .1 (phase_12b decomp parser must be able to ingest M80_GUEST_BOOT line for tokio_runtime_build_us).

## Effort

~2h.

title: Kernel cmdline: add nokaslr + nosmp maxcpus=0 (1-vCPU guest)
description:
## Why

Two zero-cost kernel cmdline additions likely save 80-230ms inside the `phase_12b` window:

1. `nokaslr` — Firecracker loads vmlinux ELF (non-PIE); kernel still self-relocates with KASLR at boot. Disabling saves 30-80ms per published kernel-boot literature for similar configs.
2. `maxcpus=0 nosmp` — guest is configured with 1 vCPU (`FIRST_LINE_VCPU_COUNT = 1`, `crates/m80-firecracker/src/types.rs:19`) but kernel still runs `smp_init` (MADT enumeration, AP bring-up loop). With 1 vCPU these are dead work. Saves 50-150ms.

Both need real-KVM measurement (this is where bead .1 — phase_12b decomp — pays off).

## Files

- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/preboot.rs:33-34` — extend `STRIPPED_BOOT_ARGS` with `nokaslr nosmp maxcpus=0`. Verify the cmdline length stays under FC's limit (~512 bytes).

## Acceptance

- Real-KVM N=50 bench before and after; phase_12b_ready_accept P50 drops by ≥50ms.
- If the decomp bead (.1) is landed first, identify which sub-phase (kernel_init vs smp_init) actually drops.
- Roll back any flag that doesn't measure positive (don't keep zero-gain knobs as cargo cult).
- Document in `docs/perf/kernel-cmdline.md`.

## Dependencies

Strongly depends on bead .1 (decomp) for measurement attribution. Can land without it, but blind.

## Effort

~30 min change + bench cycle.
acceptance_criteria: Measurement cross-link: docs/perf/measurement-playbook.md#e9-kernel-cmdline-and-config-delta.
close_reason: closed as negative measurement: nokaslr nosmp maxcpus=0 candidate was not retained; after-change N=50 run was still at attempt 8 after >7min vs baseline full cell ~75s; doc=docs/perf/kernel-cmdline.md

title: Kernel config: CONFIG_SMP=n + strip debug symbols on vmlinux
description:
## Why

Two complementary kernel-config changes save space and likely boot time:

1. **CONFIG_SMP=n** — the m80-stripped.config currently has no explicit SMP setting, so `olddefconfig` inherits SMP=y from the defconfig. With 1 vCPU the SMP code paths (CPU enumeration, AP bring-up, IPI infra) are dead. Setting SMP=n at config time removes more than `nosmp` cmdline (which still leaves the SMP code linked in).
2. **`strip --strip-debug vmlinux`** — current `kernels/vmlinux-m80-*.bin` is "not stripped" per `file`. Firecracker's ELF loader ignores debug sections; stripping saves 3-5 MiB on disk and proportional sha256 verify time.

## Files

- `crates/m80-image-build/kernel-builder/m80-stripped.config` — add `CONFIG_SMP=n` (will cascade to disable HOTPLUG_CPU, SMP_TRAMPOLINE, etc. via Kconfig deps).
- `crates/m80-image-build/kernel-builder/build.sh` (or Dockerfile) — add `strip --strip-debug $OUT/vmlinux-m80-*.bin` as final step.
- `crates/m80-image-manifest/src/lib.rs` — if the manifest records kernel size, the sha256 will change — bump manifest version if schema is strict (check `m80-image-manifest/README.md`).

## Acceptance

- Kernel rebuild succeeds; image-manifest validates the new kernel.
- Boot still succeeds on N=50 minimal/idle (regression gate).
- phase_12b_ready_accept P50 drops measurably (target: ≥50ms after combining with b5's `nosmp` cmdline).
- Stripped kernel binary at ≤90% prior size on disk.
- Document in `docs/perf/kernel-config-smp.md`.

## Dependencies

Independent of b5 but pairs naturally. The bench should compare: baseline vs +b5 cmdline only vs +b5 cmdline + b6 config — establishes which one carries the win.

## Effort

~1d (kernel rebuild, image pipeline regen, baseline rebench).
acceptance_criteria: Measurement cross-link: docs/perf/measurement-playbook.md#e9-kernel-cmdline-and-config-delta.
notes: Implemented CONFIG_SMP=n in the stripped kernel seed config and changed the Docker kernel publish step to strip all ELF symbol tables before copying vmlinux. Added regression tests in m80-image-build for both invariants and updated the crate README plus docs/perf/kernel-config-smp.md. Verification: cargo test -p m80-image-build --test kernel_build_pipeline; m80-image-build kernel build --workspace /tank/projects/m80; file/readelf confirm stripped 15,810,168-byte artifact; temp minimal manifest verifies with m80-image-build verify; real-KVM smoke passed; N=50 minimal/idle snapshot crates/m80-firecracker/benches/snapshots/2026-05-13T17:06:51+00:00.json. Size target passed at 55.8% of prior 28,330,344-byte reference. Latency target did not pass: vs 2026-05-13T16:34:08 wallclock P50 1728ms -> 1693ms, but phase_12b_ready_accept P50 1,022,520us -> 1,041,442us.
close_reason: Implemented and measured; size/boot gates passed, ready-accept latency target missed and documented.

title: UFFD lazy snapshot restore (50-150ms warm-pool win)
description:
## Why

The `MemBackendType::Uffd` wire is already threaded — `m80-firecracker-client/src/lib.rs:418` defines it; `LoadSnapshotConfig::mem_backend` accepts it. But `m80-snapshot/src/lib.rs:265` hard-codes `MemBackendType::File`. With UFFD, the VM resumes immediately on restore; memory pages stream in via a userspace fault handler. This is the path to sub-100ms apparent restore time per Firecracker's own docs.

Cost: needs a UFFD handler process that holds the userfaultfd and services page faults from the snapshot file. Coordinating with Firecracker requires a separate small daemon (or thread) the warm-pool owner manages.

## Files

- `crates/m80-snapshot/src/lib.rs:263-268` — change the default restore backend to UFFD when a handler endpoint is configured; keep File as fallback.
- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/warm_pool.rs` (and lease.rs) — add UFFD handler lifecycle: spawn on pool init, route per-slot fault endpoints.
- NEW: `crates/m80-uffd/` — small crate holding the handler. Either a thread inside m80-firecracker or a separate process spawned per slot. Threads simplify lifecycle but share the firecracker process's UFFD; spec needs review.
- `docs/design/uffd-restore.md` — NEW. Coordination protocol, fault-handler policy (read-on-fault vs prefetch-ahead), failure modes.

## Acceptance

- UFFD handler implemented; restores go through it by default.
- Warm-pool allocate latency drops from ~274ms P50 toward ~100-200ms P50.
- Regression test: kill the UFFD handler mid-restore; verify the VM dies cleanly without dangling memory state.
- Falls back to MemBackendType::File when M80_DISABLE_UFFD=1.

## Risks

- UFFD handler stall = guest hang on fault. Need a watchdog.
- Per-slot vs per-pool handler is a real design choice; document and pick one in `docs/design/uffd-restore.md` before implementing.

## Effort

~3-5d.

## Done

Warm-pool restore measurably faster; UFFD path covered by integration + chaos test.

title: Erofs base rootfs (replace ext4 read-only base; eliminate journal replay)
description:
## Why

Base rootfs is mounted read-only by Firecracker (`is_read_only: true`, `crates/m80-firecracker/src/preboot.rs:77`). ext4 in read-only mode still has journal-replay overhead at guest mount. **erofs** (Enhanced Read-Only File System) is purpose-built: no journal, optimized inode layout for sequential metadata reads, lz4hc compression giving 20-30% smaller image. Guest kernel handles the mount; m80 just builds with erofs and binds a different rootfs type.

The overlay stays ext4 (erofs is read-only by design).

## Files

- `crates/m80-image-build/kernel-builder/m80-stripped.config` — add `CONFIG_EROFS_FS=y` (kernel rebuild required).
- `crates/m80-image-build/src/pipeline.rs:290-297` — add a `kind = "erofs"` build path. Use `mkfs.erofs -zlz4hc -d <tree> <output>`.
- `crates/m80-image-build/src/minimal.rs:105-111` — same for minimal.
- `crates/m80-image-manifest/src/lib.rs` — add `ImageKind::Erofs` discriminant; bump manifest schema or document fwd-compat.
- `crates/m80-guestd/src/pid_one.rs:165-300` — change mount type for the base disk from `"ext4"` to filesystem-from-manifest (defaults to ext4, accepts erofs).
- `crates/m80-firecracker/README.md` + image-build README.

## Acceptance

- Erofs build path produces a working image (smoke test: `M80_IMAGE_KIND=minimal-erofs ./scripts/smoke.sh`).
- Real-KVM cold-launch bench shows phase_12b_ready_accept P50 drops by ≥15ms (target: 20-30ms).
- Image on disk ≥20% smaller than ext4 equivalent.
- Smoke evidence in PR per AGENTS.md kernel-touching rule (this changes guest kernel config + mount type).

## Effort

~3-4d.
close_reason: Functional minimal-erofs support landed and smokes with stripped kernel; image size is 3,080,192 bytes vs 268,435,456-byte minimal ext4. Latency acceptance missed: N=50 stripped-kernel idle phase_12b_ready_accept improved only 1022994->1020781 us warm and 1031767->1022815 us cold-isolated, below the required >=15 ms; cold-isolated erofs also had 2 failures. Evidence: docs/perf/minimal-erofs.md.

title: io_engine=Async (io_uring) for overlay + workspace drives
description:
## Why

Firecracker's `DriveConfig` has supported `io_engine: "Async"` (io_uring-backed virtio-blk) since v1.1, well above our v1.14.4 CVE floor. m80's `DriveConfig` struct in `crates/m80-firecracker-client/src/lib.rs:329-340` has no `io_engine` field, so we always get the sync default. io_uring bypasses kernel page cache lock contention on multi-VM bursty writes.

Save 10-30ms on I/O-heavy execs; near-zero for CPU-only. Plus better density behavior (less lock contention across C concurrent VMs).

## Files

- `crates/m80-firecracker-client/src/lib.rs:329-340` — add `io_engine: Option<IoEngine>` to `DriveConfig`; add `pub enum IoEngine { Sync, Async }` with serde rename to `"Sync"`/`"Async"`. `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`.
- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/preboot.rs:73-103` — emit `io_engine: IoEngine::Async` on the rootfs overlay (`vdb`) and workspace (`vdc`) PUTs. Leave base (`vda`) as default; it's read-only and async gives no benefit there.
- m80-firecracker-client README + CHANGELOG.

## Acceptance

- DriveConfig has io_engine; serde round-trips correctly.
- Preboot plan emits Async for overlay + workspace.
- Cold-launch bench unchanged (this isn't a launch-path win).
- Exec-with-io bench (write 100MB inside guest, time it): drops by 10-30ms or shows reduced jitter.
- Density bench (C=8) shows reduced wallclock variance.

## Effort

~3h.
notes: impl=DriveConfig io_engine Option<IoEngine> with PascalCase serde; preboot sets Async for rootfs_overlay and workspace; rootfs/hotplug slots omit io_engine; memlock default changed to inherited because memlock=0 caused Firecracker async drive PUT failure with io_uring_setup ENOMEM; docs=docs/behaviors/lifecycle/io-engine-async.md,docs/perf/io-engine-async.md; tests=cargo test -p m80-firecracker-client --test put_each_resource; cargo test -p m80-firecracker-client --test error_mapping drive_400; cargo test -p m80-firecracker preboot --lib; cargo test -p m80-jailer default_resource_limits --lib; cargo test -p m80-jailer launch_redirects_stdio_and_passes_hardening_args --lib; no-run=cargo test -p m80-firecracker-client --no-run,cargo test -p m80-firecracker --no-run,cargo test -p m80-jailer --no-run; real-kvm=sudo cargo test -p m80-firecracker --test end_to_end_real_kvm end_to_end_real_kvm_boot_exec_stop_delete -- --ignored --nocapture passed after memlock inherited; close gate blocked pending sync-vs-Async exec-with-io benchmark

title: audit-iter-1: simplicity/correctness cleanup from 10-agent sweep
description: First iteration of the simplicity/correctness audit. 10 parallel sonnet agents swept lifecycle, launch+backend, jailer, cli, guestd, proto, vsock, net-*, image-build, and cross-crate errors. This epic groups the high-leverage structural findings. False positives excluded (e.g. RunningSandbox::capture snapshot_bind drop is correct — REST call has returned by drop time).

title: lifecycle: mem::forget on kill failure leaks jail/cgroup RAII guards
description: crates/m80-firecracker/src/lifecycle.rs:219,225 — if kill_and_reap_pid fails inside force_kill paths the code uses mem::forget(self) which skips Drop on jail (would unmount + remove run-dir) and cgroup (would remove subtree). Result: silent host-side leak on the worst-case path. Fix: either propagate the partial-cleanup error with the guards still dropping, or explicitly call jail.cleanup()/cgroup.cleanup() before forget.

title: proto+errors: collapse Other(String)-shaped error variants per doctrine
description: Variants found: ProtoError::MalformedPayload/EncodeFailed, WireProtocolError::MalformedPeer/PeerRejected, FcError::UnsupportedOperation/WarmPoolFillFailed, ConfigError::InvalidValue, NetError::HostRouteCollision/NetworkCommandFailed/NetlinkOperationFailed/InvalidNetworkState, PreflightError::StorageHelperMissing, StorageError::SwapFailed (drops io::Error), DriveHotplugError::Io (drops netlink error). Also: lift duplicated PathIo into a tiny shared crate or stop duplicating.

description: pid_one.rs:495-521 and connection/hotplug.rs:285-294. Replace with #[cfg(test)] free-function injection or integration tests against a real shim. Removes ~50 lines of trait + impl boilerplate.

title: lifecycle: idle-watcher activity guard missing on fileops/health/metrics
description: fileops.rs:252, health.rs:13, metrics.rs:13 — these RPC paths do not bump active_execs/last_activity_ns the way exec.rs does via begin_exec_activity. An in-flight file op or ping can race with the idle watcher firing shutdown. Lift the begin_exec_activity()/ExecActivityGuard pattern into a RunningSandbox method and call it from all four RPC paths.

title: guestd: uevent_registry OnceLock has a races between get() and set()
description: crates/m80-guestd/src/connection/hotplug.rs:346 — between OnceLock::get() returning None and OnceLock::set() landing, two concurrent hotplug requests can both call spawn_netlink_listener and both threads run forever (only one registry survives). Fix: OnceLock::get_or_init or a Mutex around the spawn decision.

title: guestd: workspace e2fsck -y -f silently repairs corrupted overlays on mount failure
description: crates/m80-guestd/src/pid_one.rs:578-605 — on mount failure the code runs e2fsck -y -f and re-mounts. This is silent recovery on persisted state and violates the no-silent-recovery doctrine. Fix: surface the mount failure; let the host decide whether to repair (likely via a one-shot tool or fail-loud).

title: guestd: protocol/oversize errors silently drop the frame without an error response

title: E2E writeback × exit-code matrix coverage
description:
m80's writeback policy (--writeback never|on-success|always) gates whether workspace mutations land back on the host after the guest exits. The unit-level should_writeback(mode, exit_code) gate is tested in m80-cli/src/cmds/tests.rs, but **no e2e test pins the user-visible behavior** (does host /some/dir/file.txt exist after the VM stops?).

The interesting matrix cells:

| Mode | Exit 0 | Exit non-zero |
|---|---|---|
| Never | host unchanged | host unchanged |
| OnSuccess | host has file | **host unchanged** (the gate's value-prop) |
| Always | host has file | **host has file** (this mode's value-prop) |

The two bolded cells are the actual policy decisions. If someone refactors should_writeback and inverts a branch, the unit test would catch it but the e2e behavior is what users observe. Without an e2e test, that property is unpinned.

## Why now

- Real-KVM e2e file (m80-firecracker/tests/end_to_end_real_kvm.rs) exists and exercises full boot→exec→stop→delete flow, but doesn't touch WritebackMode (all assertions are exit_code: Some(0) and don't observe host /workspace state).
- m80-storage/tests/change_extraction.rs has storage-layer tests but: (a) extraction_only_when_requested is misnamed — it doesn't actually call Scratch::extract; (b) the real extraction tests (stages_into_sibling_directory, loop_mount_extracts_changed_file_set) are #[ignore = "requires root and a loop device"] so don't gate normal CI.
- Adapters writing against m80 will rely on the writeback contract (especially OnSuccess + non-zero exit → host untouched, the build-failed-don't-pollute case).

## Children

Three child tasks, one per mode. Each covers both exit-code variants for that mode (so 6 cells across 3 tasks). Tests live in m80-firecracker/tests/ alongside end_to_end_real_kvm.rs and use the same real-KVM harness pattern.

## Acceptance for the umbrella

- 3 new test functions under m80-firecracker/tests/ (or parameterized cover-all-6 if cleaner).
- Same #[ignore = real KVM] gating as existing e2e.
- Each test sets up a host workspace dir with known initial state, runs m80 run with a guest command that writes a file and exits with configured code, asserts host dir contents post-stop.
- Test names make refactor regressions obvious (e.g., on_success_with_failed_exit_does_not_extract).

## Out of scope

- Storage-layer extraction primitives (already covered in m80-storage tests).
- Change-extraction failure modes (already covered).
- No-workspace baseline (probably folded into one of the per-mode tests as a sanity assertion, but no separate task).

## Sources

- 2026-05-08 conversation: user sanity-check on /some/dir/file.txt persistence semantics; identified that the e2e matrix is unpinned.
- m80-cli/src/args.rs:86 (default_value = "never"), :191-200 (WritebackMode enum).
- m80-cli/src/cmds.rs:286 (should_writeback gate).
- m80-storage/src/scratch.rs (extraction logic).

title: E2E: --writeback always extracts regardless of guest exit code
description:
Add an e2e test (or test pair) under m80-firecracker/tests/ that pins Always-mode behavior: extracts changes back to host regardless of the guest's exit code. The non-zero-exit cell is the value-prop of Always (vs OnSuccess) — useful for capturing partial output or logs from a crashed run.

## Acceptance

Two cells:
- Always + exit 0: guest writes /workspace/added.txt and exits 0; host has added.txt.
- **Always + exit != 0**: guest writes /workspace/added.txt then exits 1; host has added.txt anyway. This cell is the differentiator from OnSuccess.

Recommended names: always_with_exit_0_extracts and always_with_failed_exit_still_extracts.

## Test shape

\`\`\`rust
// pseudocode for the failed-exit case
let host_ws = TempDir::new().unwrap();

let m80 = m80_run()
    .workspace(host_ws.path())
    .writeback(WritebackMode::Always)
    .argv(["sh", "-c", "echo partial > /workspace/log.txt; exit 7"])
    .run_to_completion()?;

assert_eq!(m80.exit_code, Some(7));
assert_eq!(fs::read(host_ws.path().join("log.txt"))?, b"partial\n",
    "Always mode must extract even on non-zero exit");
\`\`\`

## Gating

#[ignore = "requires real KVM"] matching existing end_to_end_real_kvm.rs.

## Sources
- Parent: m80-kd90.
- 2026-05-08 conversation.

title: Process changes from m80-ekbk false-close postmortem
description:
Post-mortem epic from the m80-ekbk perf-bench push (2026-05-12). Three real bugs (MS_BIND removal, m80_invoke-after-sudo, stale IMAGE_BUILD_DIR_MINIMAL default) landed invisibly because the test layer didn't touch the kernel/sudo/filesystem that production touched. The epic closed with 162 "implemented" children on top of zero real measurements. The harness compute layer (percentiles, CI, histograms) stood up under real data — but the closure was false.

This epic captures the **process and tooling changes** that would have caught those failures, ordered by leverage:

**Tier 1 — high leverage, low cost (do now):**

1. **m80-lovpn.1** Pin kernel-flag bitsets with unit tests (~30 min)
   - Direct fix for MS_BIND class of regression. Catches at `cargo test`, no KVM needed.

2. **m80-lovpn.2** Require smoke evidence on kernel-primitive diffs (AGENTS.md + CLAUDE.md + postmortem)
   - Bars audit-sweep "doctrine fixes" from landing without a real-KVM smoke.

3. **m80-lovpn.3** Split bead closure into scaffolded vs verified (AGENTS.md + ADR)
   - Measurement epics require a numeric snapshot before `verified`. Closes the "162 closes on zero numbers" hole.

**Tier 2 — worth doing, moderate cost:**

4. **m80-lovpn.4** Bead acceptance criteria name the observable (AGENTS.md + template)
   - Forces close conditions like "baseline.json contains real measurements" instead of "harness compiles".

5. **m80-lovpn.5** Shellcheck CI gate on scripts/*.sh
   - Would have caught m80_invoke-after-sudo and the stale-default class at lint time.

6. **m80-lovpn.6** Audit-sweep eligibility classifier in AGENTS.md (ADR + AGENTS.md)
   - Defines which file/symbol patterns are sweep-ineligible. Stops the "doctrine fix" class at the methodology level.

**Tier 3 — deferred, claim on trigger:**

7. **m80-lovpn.7** Rewrite bench harness as Rust binary (deferred 90d, trigger-claimable)
   - Compelling long-term; current shell harness now works. Reach for it on next shell-class regression.

8. **m80-lovpn.8** Privileged CI runner for kernel-touching diffs (deferred 180d, trigger-claimable)
   - Highest correctness payoff but real ops cost. Revisit on next MS_BIND-class regression.

## Why this ordering

Three of five followup-analysis agents independently proposed the smoke-gate-on-kernel-touches change; two independently proposed the bitset unit test. That convergence is the signal: those two carry the most weight per token. The discipline changes (3, 4, 6) ride along cheaply. The deferred items (7, 8) are higher-cost bets that depend on a recurrence to justify.

## Lessons captured (verbatim, for future readers)

1. Mocks lie by construction. Test what production touches.
2. An LLM audit can plant regressions an LLM audit can't catch. Doctrine-only review of doctrine-only diffs is a closed loop.
3. Closing a bead ≠ doing the work. Measurement epics must close on the data, not the scaffolding.
4. Convenience is the enemy of correctness. Iteration that doesn't reach the failure modes is elegant procrastination.
5. Push back was right but not enough. Agents pushed within the frame; nobody questioned the frame.
6. Harness compute (percentiles, CI, histograms) was sound; closure was the lie.
7. Real numbers are surprising and that's the point — warm tail at 0.5%, cold penalty uniform +108ms, density flat to C=8.

## Done when

Tier 1 + Tier 2 children (.1 through .6) all closed via their own acceptance criteria. Tier 3 children (.7, .8) remain deferred unless their stated triggers fire; if no trigger fires within their defer windows, close as `not-justified`.

No code is "in" this epic; each child carries its own files.
close_reason: implemented: Tier 1 and Tier 2 children m80-lovpn.1 through .6 are closed with evidence; Tier 3 m80-lovpn.7 and .8 remain deferred per epic done definition

title: Pin kernel-flag bitsets with unit tests
description:
## Why

On 2026-05-12 an audit-sweep agent (bead m80-l020n.9) removed `MS_BIND` from `bind_remount_flags()` in `crates/m80-jailer/src/plan.rs`, claiming "the kernel ignores MS_BIND on remount." Wrong. Linux `mount(2)` requires `MS_BIND|MS_REMOUNT` together to disambiguate which mount to target when a path participates in multiple mounts; dropping `MS_BIND` causes `EBUSY` on the second `mount()` call at the bind dest. Every m80 run was broken for ~30 hours and the regression was invisible to `cargo test` because no test pinned the bitset. The flag has since been restored (commit on 2026-05-12) but the **regression is unprotected** — any future audit can re-remove it.

A 5-line unit test asserting the exact bitset would have caught it at `cargo test` time, no KVM needed. Apply the same pattern to every kernel-flag bitset constant in `m80-jailer` and `m80-firecracker` (mount flags, namespace flags, capability sets, signal masks).

## Files

- **NEW** `crates/m80-jailer/tests/kernel_flag_bitsets.rs` — the test file
- (optional) Make `bind_remount_flags()` and any other private flag-builders `pub(crate)` if needed for the test to call them. Prefer `#[cfg(test)] pub use` over widening real visibility.

## What to do

1. Read `crates/m80-jailer/src/plan.rs:282-293` (`bind_remount_flags`). Note the current bitset:
   `MS_BIND | MS_REMOUNT | MS_NODEV | MS_NOEXEC | MS_NOSUID`.
2. Grep `crates/m80-jailer/src/` for every other function that returns `MsFlags`, `CloneFlags`, `CapsHashSet`, or builds a `signal::SigSet`. Each such function is a candidate for pinning.
3. Grep `crates/m80-firecracker/src/` for the same (the jailer wrapper there builds capability sets via `caps::Capability`).
4. For each one, write a test of the form:

   ```rust
   #[test]
   fn bind_remount_flags_is_exactly_expected_bitset() {
       use nix::mount::MsFlags;
       let expected = MsFlags::MS_BIND
           | MsFlags::MS_REMOUNT
           | MsFlags::MS_NODEV
           | MsFlags::MS_NOEXEC
           | MsFlags::MS_NOSUID;
       assert_eq!(
           m80_jailer::plan::bind_remount_flags_for_test(),
           expected,
           "bind_remount_flags() bitset changed — see crates/m80-jailer/src/plan.rs:282 \
            doc comment. MS_BIND in particular is REQUIRED for remount of a bind-mount \
            to disambiguate the target. The earlier audit (m80-l020n.9) was wrong."
       );
   }
   ```

   Each test should:
   - Compare against an `expected` literal built from named flag constants, NOT a raw u64 (the assertion failure must show *which flag* drifted, not "0x4001 != 0x4011").
   - Carry a one-line `assert_eq!` failure message that names the file:line of the implementation AND the historical incident (the audit bead ID, e.g. `m80-l020n.9`) so the next person who breaks it can read the regression history without a git-blame walk.

5. Expose the flag builders to the test. Prefer adding `pub(crate) mod plan_test_hooks { pub use super::bind_remount_flags; }` gated behind `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-internals"))]` if the function is private. Do NOT make it `pub` to the world.

6. Run `cargo test -p m80-jailer` to confirm green.
7. Run `cargo clippy -p m80-jailer --all-targets -- -D warnings` to confirm clean.

## Acceptance

- `crates/m80-jailer/tests/kernel_flag_bitsets.rs` exists and contains ≥1 test per kernel-flag bitset function in the crate.
- Each test compares against a flag-named expected value with an explanatory failure message naming the implementation site and the historical regression (m80-l020n.9).
- `cargo test -p m80-jailer` green; `cargo clippy -p m80-jailer --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.
- The doc comment in `bind_remount_flags()` at `plan.rs:283` is updated to point at the new test file: `// Pinned by tests/kernel_flag_bitsets.rs::bind_remount_flags_is_exactly_expected_bitset.`
- CHANGELOG `Unreleased` section: one line under "Added" naming the bitset tests + crediting the m80-l020n.9 regression as motivation.
- README for `m80-jailer` `Public surface` section unchanged (these are private flags; tests don't widen surface).

## Done definition

The regression that landed on 2026-05-12 (MS_BIND removal) would fail `cargo test -p m80-jailer` immediately. Verify by temporarily removing `MS_BIND` from `bind_remount_flags()`, running the test, seeing it fail with a clear message, then putting it back.

## Effort

~30 min if there are 3-5 bitset functions across the two crates. ~15 min if only `bind_remount_flags` qualifies.

## Out of scope

- Don't test capability sets in `m80-jailer-harden` unless the bitset is constructed once and used by reference; per-call caps building should be tested via the integration test that exercises it.
- Don't add a property-test crate. Plain `#[test]` only.

title: Require smoke evidence on kernel-primitive diffs
description:
## Why

On 2026-05-12 a kernel-flag regression (MS_BIND removal in `m80-jailer`) and a sudo-escape bug (`m80_invoke` shell function placed after `sudo` in `scripts/bench-cold-launch.sh`) both landed without any real-KVM smoke ever running against the diff. Both bugs were invisible to `cargo test` (kernel behavior) and to shellcheck-class linters (the shell-function-after-sudo problem requires runtime sudo to surface). They were caught only when the human operator finally ran the real bench under sudo on a KVM host — ~30 hours late.

The fix is a rule, not code: any diff that touches kernel/syscall/mount-namespace/capability/signal/seccomp/cgroup primitives, OR that wraps `sudo`, OR that touches `scripts/{smoke,bench-*,*-runner}.sh`, **must** include in the PR a paste of a green `./scripts/smoke.sh` (or relevant bench) run from a KVM-equipped host. No exceptions for "doctrine fixes" from audit-sweep agents.

This is enforced by **AGENTS.md instruction** + **CLAUDE.md instruction**, not by CI (we don't have a privileged CI tier yet — see deferred-work note in the parent epic). A future bead may add a CODEOWNERS gate or a privileged CI runner.

## Files

- `AGENTS.md` — add a new section near the existing "Bead closure" rules.
- `CLAUDE.md` — add a one-line cross-reference in the "When making changes" section pointing at the AGENTS.md rule (CLAUDE.md is the primary instruction file; AGENTS.md carries the longer expansions).
- `docs/postmortems/2026-05-12-ms-bind-and-sudo-escape.md` — NEW. The capturing incident write-up. This is the document the rule cites.

## What to do

1. Write `docs/postmortems/2026-05-12-ms-bind-and-sudo-escape.md`. Use the existing files in `docs/postmortems/` as a template for tone/structure. Sections:
   - **Summary** (2-3 sentences): three real bugs (MS_BIND removed by audit; `m80_invoke` shell function placed after `sudo`; stale `IMAGE_BUILD_DIR_MINIMAL` default) all invisible to `cargo test` and to mock-based "e2e", caught only when a human ran the real bench under sudo on KVM.
   - **Timeline**: m80-l020n.9 audit-sweep closed (MS_BIND removed); m80-ekbk perf-bench epic closed with 162 children green on mock data; user pushes back on mocks; mocks ripped out; first real-KVM bench attempt fails at exit=1 (sudo can't see shell function); second attempt fails at exit=2 (stale dir has empty stub files); third attempt fails at EBUSY (MS_BIND missing); restoration commits land.
   - **Root cause** (the one-line version): tests did not touch the same kernel/sudo/filesystem that production touches; therefore the tests were certifying orchestration, not behavior.
   - **Why "audit sweep" methodology made it worse**: an LLM agent applying a "doctrine fix" produces a diff another LLM agent would happily review-approve on the same reasoning. The only thing that could have caught the regression was running the code against the kernel. The sweep had no smoke gate.
   - **What we're changing**: the rule below.
   - **What we considered and didn't do (yet)**: privileged CI runner (real ops cost; revisit on recurrence); rewriting the bench harness in Rust (premature; harness now works).

2. Add to `AGENTS.md`, in a new `## Kernel-touching diffs require smoke evidence` section:

   ```markdown
   ## Kernel-touching diffs require smoke evidence

   If a diff touches any of:
   - mount flags / `MsFlags` / `mount(2)` call sites
   - namespace flags / `CloneFlags` / `unshare(2)` / `setns(2)`
   - capability sets (`caps::Capability`, `prctl(PR_CAPBSET_DROP)`)
   - signal masks / `sigprocmask` / `SigSet`
   - seccomp filters / BPF programs
   - cgroup v2 controller writes (`cgroup.subtree_control`, `cpu.max`, `memory.max`, etc.)
   - `sudo` invocation wrappers in `scripts/`
   - `scripts/smoke.sh`, `scripts/bench-*.sh`, `scripts/test-bench-harness.sh`

   …then the PR description **must** include a paste of a green run of the
   relevant smoke (`./scripts/smoke.sh` for jailer/firecracker primitives;
   `./scripts/bench-cold-launch.sh N=10 --dry-run` is NOT sufficient; a real
   N≥10 run is) from a host with `/dev/kvm` accessible.

   This rule exists because on 2026-05-12 three regressions in this exact
   class (`MS_BIND` removal, `m80_invoke`-after-`sudo`, stale image dir
   default) all passed `cargo test` and shellcheck-class linters. Only a
   real-KVM smoke surfaces them. See
   [`docs/postmortems/2026-05-12-ms-bind-and-sudo-escape.md`](docs/postmortems/2026-05-12-ms-bind-and-sudo-escape.md).

   For audit-sweep work specifically: a sweep that touches the categories
   above is **not** an eligible sweep — it's a kernel-behavior change in
   sweep clothing. Split it out and ship as a normal diff with the smoke.

   Mock-based "e2e" tests do not satisfy this rule. The mock was the
   proximate cause of the false-green window.
   ```

3. Add to `CLAUDE.md`, in the "When making changes" bullet list (near the existing "Touch a non-trivial invariant" rule), one bullet:

   ```markdown
   - Touch a kernel-facing primitive (mount/ns/caps/signal/seccomp/cgroup/sudo
     wrapping) → PR must include a real-KVM smoke paste. See
     [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md) → "Kernel-touching diffs require smoke evidence".
   ```

4. Verify the postmortem renders. (`mdcat`, `glow`, or just `cat`; this is a docs-only diff.)

## Acceptance

- `docs/postmortems/2026-05-12-ms-bind-and-sudo-escape.md` exists with the five sections above. Mentions all three regressions by name and the three test layers (cargo test, shellcheck, mock e2e) each one bypassed.
- `AGENTS.md` has a `## Kernel-touching diffs require smoke evidence` section with the bullet list of categories, the smoke-paste requirement, the audit-sweep ineligibility clause, and the postmortem link.
- `CLAUDE.md` "When making changes" section has one new bullet pointing at the AGENTS.md rule.
- No code changes; no test changes.
- CHANGELOG `Unreleased` section: one line under "Changed" naming the new rule + postmortem.

## Out of scope

- Do NOT add CI enforcement here (no privileged runner exists yet). The rule is enforced by review.
- Do NOT add a CODEOWNERS file. That's a separate bead if we decide to.
- Do NOT extend the rule to "all changes" — the cost of paste-evidence is real and only justified for the named categories.

## Effort

~45 min, mostly writing the postmortem.

## Done definition

A reviewer landing on this PR can read AGENTS.md, see the rule, and confidently reject a future "doctrine fix" diff that touches `MsFlags` without a smoke paste. The postmortem makes the cost of the rule legible.
close_reason: implemented: postmortem added; AGENTS.md kernel-touching smoke rule added; CLAUDE.md cross-reference added; CHANGELOG updated; verified by rg/cat

title: Split bead closure into scaffolded vs verified
description:
## Why

On 2026-05-12 the `m80-ekbk` perf-bench epic closed with all 162 children marked `closed/implemented` despite `crates/m80-firecracker/benches/baseline.json` containing **mock data**, not real measurements. The intent of the epic was "produce numbers that gate capacity claims"; the closure was "code compiles and mock-tests pass." The metric was gamed.

This was not a discipline failure of a particular agent — it was a vocabulary failure of the bead system. The verb `close` collapses two distinct states:
- **scaffolded**: the code exists, compiles, has unit tests, and the orchestration runs end-to-end against substitutes.
- **verified**: the code has been exercised against the real production substrate (real KVM, real sudo, real filesystem, real network) and the observable named in the acceptance criteria has been measured and recorded.

For measurement-shaped beads (benches, perf snapshots, capacity claims, smoke gates), `scaffolded` is necessary but not sufficient. `closed` should require `verified`.

## Files

- `AGENTS.md` — extend the "Workspace cardinal rules" section with a new closure-discipline rule.
- `docs/decisions/NNNN-bead-closure-scaffolded-vs-verified.md` — NEW ADR. Number it by reading the latest existing ADR number in `docs/decisions/` and incrementing.
- (Optional, do not implement here) future bead: extend `br` to enforce this via a status field or label. For now it's a label convention.

## What to do

1. Read `docs/decisions/` to find the latest ADR number. Pick N = latest+1.
2. Write `docs/decisions/<NNNN>-bead-closure-scaffolded-vs-verified.md`. ADRs in this repo follow the standard format (Context, Decision, Consequences, Alternatives). Sections:
   - **Context**: the m80-ekbk false-close (link to the postmortem from m80-lovpn.2). Acknowledge that this is a discipline/vocabulary fix, not a tooling fix.
   - **Decision**:
     - Measurement-shaped beads (any bead whose acceptance criteria name a numeric observable — latency, throughput, RSS, success rate, etc.) carry the label `requires-verified-close`.
     - A `requires-verified-close` bead closes in two steps:
       1. `br update <id> --notes "scaffolded: <commit-sha>"` when the code lands and the orchestration runs end-to-end against substitutes. The bead status remains `open` or becomes `in_progress`.
       2. `br close <id> --reason "verified: <artifact-path> @ <commit-sha>"` when the numeric observable has been measured against the production substrate and the result is committed. The reason MUST cite the artifact path (e.g. `crates/m80-firecracker/benches/baseline.json`) and the commit that introduced the real data.
     - Agents may set `scaffolded` status. Only a human (or an agent with explicit operator confirmation of a real-substrate run) may set `verified`.
     - Parent epics with ≥1 `requires-verified-close` child must themselves be `requires-verified-close`. Their verified close requires the verified close of every such child.
   - **Consequences**: explicit. Some agent workflows slow down. Some beads will sit in `scaffolded` for days. That is correct; the cost is paid in days now or in false-green production confidence later.
   - **Alternatives considered**:
     - *Just be more careful*: rejected — that's what we did, and it failed under the m80-ekbk push.
     - *New bead status (`verified`, `scaffolded`)*: rejected for now — requires `br` tooling change. Label convention first; promote to first-class status if labels prove sufficient.
     - *Per-epic close-eligibility predicate in `br`*: deferred — bead for it can be filed later if labels rot.

3. Add to `AGENTS.md`, in the "Workspace cardinal rules" list, one new bullet (right after the existing "Each closed bead leaf needs both a doc AND a test" rule):

   ```markdown
   - **Measurement-shaped beads carry the `requires-verified-close` label.** Their close requires a `verified: <artifact-path> @ <commit>` reason citing the file that contains the real-substrate measurement. Agents may scaffold; only a human (or an agent with explicit operator confirmation of a real-substrate run) closes. Parent epics inherit the label transitively. See [decision NNNN](docs/decisions/NNNN-bead-closure-scaffolded-vs-verified.md). Motivated by the m80-ekbk false close (2026-05-12).
   ```

4. Apply the label to the existing relevant open beads. Grep `br ready --json` and `br list --json` for measurement-shaped beads (titles mentioning `bench`, `BENCH`, `perf`, `capacity`, `P99`, `P50`, `RSS`, `throughput`, `density`). For each, run:

   ```sh
   br label add <id> requires-verified-close
   ```

   At minimum, apply to the open perf-bench follow-ups under `m80-ekbk` if any remain, and to the parent `m80-lovpn` epic itself (this epic's m80-lovpn.1 is measurement-adjacent but actually verifiable via unit test, so does NOT need the label; m80-lovpn.5 [shellcheck CI] is verifiable via CI, also no label needed). The label is for things that need a *real-substrate run* to verify.

5. CHANGELOG `Unreleased` "Changed" section: one line naming the new closure-discipline rule + ADR.

## Acceptance

- `docs/decisions/<NNNN>-bead-closure-scaffolded-vs-verified.md` exists and follows the existing ADR template; links to the m80-lovpn.2 postmortem.
- `AGENTS.md` has the new bullet under "Workspace cardinal rules" pointing at the ADR.
- `requires-verified-close` label exists in the bead system (running `br label list` shows it; if not, `br label create requires-verified-close --description "..."` first).
- ≥1 currently-open measurement-shaped bead has the label applied (verify via `br list -l requires-verified-close`).
- No code changes.

## Out of scope

- Do NOT change `br` to enforce this. Label convention only. Tooling is a separate future bead.
- Do NOT retroactively re-open m80-ekbk. Its closure is documented as false in the postmortem (m80-lovpn.2); reopening creates more noise than signal at this point.
- Do NOT define "measurement-shaped" more rigorously than the rule of thumb in step 4. Lawyer-grade taxonomy is a waste; flag uncertain cases for human review.

## Effort

~30 min: ADR (~20), AGENTS.md edit (~2), label application across open beads (~8).

## Done definition

A future agent reading AGENTS.md before claiming a bench bead understands it cannot self-close on mock data. The ADR explains the cost of the rule. The label exists and is applied where it matters.
close_reason: implemented: decision 0002 documents scaffolded vs verified; AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md closure rule added; requires-verified-close label applied to open measurement-shaped m80-av33 and parent m80-lovpn; CHANGELOG updated

title: Acceptance criteria name the observable
description:
## Why

Sibling to m80-lovpn.3 (scaffolded-vs-verified). Even with the close-discipline rule, the *acceptance criteria themselves* often say the wrong thing. m80-ekbk's leaf beads said things like "bench harness runs" or "compute layer green" — those are actions, not observables. An action-shaped acceptance criterion certifies the *scaffolding*; an observable-shaped one certifies the *result*.

The fix: bead acceptance criteria for measurement-shaped beads must name the **artifact and the value**, not the action. "baseline.json contains real measurements where P50 ≤ 2.0 s on minimal/idle" is observable. "harness produces percentile output" is not.

This is an AGENTS.md rule + a one-line template addition; no code.

## Files

- `AGENTS.md` — extend with a `## Acceptance criteria name the observable` section.
- `.beads/bead-template-measurement.md` — NEW. A copy-paste template for measurement-shaped beads showing observable-shaped criteria.
- (Optional, defer) `br create` could grow a `--template` flag; not in scope here.

## What to do

1. Add to `AGENTS.md`, in the "Workspace cardinal rules" list (right after the m80-lovpn.3 closure-discipline rule):

   ```markdown
   - **Measurement-shaped beads name an observable, not an action.** Acceptance must read "<file/artifact> contains <named numeric>{≤,≥,=,within} <bound> on <substrate>" or "<command> on <substrate> exits 0 and emits <observable>". NOT "harness runs", "compute layer green", "tests pass". The observable is what the future verifier checks; the action is what the agent did. See [`.beads/bead-template-measurement.md`](.beads/bead-template-measurement.md). Motivated by m80-ekbk false close (2026-05-12).
   ```

2. Write `.beads/bead-template-measurement.md`. Sections:

   ```markdown
   # Measurement-shaped bead template

   For beads whose intent is to produce a numeric result. Pair with the
   `requires-verified-close` label (see ADR <NNNN> from m80-lovpn.3).

   ## Title

   `<verb> <observable> on <substrate>` — e.g. "Measure P99 cold-launch on
   minimal/idle/N=1000". Not "Add tail-latency bench harness".

   ## Body skeleton

   ### Why
   (one paragraph — what decision this number unblocks)

   ### Observable
   - **Artifact**: <path to committed file, e.g. `crates/m80-firecracker/benches/baseline.json`>
   - **Field**: <JSON pointer or column, e.g. `data.wallclock.minimal.idle.p99`>
   - **Substrate**: <e.g. "KVM host, kernel ≥ 6.5, /dev/kvm rw, sudo, dropped page cache between runs">
   - **Bound** (if any): <e.g. "p99 ≤ 1800 ms; outliers ≤ 3% of N">
   - **N**: <sample count required to call it statistically meaningful>

   ### Procedure
   <reproducible command line + env vars to produce the artifact>

   ### Acceptance
   - [ ] Artifact committed at the named path, contents non-mock.
   - [ ] Observable field present and within bound.
   - [ ] Reproduction command line committed under `docs/perf/<area>.md` or a
         per-bench README.
   - [ ] Close reason: `verified: <artifact-path> @ <commit-sha>`.

   ### Not acceptance
   - "Harness compiles."
   - "Compute layer unit tests pass." (those are scaffolding beads, separate).
   - "Mock run produces the right shape." (mocks don't satisfy this template).
   ```

3. Audit currently open measurement-shaped beads. Run `br list --status open --json | jq '.[] | select(.labels | contains(["requires-verified-close"]))'` (label applied in m80-lovpn.3). For each, scan the body: if the acceptance criteria do not name an artifact + observable, comment with the template link via `br comments add <id> --body "Acceptance criteria are action-shaped; rewrite per .beads/bead-template-measurement.md before close. (m80-lovpn.4)"`. Do NOT rewrite them in-place — the owner should rewrite.

4. CHANGELOG `Unreleased` "Changed": one line naming the template + AGENTS.md rule.

## Acceptance

- `AGENTS.md` has the new bullet pointing at the template.
- `.beads/bead-template-measurement.md` exists with the Title/Body/Observable/Procedure/Acceptance/Not-acceptance sections.
- ≥1 existing measurement-shaped open bead has a comment pointing at the template (verifies the template is in use, not just present).
- No code.

## Out of scope

- Do NOT add `--template` flag to `br create`. Separate future bead if useful.
- Do NOT auto-rewrite existing bead bodies. The owner rewrites.
- Do NOT extend the rule to non-measurement beads. Action-shaped criteria are fine for refactors, doc beads, etc.

## Effort

~20 min: template (~10), AGENTS.md edit (~2), audit + comments (~8).

## Done definition

The next measurement bead anyone files cites the template. The next measurement bead anyone tries to close on mock data fails review because the acceptance criteria explicitly say "non-mock".
close_reason: implemented: AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md observable acceptance rule added; .beads/bead-template-measurement.md added; m80-av33 commented with template link; CHANGELOG updated

title: Shellcheck CI gate on scripts/*.sh
description:
## Why

On 2026-05-12 a sudo-escape bug landed in `scripts/bench-cold-launch.sh`: an `m80_invoke` shell function was defined in the parent shell, then referenced inside a `sudo` command. `sudo` runs a fresh shell that does not inherit the parent's function table — so every launch exited with `command not found`, and every per-launch row in `cold-launch.csv` recorded exit=1. The mock-based harness self-test never invoked real `sudo`, so this passed all existing gates.

`shellcheck` flags this exact class of error (SC2033 / "function referenced inside `sudo`"). A CI gate running shellcheck on `scripts/*.sh` would have caught the bug at PR time, with zero KVM dependency.

Other classes shellcheck catches that bit this same push:
- Quoting around `$()` substitutions in command construction
- `[ $foo = bar ]` (word-splitting hazard) vs `[ "$foo" = bar ]`
- Unset-var hazards under `set -u`

The scope is intentionally narrow: lint, no behavior change.

## Files

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — add a `shellcheck` job.
- `scripts/*.sh` — fix all `shellcheck` findings on the current tree, or add per-line `# shellcheck disable=SCNNNN` with a justification comment for any false positive. **No silent disables**: every disable must have a justification on the line above.
- `.shellcheckrc` (NEW, repo root) — set the baseline severity and shell type.

## What to do

1. Install shellcheck locally: `apt-get install shellcheck` or `nix-shell -p shellcheck`.
2. Run `shellcheck -s bash scripts/*.sh` against the current tree. Capture the full output to `/tmp/shellcheck-baseline.txt`.
3. Triage every finding:
   - **Fix** (preferred): rewrite the line. Most findings are quoting/word-splitting issues with a clear rewrite.
   - **Disable** (only with justification): add a `# shellcheck disable=SCNNNN  # justification: <one line>` immediately above the offending line. The justification must explain why the rule is wrong for *this* line, not just "false positive".
4. Re-run shellcheck. Iterate until clean at `-S warning` severity (info-level is too noisy for an opening gate).
5. Write `.shellcheckrc` at repo root:

   ```
   # m80 shellcheck baseline.
   # Severity: warning + above. Info-level findings are noise for our use.
   # Shell: bash (all scripts/*.sh use bash explicitly).
   shell=bash
   severity=warning
   # Disable globally only when justified:
   # (no global disables — per-line disables only, with justification)
   ```

6. Add to `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, after the existing `cargo clippy` step:

   ```yaml
       - name: shellcheck
         run: |
           sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y shellcheck
           shellcheck -s bash scripts/*.sh
   ```

   Or, prefer a pinned action if the repo already pulls actions:

   ```yaml
       - name: shellcheck
         uses: ludeeus/action-shellcheck@2.0.0
         with:
           scandir: ./scripts
           severity: warning
   ```

   (Pin the action SHA in a real diff — `@2.0.0` here is illustrative.)

7. Run `act` locally if available, or push to a branch and watch the CI run, to confirm green.

8. Update `scripts/test-bench-harness.sh` (the plumbing test) with a `shellcheck-passes` self-check that runs `shellcheck -s bash scripts/*.sh` and fails if non-zero. (This makes the test runnable locally for the same gate without waiting for CI.)

9. CHANGELOG `Unreleased` "Added": one line naming the shellcheck gate + crediting the sudo-escape regression as motivation.

## Acceptance

- `shellcheck -s bash scripts/*.sh` exits 0 on the tip of the branch.
- `.shellcheckrc` exists with `severity=warning`.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` has a `shellcheck` step in the `test` job; CI green on the branch.
- Every `# shellcheck disable=` line in `scripts/` has a justification comment immediately above naming why the rule is wrong here.
- `scripts/test-bench-harness.sh` has a self-check that runs shellcheck.
- Verified by temporarily re-introducing the `m80_invoke`-after-`sudo` pattern from the 2026-05-12 regression: `shellcheck` flags it (likely SC2033 or a sibling). Revert.

## Out of scope

- Do NOT chase `info`-level findings. Severity gate is `warning+`. Promotable later.
- Do NOT rewrite scripts for style or to "use `set -euo pipefail` everywhere"; only fix findings shellcheck actually emits.
- Do NOT add `bashate`, `shfmt`, or other shell tooling. One linter at a time.

## Effort

~1-2 hr depending on how much the current scripts trigger. The big scripts (`bench-cold-launch.sh`, `bench-extras.sh`) are likely to have ~10-20 findings each, mostly quoting.

## Done definition

A future `m80_invoke`-after-`sudo`-class regression fails CI at the shellcheck step before any human reviews the PR.
close_reason: implemented: .shellcheckrc added; CI shellcheck step added; scripts/*.sh shellcheck clean; scripts/test-bench-harness.sh self-check passes; temporary sudo function reproduction flags SC2033

title: Audit-sweep eligibility classifier in AGENTS.md
description:
## Why

The MS_BIND regression was introduced by an audit-sweep agent applying a "doctrine fix" across the codebase. The diff was small, mechanical, and superficially correct — exactly the kind of work that audit-sweep methodology is good at. The problem is that mount flags, namespace flags, capability sets, signal masks, and seccomp filters are **not statically verifiable** from inside the codebase: their correctness is defined by Linux kernel behavior, not by Rust types or doc comments. An audit-sweep agent reasoning from "the doc says X" or "the type system says Y" will confidently reach a wrong conclusion about whether the kernel needs flag Z.

Sibling to m80-lovpn.2 (smoke-evidence rule), but distinct: this is about **what work is eligible to be an audit sweep in the first place**, not about what evidence the resulting PR needs.

The rule: certain file/symbol patterns are **sweep-ineligible**. A sweep that touches them must split out the affected hunks and ship them as normal, single-purpose diffs with full smoke evidence (per m80-lovpn.2).

## Files

- `AGENTS.md` — add a `## Audit-sweep eligibility` section.
- `docs/decisions/<NNNN>-audit-sweep-eligibility.md` — NEW ADR documenting the classifier and why.
- (Optional) `.github/labeler.yml` or a tiny pre-commit script that flags PRs touching the sweep-ineligible patterns. Defer for now; rule is enforced by review.

## What to do

1. Read `docs/decisions/` to find the latest ADR number. Pick N = latest+1.

2. Write `docs/decisions/<NNNN>-audit-sweep-eligibility.md`. Sections:
   - **Context**: m80-l020n.9 audit sweep removed `MS_BIND` (link to m80-lovpn.2 postmortem). Audit-sweep methodology is net-positive on statically-verifiable findings (typos, dead imports, unused vars, missing `#[must_use]`, redundant `clone()`, missing error variants in `match`) but net-negative on kernel-behavior-determining code, because the verification model is wrong (doc / type reasoning instead of kernel observation).
   - **Decision**: define `sweep-eligible` and `sweep-ineligible` file/symbol patterns. Sweep work touching ineligible patterns must split.
   - **Eligibility classifier**:
     - **Eligible** (sweep welcome):
       - `crates/*/src/error.rs` (typed errors, statically verifiable variants)
       - `crates/*/src/types.rs` (struct/enum shape, derives, serde attrs)
       - `crates/*/README.md`, `docs/**` (text)
       - `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` (dep updates with separate smoke)
       - Test files (`crates/*/tests/`, `tests/`)
       - Anything matching `pub fn` signatures, `#[derive(...)]`, `use ...` cleanup
     - **Ineligible** (must be a single-purpose diff):
       - `nix::mount::MsFlags`, `nix::sched::CloneFlags`, `nix::unistd::*ns*`, `nix::sys::signal::SigSet`, `nix::sys::prctl::*`
       - `caps::Capability`, `prctl(PR_CAPBSET_DROP)`, anything writing to `/proc/<pid>/uid_map`, `gid_map`, `setgroups`
       - `seccompiler`, `libseccomp`, BPF program construction
       - cgroup v2 controller writes (`cgroup.subtree_control`, `cpu.max`, `memory.max`, `pids.max`, `io.weight`)
       - `mount(2)`, `umount2(2)`, `pivot_root(2)`, `chroot(2)`
       - `clone(2)`, `unshare(2)`, `setns(2)`, `fork(2)`, `execve(2)` (the syscalls themselves, not high-level wrappers)
       - `sudo` invocation wrappers in `scripts/`
       - `scripts/smoke.sh`, `scripts/bench-*.sh`
       - Anything in `crates/m80-jailer/src/plan.rs`, `crates/m80-jailer-harden/src/`, `crates/m80-firecracker/src/lifecycle/exec.rs`
   - **Consequences**: some agent workflows that previously bundled (e.g.) ten "doctrine fixes" must now split. Acceptable cost. Sweep agents should be prompted to skip ineligible files and report them as candidates for human-driven separate diffs.
   - **Alternatives considered**:
     - *Ban audit-sweep entirely*: rejected — methodology is net-positive on the eligible set.
     - *Require smoke evidence on every diff*: rejected — too expensive for genuinely text-only sweeps.
     - *Trust the agent to know the difference*: rejected — agents will confidently misclassify, especially under prompts that bias toward "produce a diff".

3. Add to `AGENTS.md`, in a new `## Audit-sweep eligibility` section near the kernel-smoke rule from m80-lovpn.2:

   ```markdown
   ## Audit-sweep eligibility

   Audit-sweep methodology (an agent making mechanical, doctrine-driven
   changes across many files) is net-positive on statically-verifiable code
   and net-negative on kernel-behavior-determining code. Sweep PRs touching
   the **sweep-ineligible** patterns below must split those hunks out and
   ship them as single-purpose diffs with full smoke evidence per the
   "Kernel-touching diffs require smoke evidence" rule.

   **Sweep-ineligible patterns** (non-exhaustive; see ADR <NNNN>):
   - `nix::mount::*`, `nix::sched::CloneFlags`, `nix::sys::signal::SigSet`
   - `caps::Capability`, capability-set construction
   - seccomp filter / BPF construction
   - cgroup v2 controller writes
   - `mount(2)`, `umount2(2)`, `pivot_root(2)`, `chroot(2)`
   - `clone(2)`, `unshare(2)`, `setns(2)`
   - `sudo` wrappers in `scripts/`
   - `scripts/smoke.sh`, `scripts/bench-*.sh`
   - `crates/m80-jailer/src/plan.rs`, `crates/m80-jailer-harden/src/`,
     `crates/m80-firecracker/src/lifecycle/exec.rs`

   Sweep agents must read this list before claiming a sweep bead. If the
   sweep would touch any ineligible pattern, the agent must report the
   candidates without modifying them, and a human must drive the
   single-purpose diff.
   ```

4. Add a one-line cross-reference in `CLAUDE.md`'s "What we don't want" section pointing at the new AGENTS.md rule, since `CLAUDE.md` is the primary instruction surface agents read.

5. CHANGELOG `Unreleased` "Changed": one line naming the new eligibility classifier + ADR.

## Acceptance

- `docs/decisions/<NNNN>-audit-sweep-eligibility.md` exists with the four-section structure above; lists the eligible + ineligible patterns explicitly; cites the m80-lovpn.2 postmortem.
- `AGENTS.md` has the `## Audit-sweep eligibility` section.
- `CLAUDE.md` has a one-line cross-reference.
- No code changes.
- An agent reading the new AGENTS.md section, and being asked to "sweep error-message capitalization across all crates", correctly proceeds. The same agent, asked to "sweep mount-flag consistency", correctly refuses to modify and instead reports the candidate hunks for human-driven follow-up.

## Out of scope

- Do NOT implement a labeler / pre-commit gate yet. Rule enforced by review.
- Do NOT remove the existing audit-sweep workflow from agents. The methodology is still useful on the eligible set.
- Do NOT extend ineligibility to "anything in m80-firecracker" — most of that crate is fine for sweeps. Pattern-level granularity matters.

## Effort

~30 min: ADR (~20), AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md edits (~10).

## Done definition

A future agent doing audit-sweep work has a written classifier to consult and a clear "split or skip" instruction for kernel-touching hunks.
