title: Rewrite bench harness as Rust binary (deferred)
description:
## Why (and why deferred)

On 2026-05-12 a sudo-escape bug (`m80_invoke` shell function placed after `sudo`) landed in `scripts/bench-cold-launch.sh` invisibly. Sibling bugs (stale env-var default, mock contamination of CSV outputs) also lived in the shell layer. Bash is the wrong language for the bench harness:

1. No type system → arg-passing bugs surface at runtime, often only under sudo.
2. No `argparse`-grade flag handling → `--cold-isolation` and friends grew ad-hoc and are tested by string-matching help output.
3. Sudo-traversal-of-shell-functions is a structural footgun bash cannot lint away.
4. JSON output requires `python3 scripts/bench-summary.py` shelling out — the data ownership boundary is awkward.

A Rust bench binary (a `xtask`-style crate, `cargo run -p m80-bench --` or a `bench` subcommand on the `m80` CLI) would:
- Carry typed args + `clap` help.
- Manage `sudo` invocation via `Command::new("sudo").arg("--").arg(...)` with no shell interpolation.
- Emit JSON snapshots natively; eliminate the bash+python boundary.
- Be `cargo test`-able with proper unit + integration coverage.
- Run under `RUST_LOG=trace` for diagnostics.

**Status: deferred.** The current shell harness now works (real N=200 cold-cold + density data committed 2026-05-12 in commit 3455d73). The shellcheck gate (m80-lovpn.5) catches the proximate class of bug. Rewriting in Rust is a ~3-day push with no immediate observable gain. The right trigger to reach for this bead is "we hit a second sudo-escape-class bug that shellcheck failed to catch" or "the shell harness has grown a new sub-mode that's too complex to test from outside."

## When to claim this bead

Claim only when **one** of the following triggers fires:
- A new bash regression in `scripts/bench-*.sh` lands that shellcheck (m80-lovpn.5) did not catch.
- The bench harness grows a feature that's painful to express in bash (a real concurrency primitive, structured retries, in-process log parsing).
- A new measurement need (e.g. per-syscall tracing integration, eBPF probe attach) requires the harness to interleave Rust libraries.

If none of those have fired in 90 days, close this bead with reason `not-justified: shell harness held up; revisit if a trigger surfaces`.

## Files (when claimed)

- `crates/m80-bench/` — NEW workspace member.
  - `crates/m80-bench/Cargo.toml`
  - `crates/m80-bench/src/main.rs` — clap-based CLI entry
  - `crates/m80-bench/src/cells.rs` — per-cell loop (`KIND × LOAD × KERNEL_KIND`)
  - `crates/m80-bench/src/launch.rs` — wraps `Command::new("sudo")` to invoke the `m80` binary; captures phase events
  - `crates/m80-bench/src/snapshot.rs` — JSON snapshot emitter (replaces `bench-summary.py`'s output role)
  - `crates/m80-bench/src/stats.rs` — percentile / bootstrap-CI / histogram math (port from `scripts/bench-summary.py`)
  - `crates/m80-bench/tests/` — unit + integration
  - `crates/m80-bench/README.md`
- `Cargo.toml` (workspace) — add `crates/m80-bench` to `members`.
- `scripts/bench-cold-launch.sh` — DELETE.
- `scripts/bench-extras.sh` — DELETE or keep as a `m80-bench --extras` invoker.
- `scripts/bench-summary.py` — DELETE.
- `scripts/test-bench-harness.sh` — DELETE.
- `docs/perf/bench-harness.md` — rewrite to document the Rust binary's CLI.

## Design notes (when claimed)

- **Sudo strategy**: the binary itself runs unprivileged. It shells out to `sudo -n target/release/m80 run ...` for each launch. The `-n` (non-interactive) flag ensures any sudo failure surfaces as a typed error rather than a hung TTY. The agent that claims this bead must read the existing `scripts/bench-cold-launch.sh` lines around the `TASKSET_PREFIX` array to understand the current sudo pattern.
- **Phase event ingestion**: m80 already emits per-phase events when `M80_PHASE_TRACE=1` is set. Parse them from stderr into typed `PhaseEvent` records and write to a `phases.csv` plus optional `PHASE_JSONL=` stream — keep the on-disk format compatible with the existing snapshot diff infrastructure so historical baselines remain comparable.
- **Snapshot compatibility**: `crates/m80-firecracker/benches/baseline.json` is a v1 schema. Either preserve v1 exactly, or bump to v2 and write a one-time migrator. Prefer preserve — historical regression-gate runs depend on the schema.
- **Concurrency**: use `std::thread::scope` and `Command::spawn`; do not pull in tokio. The benches are wallclock-bound, not IO-bound; async buys nothing.
- **Output**: stdout = human-readable summary; stderr = diagnostics; `--json` flag for machine output. `--dry-run` prints the plan.

## Acceptance (when claimed)

- `cargo run -p m80-bench -- --dry-run` prints the same cells the current shell harness plans.
- `sudo cargo run -p m80-bench -- N=10 SKIP_LOADED=1` produces the same CSV columns + a `latest.json` snapshot byte-comparable in *shape* to the current bash+python output (numeric values will differ run-to-run).
- `python3 scripts/bench-summary.py diff baseline.json latest.json` still works against the new snapshot (preserving v1 schema) — OR a new `m80-bench diff` subcommand replaces it.
- All shell scripts and the Python helper deleted.
- `docs/perf/bench-harness.md` updated.
- Real-KVM smoke evidence in PR (per m80-lovpn.2 rule).

## Out of scope

- Do NOT build this until a trigger fires.
- Do NOT rewrite the *compute* layer; port it. The percentile / bootstrap-CI / histogram math in `scripts/bench-summary.py` is correct and unit-tested; treat it as a port, not a redesign.
- Do NOT add an interactive TUI. Plain stdout.

## Effort (when claimed)

~3 days. Rough split: 1d port stats + snapshot emitters, 1d port launch loop + sudo handling, 1d port sweep/concurrent/cold-isolation modes + delete shell scripts + docs.

## Done definition

Either: a working Rust replacement that passes all of the above, with the shell harness deleted; or this bead closed with `not-justified` reason after 90 days of stable shell-harness operation.

title: Privileged CI runner for kernel-touching diffs (deferred)
description:
## Why (and why deferred)

Three of five followup-analysis agents on 2026-05-13 independently proposed building a privileged CI runner with `/dev/kvm` access so that every PR touching kernel/jailer/firecracker code runs `./scripts/smoke.sh` automatically. That's the highest correctness payoff available — it converts m80-lovpn.2 (the "smoke evidence required" rule) from a review-time check into a CI gate, eliminating the human-attention dependency.

The reason it's deferred: real ops cost. A privileged self-hosted GitHub Actions runner needs:
- A physical or VM host with KVM access (most cloud CI lacks this; the GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-latest` runner is itself a VM with no nested-virt).
- Sudo, image build artifacts (~1-2 GB), kernel + rootfs caching for fast turnaround.
- Network access to pull firecracker, kvm-unit-tests, etc.
- Runner-secret management (the runner token, image-cache signing key if used).
- Operational maintenance: a runner that's down silently stops gating PRs, which is worse than no gate (false confidence). Requires uptime monitoring.

**Status: deferred.** Trigger to claim: a second `MS_BIND`-class regression lands despite m80-lovpn.1 (bitset tests) + m80-lovpn.2 (smoke-evidence rule) + m80-lovpn.5 (shellcheck). The current set of three changes is expected to catch the same class via review and unit tests. If they prove insufficient, the cost-benefit of a privileged runner flips.

## When to claim this bead

Claim if **any** of:
- A regression of the same shape as MS_BIND, m80_invoke-after-sudo, or stale-default lands invisibly despite m80-lovpn.1, .2, .5 being in force.
- An external (non-team) contributor opens a PR touching `m80-jailer` or `m80-firecracker`. The review-based smoke-evidence rule does not scale to drive-by PRs; a privileged CI gate would.
- Headcount on the project grows past ~3 active contributors. Review-bandwidth scaling makes manual smoke pasting expensive.

If no trigger fires in 180 days, close with `not-justified: review-based smoke gate held up`.

## Files (when claimed)

- `.github/workflows/privileged-smoke.yml` — NEW. Triggers on PR to `main` when paths matching the m80-lovpn.6 ineligibility classifier are touched.
- `docs/ops/privileged-runner.md` — NEW. How to provision a fresh runner, what's on it, how to rotate the runner token, how to monitor it.
- `scripts/ci-smoke.sh` — NEW. Wrapper around `scripts/smoke.sh` that the CI workflow invokes. Adds:
  - artifact cache priming (kernel, rootfs)
  - artifact upload of phase JSONL on failure
  - clear pass/fail summary to GitHub Actions step summary
- `crates/m80-firecracker/benches/baseline.json` — CI may diff against this; ensure the regression gate runs on the privileged runner too.

## Provisioning checklist (when claimed)

1. Choose host: bare-metal Linux with `/dev/kvm`. Recommended: dedicated, not shared with developer machines. Spec: ≥8 cores, ≥16 GB RAM, ≥100 GB SSD.
2. Install: GitHub Actions runner, `firecracker`, `jailer`, `qemu-system-x86_64` (for `kvm-ok` checks), `cgroup-tools`, the m80 build deps from `crates/m80-firecracker/README.md`.
3. Pre-build the m80 binary into a known location; CI uses a release build per PR but seeds from cache.
4. Seed the image cache at `/var/cache/m80-ci/images/` with the rootfs + kernel from `m80-image-build`.
5. Configure the runner with labels `self-hosted, linux, kvm`. The workflow targets `runs-on: [self-hosted, linux, kvm]`.
6. Set up Prometheus / heartbeat ping or a daily cron sanity check to alert on runner downtime. (A silent runner is the failure mode.)

## Workflow shape (when claimed)

```yaml
name: privileged-smoke

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - 'crates/m80-jailer/**'
      - 'crates/m80-jailer-harden/**'
      - 'crates/m80-firecracker/src/lifecycle/**'
      - 'crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch.rs'
      - 'scripts/smoke.sh'
      - 'scripts/bench-cold-launch.sh'
      - 'scripts/bench-extras.sh'

jobs:
  smoke:
    runs-on: [self-hosted, linux, kvm]
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: kvm sanity
        run: |
          test -r /dev/kvm && test -w /dev/kvm
          kvm-ok || true
      - name: cargo build --release -p m80-cli
        run: cargo build --release -p m80-cli
      - name: scripts/ci-smoke.sh
        run: ./scripts/ci-smoke.sh
      - name: upload phase trace on failure
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: phase-trace
          path: /tmp/m80-ci-phase-*.jsonl
```

## Operational rules (when claimed)

- The runner runs **only** the smoke workflow. Do not allow arbitrary CI workloads on the privileged host (untrusted PR code can read `/dev/kvm` and escape).
- Forks: do not run on PRs from forks unless explicitly approved (`pull_request_target` is dangerous; use `pull_request` + label-gating + an explicit approval action).
- The smoke must run **after** a maintainer's manual approval for fork PRs. Internal PRs run automatically.
- Heartbeat: a daily cron job pings the runner and fails CI on the main branch if the runner is offline >24h. Otherwise the privileged-smoke workflow silently stops gating and we are back to the m80-ekbk failure mode.

## Acceptance (when claimed)

- A PR touching `crates/m80-jailer/src/plan.rs` automatically triggers the privileged-smoke workflow and the workflow runs `scripts/smoke.sh` end-to-end.
- A PR not touching any of the path-filtered files does NOT trigger the workflow (cost discipline).
- `docs/ops/privileged-runner.md` exists with provisioning + rotation + monitoring procedures.
- Heartbeat monitoring is live: a deliberately-broken runner causes main-branch CI to fail within 24h.
- A test PR with the 2026-05-12 MS_BIND removal pattern is rejected by the privileged-smoke step (validates the gate catches the historical regression).
- CHANGELOG `Unreleased` "Added": one line crediting the privileged-smoke runner + linking the postmortem.

## Out of scope

- Do NOT build this until a trigger fires.
- Do NOT use a cloud-hosted nested-virt runner (the latency and cost are wrong vs. a dedicated bare-metal host).
- Do NOT extend the gate to "every PR" — path filtering is essential for cost discipline.

## Effort (when claimed)

~2-3 days first-time setup (host provisioning is the long pole), ~1 day/quarter ongoing maintenance. Budget for ~4 hours/month of unexpected runner-down incidents based on community baselines for self-hosted runners.

## Done definition

A future MS_BIND-class regression cannot land on main without passing a real-KVM smoke. Heartbeat monitoring ensures the gate doesn't silently fail open.

title: CLI process facade, end-to-end harness, and warm-pool surface
description:
Purpose: make crates/m80-cli expose m80 as a transparent process wrapper: run this command with a constrained view of the host filesystem, environment, runtime image, and network. The VM is an implementation detail that provides isolation; the primary user model is process-transparent and environment-explicit.

Headline contract: `m80 run [visibility/effect/world options] -- <program> [args...]` forwards guest stdout to host stdout, guest stderr to host stderr, and returns the guest process exit code. m80 wrapper failures are separate: they render on stderr and return stable m80 exit codes.

Supported command families:
- `run` — the front door: one process with explicit visibility/effect/world policy, selected guest image/profile, pipe streaming, and optional PTY mode.
- `preflight`, `config show`, `version` — host/config/artifact introspection.
- `list`, `inspect`, `cleanup` — preserved run-root/debug surfaces, not the happy path.
- `warm ...` — explicit warm-owner control surface after the lifetime design proves how a resident owner is created, observed, drained, and stopped.

Non-goals: no Docker-like lifecycle UX as the primary model, no hidden daemon, no agent tool catalog, no backward-compatible aliases for renamed commands. Out-of-process live exec/snapshot/pool IPC must be explicit beads, not accidental side effects of the CLI refactor. Interactive support lives only through the `m80 run --tty` lane; m80 does not grow a separate shell/container lifecycle product.

Acceptance: every child closes with docs + tests; the primary ignored KVM e2e proves `m80 run` passthrough semantics; streaming and PTY lanes cover long-running and TUI workloads without stdout/stderr contract drift; warm-pool beads define what a warm VM is doing and how CLI users create/observe/drain ready slots; README/help text teach "run a process with a constrained view" rather than "manage a VM".
notes: closed child sequence covers command hard cutover, config/preflight fixtures, JSON/exit errors, run-root list/inspect/cleanup, KVM passthrough, visibility/effects, egress policy, streaming, cancellation, PTY/TUI, warm owner lifecycle, warm streaming, and CLI smoke harness. Verification includes cargo test -p m80-cli --tests; cargo test -p m80-firecracker --lib --tests; ./scripts/smoke-cli.sh; cargo fmt --all --check; git diff --check

title: CLI process-wrapper command contract hard cutover
description:
Decide and pin the v0.1/v0.2 CLI command vocabulary against the new mental model: m80 runs a process with a constrained view of the host. Resolve the current launch/run/list/ls mismatch with a hard cutover: no alias shim, no compatibility wrapper.

Proposed command set to validate and then bake into docs/tests:

- `m80 run [OPTIONS] -- <program> [args...]` — primary command. Process-transparent stdout/stderr/exit-code in pipe mode. Options describe visibility/effect/world policy, not VM mechanics: `--profile <name>` or the selected image/profile override, `--workspace <dir>`, `--cwd <path>`, `--env KEY=VAL`, `--stdin`, `--egress none|outbound`, optional `--allow-host` / `--allow-cidr` only if the egress-policy bead accepts that surface, `--scratch-size <size>`, `--writeback never|on-success|always`, `--keep-on-failure`, and sizing knobs only where still necessary.
- Runtime availability is explicit: the requested program must exist in the selected guest image/profile or in the visible workspace. m80 does not execute host binaries, pull OCI images, or install packages implicitly.
- `m80 run --tty` / `-t` / `-i` shape is reserved for the interactive PTY lane. PTY mode has a different I/O contract: terminal byte stream, no stdout/stderr separation, host terminal resize/signals forwarded.
- CLI egress default must be decided explicitly. Product hypothesis: for the transparent host-process feel, `m80 run` defaults to outbound egress where host preflight can support it, with `--egress none` as the lockdown mode. The lower-level library may still default to NoEgress; the CLI facade is allowed to choose a different user-facing default if docs/tests pin it.
- `m80 preflight` — host capability/artifact check.
- `m80 config show` — merged config, source labels, and effective runtime profile/artifact identity.
- `m80 list`, `m80 inspect <id>`, `m80 cleanup` — preserved sandbox/run-root debug/admin commands.
- `m80 warm ...` — reserved command family for explicit warm-owner control; exact verbs are gated by the warm-lifetime CLI design bead.
- `m80 version`.

Commands that make the VM the product (`launch`, out-of-process `exec`, foreground `stop`, snapshot capture) are not the front door. If retained temporarily, they must be documented as feature-gap/debug surfaces with tests; otherwise remove them in the same hard cutover.

Acceptance:
- crates/m80-cli/README.md and docs/behaviors/cli/command-surface.md describe exactly the supported commands, flags, JSON modes, runtime profile selection, and explicit stubs.
- Top-level help says "run a process with a constrained view of the host" or equivalent; it does not lead with VM lifecycle management.
- Clap argv tests cover every documented command and reject removed/unsupported aliases.
- m80-cli help smoke tests include top-level help and every supported subcommand help.
- Notes at close name the chosen headline command, the CLI egress default, the final warm verbs if any, the PTY flag shape, the runtime profile flag shape, and any deferred v0.2 commands.

title: CLI warm owner enable/status/drain and run --warm e2e
description:
Implement the CLI warm surface after m80-lt15.9 locks the command design. This is the first point where the CLI may need explicit IPC/residency; keep that ownership visible and intentional.

Expected shape if design confirms it:
- `m80 warm enable --size <n> ...` starts or enables the resident warm owner, creates/loads the clean snapshot, restores slots to Ready, and refills after leases. If a foreground/dev mode exists, it is explicit.
- `m80 warm status` reports target_ready/ready/filling/leased/discarded/last_error and profile identity in human and JSON forms.
- `m80 warm drain` stops accepting new leases and tears down ready slots.
- `m80 warm disable` stops/removes the resident owner.
- `m80 run --warm -- <cmd>` leases a ready slot, execs the command, forwards stdout/stderr/exit exactly like cold `m80 run`, then releases/discards/refills according to warm-pool reset evidence.

Acceptance:
- No hidden daemon: tests and docs show how the resident warm owner is started and stopped. If systemd/user-service supervision is supported, it is a wrapper around the documented owner command, not a separate secret m80d contract.
- `m80 run --warm` against no owner or empty owner fails with a clear warm-unavailable/PoolEmpty exit and does not cold boot.
- `m80 run --warm --workspace ...` fails clearly unless the design bead delivered attach-late workspace support.
- Ignored KVM e2e proves a prefilled warm owner serves a command with unchanged stdout/stderr/exit semantics and then refills or reports discard explicitly.
- docs/behaviors/cli/warm-lifetime.md links to the KVM test and to docs/behaviors/lifecycle/warm-pool.md.

title: CLI egress default and visibility policy
description:
Settle the CLI-level egress default for the process-wrapper model. The lower-level library can remain conservative, but the CLI needs a user-facing rule that matches the promise "run this process with a constrained view of the host".

Product hypothesis to test and either accept or reject: `m80 run` defaults to outbound egress because host processes usually have outbound egress; callers opt into lockdown with `--egress none`. If outbound setup is unavailable, wrapper failure is explicit and points at `m80 preflight` / config.

Scope:
- Decide defaults for `m80 run` pipe mode and `m80 run --tty` interactive mode.
- Define aliases/values: prefer `--egress outbound|none` over VM-ish `--network noegress|outbound`; hard cutover if names change.
- Define whether hostname/CIDR allowlist flags are part of this surface now or deferred to the DNS-name allowlist bead.
- Define how config/env can override the default without surprising scripts.
- Verify `m80 run --egress none` does not create tap/bridge/NAT and `--egress outbound` does.

Acceptance:
- docs/behaviors/cli/egress-policy.md states the default and rationale.
- crates/m80-cli/README.md and help text use `egress` / world-visibility vocabulary, not VM network vocabulary.
- CLI parse tests pin the default and reject legacy/ambiguous spellings if removed.
- KVM or fixture tests prove the selected policy reaches `SandboxConfig::network`.
- If default outbound is rejected, the bead records why and the exact alternative default.

title: DESIGN: interactive PTY run contract
description:
Design interactive process mode for TUIs such as Claude Code. This is still generic m80 scope: run one process with constrained filesystem/env/network visibility, but attached to a terminal instead of pipe-captured stdout/stderr.

Questions to lock:
- Flag shape: `m80 run --tty --stdin -- <cmd>` vs Docker-like `-it`; decide exact spelling.
- I/O contract: PTY mode has one terminal byte stream; stdout/stderr are not separable and `--json` is incompatible or limited to pre/post metadata on stderr.
- Terminal setup: host raw mode, restoration on panic/error, `TERM`/locale propagation, terminal size propagation, SIGWINCH forwarding.
- Signal semantics: Ctrl-C/Ctrl-D pass to the guest process through the PTY; wrapper-level cancellation needs an escape hatch or documented behavior.

title: Guest exec cancellation kills process groups, not only direct child
description:
Tighten the process-wrapper cancellation contract at the guest boundary. The streaming implementation can kill the immediate child, but shell/TUI workloads can spawn grandchildren that keep stdout/stderr/PTY fds open or continue running after the wrapper is cancelled. m80 run must behave like a constrained process wrapper: cancellation, timeout, host disconnect, and PTY teardown stop the whole requested process tree.

Scope:
- guestd starts pipe-mode execs in an isolated process group or session before running the requested program.
- PTY mode consumes the same process-group/session rule when its runner lands; it must not invent separate child-only cancellation semantics.
- Cancel, timeout, host disconnect, and wrapper signal paths send the chosen signal to the group/session, then use a bounded SIGKILL fallback before returning to the accept loop.
- guestd reaps the direct child and prevents zombies; tests must prove shell-spawned descendants do not keep stdout/stderr or terminal fds open after cancellation.
- Keep the surface generic: no agent/tool semantics and no compatibility shim.

Acceptance:
- docs/behaviors/cli/signal-cancellation.md and the m80-guestd README state process-group/session semantics, escalation order, timeout, and diagnostics.
- guestd tests cover direct child, /bin/sh-spawned grandchild, timeout, host disconnect/read EOF, and explicit CancelRequest.
- An ignored KVM or PTY follow-up test proves a shell-spawned sleeper does not survive wrapper cancellation and the next exec can run.
- Existing streaming exec tests still pass and no stdout/stderr metadata is emitted by the wrapper.

title: CLI warm lifetime semantics and command design
description:
Define the CLI meaning of warm execution before implementation. A warm VM is not a user session and not a hidden Docker container. It is a pre-restored, guestd-ready blank slot owned by an explicit resident warm owner, waiting to lease exactly one process run.

Design questions to settle:
- User-facing command family should prefer `m80 warm ...` over `m80 pool ...` unless the design finds a better name. Proposed: `m80 warm enable --size <n>` (install/start resident owner), `m80 warm status`, `m80 warm drain`, `m80 warm disable`, and `m80 run --warm -- <cmd>`.
- Lifetime owner: system service, user service, or foreground/dev mode. No hidden daemon: the owner must be visible, inspectable, and intentionally enabled.
- Does warm enable create the clean snapshot if absent, or require an explicit prepare step? Prefer a single understandable flow if it remains auditable.
- What visibility profiles are eligible for warm slots? Current `WarmPool` rejects workspace-backed pools, so `m80 run --workspace ... --warm` must either fail clearly or depend on a later attach-late workspace design. No silent cold fallback.
- Warm profile identity must include the exact selected image/profile: kernel sha, rootfs/base sha, manifest identity, image_kind, overlay template identity, egress policy, mem/vcpu, no-workspace status, and any env/secret/terminal constraints that affect a ready slot's validity.
- How are warm-empty and warm-owner-unavailable reported? Use `FcError::PoolEmpty` / exit 8 or a dedicated wrapper error; do not cold boot unless a future explicit `--cold-fallback` bead adds it.

Acceptance:
- docs/behaviors/cli/warm-lifetime.md states what a warm VM is doing while idle: restored from clean snapshot, guestd listening, no user process running, no workspace attached, ready_probe already passed, waiting in the resident owner.
- crates/m80-cli/README.md documents final warm verbs and their v0.1/v0.2 status.
- The command contract bead m80-lt15.1 is updated if this design changes top-level help.
- Dependency on `docs/behaviors/lifecycle/warm-pool.md` is acknowledged; CLI docs do not redefine reset evidence.
- The design states what happens across owner crash, binary/artifact/profile upgrade, idle timeout, explicit drain, and incompatible `m80 run --warm` policy.

title: E2E EgressMode × isolation matrix
description:
m80 has 3 EgressMode variants (None / Outbound / JoinNetns) with strong user-facing isolation promises. Today's e2e coverage is structural-only:
- NoEgress is the *only* mode used by the 5 main e2e tests, but none verify that a guest under NoEgress *actually fails* to reach external IPs.
- AllowOutbound has zero e2e — no test confirms the guest can reach external addresses or that DNS resolves.
- JoinNetns has structural verification (FC PID lands in the namespace via /proc/<pid>/ns/net) but not functional (no test that guest traffic routes through the netns).

Same writeback-shape gap: typed enum, unit tests pass, behavior unpinned.

## Children
3 child tasks, one per mode. Each verifies the mode's actual user-visible promise via a minimal real-KVM e2e.

## Acceptance for the umbrella
- 3 new test functions under crates/m80-firecracker/tests/.
- #[ignore = "requires real KVM"] gating matches existing pattern.
- A regression that inverts isolation (e.g., NoEgress accidentally allowing traffic) fails a named test.

- 2026-05-08 conversation; survey of e2e gaps after the writeback discovery.
- crates/m80-cli/src/args.rs (EgressMode enum).
- crates/m80-firecracker/tests/end_to_end_real_kvm.rs (existing e2e baseline).

title: Guest PID1 configures outbound NIC without systemd
description:
m80-net-outbound's guest config injection writes systemd-networkd/resolved files into a supplied runtime rootfs image. That assumption no longer matches current m80 images: Ubuntu and Minimal both boot m80-guestd as PID 1, Minimal has no systemd, and the writable overlay is mounted at /upper/root after PID1 starts. To make AllowOutbound work, guestd PID1 needs a direct NIC/DNS configuration path for the Firecracker virtio-net device.

Acceptance:
- m80-guestd PID1 reads a bounded host-provided network config source (kernel cmdline, mounted config drive/file, or existing rootfs marker) containing interface MAC/IP/prefix/gateway/DNS.
- PID1 configures eth0 directly using kernel interfaces available in Minimal (prefer rtnetlink via a small Rust implementation or proven crate; no shelling to ip/ifconfig).
- DNS config works for guest execs under Minimal and Ubuntu PID1 images.
- m80-net-outbound no longer relies on systemd-networkd/resolved injection for the current image kinds, or the old injection is explicitly kept only for a future systemd image mode.
- tests cover rendered/config-parsed network settings and an ignored real-KVM outbound DNS/connectivity path can consume it.
- docs/behaviors/network-outbound-nat/injection.md is updated to reflect the PID1 configuration mechanism.

title: exec.rs cancel forwarder thread joined on Drop with no timeout
description:
site: crates/m80-firecracker/src/lifecycle/exec.rs (`_cancel_forwarder` thread)
finder: trim-the-fat r5 correctness review

Problem: The cancel forwarder thread is joined only when `_cancel_forwarder` is dropped at function exit. The join has NO timeout. If the forwarder is stuck on a slow vsock send (e.g., guest unresponsive), the calling exec function blocks indefinitely on Drop.

Fix: bounded join (50-100ms) with log-on-timeout, then detach. Or: add an explicit cancel-of-cancel-forwarder mechanism that runs before Drop.
notes: implemented bounded Drop join for same-connection cancel forwarder; helper signals completion through done channel, Drop waits 100 ms then logs/detaches instead of blocking indefinitely. Applied same bounded helper to PTY event forwarder because it had the same join-on-drop shape. doc=crates/m80-firecracker/README.md cancellation contract. test=crates/m80-firecracker/src/lifecycle/exec.rs::tests::cancel_forwarder_drop_detaches_after_join_timeout. verification: cargo test -p m80-firecracker cancel_forwarder_drop_detaches_after_join_timeout -- --nocapture; cargo test -p m80-firecracker --lib; cargo clippy -p m80-firecracker --all-targets -- -D warnings; git diff --check.

title: guestd pty.rs join_output_thread.expect() crashes event loop on output-thread panic
description:
site: crates/m80-guestd/src/connection/pty.rs:33 (inside abort_pty! macro)
finder: trim-the-fat r5

Problem: `join_output_thread(...).expect("pty output thread panicked")` propagates a panic from a worker thread up through the abort_pty! macro into the connection event loop. A single PTY output-thread panic crashes the entire guestd handler.

Fix: replace `.expect(...)` with match-on-result + `tracing::error!` log; gracefully terminate the connection without panicking the loop. Mirror the cancel-forwarder fix from bead m80-n40s pattern.

title: Admission: vm_id × run_root × fc_basename path budget check
description:
Backend admission must reject configurations whose constructed AF_UNIX socket path would exceed the kernel's 107-byte usable cap (sun_path = 108 bytes including null terminator). Currently the failure surfaces as an opaque IO error at bind() time, deep inside launch — far from where the bad input was accepted.

## Structural fix

In `crates/m80-firecracker/src/backend.rs::admit()` (or wherever the SandboxConfig is finalized), compute:

```rust
const SUN_PATH_BUDGET: usize = 107;

fn check_path_budget(run_root: &Path, vm_id: &str, fc_basename: &str) -> Result<(), ConfigError> {
    // <run_root>/<vm_id>/<fc_basename>/<vm_id>/root/firecracker.sock
    let path_len = run_root.as_os_str().len()
        + 1 + vm_id.len()              // /<vm_id>
        + 1 + fc_basename.len()        // /<fc_basename>
        + 1 + vm_id.len()              // /<vm_id>
        + "/root/".len()
        + "firecracker.sock".len();
    if path_len > SUN_PATH_BUDGET {
        return Err(ConfigError::VmIdPathBudgetExceeded {
            run_root: run_root.to_path_buf(),
            vm_id: vm_id.to_owned(),
            fc_basename: fc_basename.to_owned(),
            path_len,
            budget: SUN_PATH_BUDGET,
        });
    }
    Ok(())
}
```

`fc_basename` is `firecracker_bin.file_name()`. vsock.sock and firecracker.sock are the same length (16 bytes) so checking firecracker.sock covers both.

## Files

- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/error.rs` — add `ConfigError::VmIdPathBudgetExceeded { run_root, vm_id, fc_basename, path_len, budget }`
- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/backend.rs` — call `check_path_budget` from `admit()`
- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/layout.rs` — expose `SUN_PATH_BUDGET` and a `compute_socket_path_len(...)` helper for reuse
- `crates/m80-cli/src/errors.rs` — extend `exit_code_for` and `variant_name` with the new variant

## Acceptance

- doc at `docs/behaviors/admission/vm-id-path-budget.md` (path layout + cap derivation + worked example)
- test `crates/m80-firecracker/tests/path_budget.rs`:
  - `vm_id_within_budget_admits_cleanly` — 24-char vm_id with `/var/lib/m80-run` admits
  - `vm_id_at_budget_admits_cleanly` — exact-fit case admits (path_len == 107)
  - `vm_id_over_budget_returns_typed_error` — 28-char vm_id with `/var/lib/m80-run` returns `ConfigError::VmIdPathBudgetExceeded` with all three components named
  - `long_fc_basename_subtracted_from_budget` — fake firecracker name eats into the budget; test verifies the helper accounts for it
- exit-code mapping: VmIdPathBudgetExceeded surfaces a distinct CLI exit code (or maps to the existing config-error code per CLAUDE.md exhaustive-mapping rule)

title: Resolved: fake firecracker writes /firecracker.pid
description:
Fake Firecracker phase injection cannot be a shell script under the real jailer. The jailer chroots before execing Firecracker, so a script fake depends on /bin/sh and loader/libs that are not present in the jail root; that short-circuits at FirecrackerPidTimeout before the intended api-socket-timeout or cgroup-create-failure phase.

Fix: write_fake_firecracker now compiles a tiny static C ELF at test runtime. The fake writes /firecracker.pid from inside the jail, then pauses forever without creating firecracker.sock. That makes m80-jailer cross the pid-file boundary and lets the lifecycle tests exercise the intended downstream phase.

title: m80 logs <vm>: unified tail of guest console + host diagnostics
description:

- m80 logs <vm> on a stopped VM dumps the full interleaved log.

- Filter by request_id returns only matching lines (zero false positives).

title: streaming/PTY truncation flag never set; CAPTURE_LIMIT not enforced
description:
site: crates/m80-guestd/src/connection/{streaming.rs:253, pty.rs:344}
finder: trim-the-fat r5

Problem: Both `ExecExit::truncated` and `PtyExit::truncated` are set to `false` unconditionally. There is NO CAPTURE_LIMIT enforcement in the streaming path — the host receives all bytes regardless of size. The buffered `exec()` path enforces a limit via the wrapper closure (#2 / m80-hxur).

Fix: either (a) wire up a CAPTURE_LIMIT to streaming and set the flag when crossed, or (b) document explicitly that streaming has no cap and update README to say so. Pick whichever matches actual security/operator expectations.

title: m80-proto + m80-guestd: FileMkdir verb (with optional mode, recursive flag)
description:
m80's host-driven file-op surface is FileRead/Write/List/Stat/Remove + chunked write begin/chunk/commit. There is NO mkdir verb. Host callers wanting to create directories must round-trip via ExecRequest (`mkdir -p /path`) — a separate request, process spawn, exit-code parsing.

## Why this matters now (the conveyor-belt case)

The Bestiary's per-tenant drive-attach workflow needs to bootstrap workspace structure: /workspace/.cache, /workspace/output, fixture directories, etc. Today that's an exec per directory — 30-50 ms each on the request path. With FileMkdir it's a single envelope (~5-15 ms). Multi-dir bootstrap is a real cost the m80-iswt request-path pays today.

This isn't speculative — it's the exact use case in docs/future-directions/bestiary-conveyor-belt.md.

## Scope

m80-proto:
- FileMkdirRequest { path: String, mode: Option<u32>, recursive: bool }
- FileMkdirResponse { created: bool, error: Option<FileError> }

m80-guestd:
- file_ops handler that calls fs::create_dir or fs::create_dir_all per `recursive`.
- mode applied via fs::Permissions after creation.
- Honor the same path-canonicalization / safety rules as other file-ops (no .. traversal, etc.).

## Acceptance
- FileMkdirRequest creates the directory at the given path with the specified mode.
- recursive=true creates parent directories as needed (mkdir -p analog).
- recursive=false fails with a typed FileError if the parent doesn't exist.
- Idempotent on existing directories: returns created=false, error=None when the path already exists with the requested mode (or returns AlreadyExists with explicit decision in IMPL — pick and document).
- Permissions verifiable via FileStat after creation.

## Out of scope (deferred unless needed)
- Chown variant: m80 runs as a single uid/gid in the guest (typically root). Per-dir ownership doesn't help in the current model. Add later if multi-user-in-guest becomes a thing.
- rmdir on non-empty directories: FileRemove rejects directories today; if recursive directory removal is needed, file separately.

## Audit reference
20-agent deep audit Lens K5.7 (kata-agent file-op directory ops), 2026-05-07. kata's rpc.rs:2158-2164 supports directory creation with set_permissions + chown. This bead picks up the create-and-mode part; chown deferred per scope above.

title: Define JoinNetns guest NIC attachment contract
description:
m80-mx2t.3 asks for a functional JoinNetns E2E where guest traffic routes through a caller-created netns. The current JoinNetns implementation only passes --netns to the official Firecracker jailer so the VMM process enters the namespace; preboot emits no NetworkInterfaceConfig, no TAP is created inside or moved into that namespace, and the guest sees no NIC.

Before a functional guest-traffic E2E can be honest, m80 needs an explicit hard-cutover contract for how JoinNetns supplies a guest NIC. Decide and implement one shape, likely either: (a) m80 creates/configures a TAP inside the caller netns from a supplied guest IPv4/MAC/gateway contract, or (b) caller provides an already-created TAP/device descriptor and m80 only wires Firecracker. Update m80-net-mode, m80-firecracker, m80-jailer docs/READMEs, and real-KVM tests in the same diff.

Acceptance: JoinNetns launch creates or consumes a concrete guest NIC according to the chosen contract; Firecracker gets a network-interface PUT for that NIC; a real-KVM test proves a guest can reach a veth peer available only inside the joined netns; NoEgress and AllowOutbound behavior remain unchanged.

title: Warm-pool / Blank VM Allocator (active v0.2 clean-VM latency path)
description:
Warm-pool / blank-VM allocator for sub-200 ms clean-VM allocation on the request path. The snapshot-restore primitive is now captured under m80-rrp.3 with measured restore latency of 274.204 ms P50 idle and 444.972 ms P50 loaded; that is too high to put directly on every clean stateless request. The remaining warm-pool goal is to pre-restore guestd-ready slots ahead of demand and hand them out cheaply.

Current active sequence:

1. m80-rrp.1: reset evidence vocabulary. Reuse requires explicit proof; any missing or ambiguous input discards the VM.
2. m80-rrp.2: non-inference rule. Liveness, sockets, metrics, or clean-looking dirs never imply reusable state.
3. m80-rrp.4: design allocator contract, state machine, targets, and sizing model.
4. m80-rrp.5: implement fill / lease / discard / refill.
5. m80-rrp.6: benchmark request-path allocation latency idle and loaded.

Relationship: persistent VMs (m80-qokt.2) are now implemented and measured around 20.6 ms for stateful turn-to-turn sessions. Warm pool is for clean stateless calls where persistence is wrong. Adapter-level routing remains outside m80 core.

title: Snapshot-restore launch path: 0-boot via firecracker snapshot
description:
Wire m80-snapshot's capture()/restore() execution lane to Firecracker's snapshot REST endpoints. Today the schemas + persistence-path helpers are active in v0.1 but capture() and restore() return SnapshotError::Deferred; this bead replaces those stubs with real plumbing.

## Scope

Snapshot CAPTURE/RESTORE PLUMBING ONLY. Specifically:

- m80-firecracker-client: add put_snapshot_create + put_snapshot_load REST methods + their config types (CreateSnapshot, LoadSnapshot)
- m80-snapshot: real capture() that pauses the VM, calls CreateSnapshot, writes the manifest + restore-metadata, and verifies the artifact set; real restore() that reads the manifest, validates compat (firecracker version + image identity), and orchestrates the LoadSnapshot REST call
- m80-firecracker: a Sandbox::launch_from_snapshot(...) alternative path that skips the cold-boot phases (3,4 partial,11) and instead PUTs LoadSnapshot then InstanceStart-from-snapshot, joining the regular Phase 12b ready-probe path
- m80-cli: m80 launch --from-snapshot <path> wired to the new code path
- Bench: P50/P95 of restore-launched ready latency on idle + loaded host
- Docs: suitability bounds (stale clocks, pre-baked process trees) + compat-check decisions

## NOT in scope (other m80-rrp children)

- Warm-pool management (allocator that holds N pre-restored VMs ready)
- Eviction policy / pool sizing / refill triggers
- Allocation contract surface (lease / handoff to caller)
- Reset-evidence vocabulary integration with restored VMs

This bead delivers the primitive; m80-rrp.4+ (TBD) consumes it for warm pools.

## Acceptance

- m80-firecracker-client exposes put_snapshot_create + put_snapshot_load with fixture-server tests
- m80-snapshot capture() and restore() return Ok in happy-path; SnapshotError::Deferred is removed
- A Sandbox can be launched from a captured snapshot end-to-end on real-KVM (gated behind the existing end_to_end_real_kvm flag)
- m80 launch --from-snapshot <path> works in the CLI
- Bench numbers landed in docs/behaviors/snapshot/restore-latency.md
- README updates for m80-snapshot (capture/restore active), m80-firecracker-client (snapshot endpoints), m80-firecracker (launch_from_snapshot), m80-cli

## Open design questions, captured in leaves

- Capture preconditions: does the VM need to be Paused? Is snapshot a stop-the-world primitive vs concurrent? (DESIGN leaf)
- Compat checks at restore: firecracker version (already in RestoreMetadata), kernel sha, rootfs sha, machine-config (vcpu/mem) — what's the minimum viable check, what produces silent corruption on mismatch? (DESIGN leaf)
- Vsock state across snapshot: does the in-VM guestd's vsock channel survive a snapshot/restore? (research leaf, may overlap with DESIGN)
- Are CreateSnapshot/LoadSnapshot covered by Firecracker's stable API guarantees, or version-pinned? (DESIGN leaf)

## Relationship

This + minimal-init (m80-6a0q) together get end-to-end agent-ready VMs in roughly 300ms steady-state. SmolVM has snapshots too at ~500ms; with both pieces m80 should beat them at roughly half the latency. Warm-pool management on top (other m80-rrp children) makes that latency the steady-state for every exec, not just the second one.
notes: Update 2026-05-04 (post-kata recon): differentiation is stronger than the smolvm framing alone implied. Kata-containers ALSO did not wire firecracker's snapshot REST API — their FC backend's PauseVM/SaveVM/ResumeVM are silent no-ops; their 'VM factory' is QEMU-only and uses QEMU migration machinery (migrate exec:cat>file), not snapshot. No production runtime we surveyed (smolvm libkrun, kata-containers) has a working firecracker snapshot lifecycle. m80-rrp.3 is unclaimed territory in the firecracker microVM space. See kata-exploration/09-snapshot-templates-lifecycle.md and kata-exploration/00-synthesis.md.

title: DESIGN: snapshot capture/restore preconditions and compat-check matrix
description:
Pin down the Firecracker REST contract for CreateSnapshot/LoadSnapshot before writing client or orchestrator code. Output is a doc at docs/behaviors/snapshot/firecracker-rest-contract.md plus design notes on each open question.

## Topics to nail down

1. CAPTURE preconditions
   - Does the VM need to be in Paused state before CreateSnapshot? (Firecracker docs say yes — confirm and note exact REST sequence.)
   - Is snapshot a stop-the-world primitive (vCPU paused, memory frozen) or can it run concurrently? Document the stall window callers see.
   - What CreateSnapshot fields exist (snapshot_path, mem_file_path, snapshot_type [Full/Diff], version)? Map them to SnapshotManifest artifact paths.

2. RESTORE preconditions
   - LoadSnapshot REST flow: which PUTs are skipped vs still required (boot-source, drives, vsock — does any of this come from the snapshot, or must we re-PUT)?
   - LoadSnapshot fields (snapshot_path, mem_backend [File/Uffd], enable_diff_snapshots, resume_vm).
   - What state is the VM in immediately after LoadSnapshot — Paused, Running, or do we need a separate Resume action?
   - vsock state across snapshot: does the in-VM guestd's vsock channel survive? If not, we need a guestd reconnection protocol — out of scope here, capture as a follow-up bead.

3. COMPAT MATRIX at restore time
   - expected_firecracker_version is already in RestoreMetadata. Must restore() reject mismatches? (Yes — Firecracker doesn't guarantee snapshot compat across versions.)
   - kernel sha: if the captured-VM's kernel differs from the to-restore kernel, what fails (silent corruption vs guaranteed crash)? Add kernel_sha256 to RestoreMetadata?
   - rootfs sha: same question — restore on a different rootfs is almost certainly broken.
   - machine-config: vcpu_count + mem_size_mib must match the captured VM. Add to RestoreMetadata?
   - Recommendation for v0.2: minimum compat check is firecracker_version + kernel_sha + mem_size_mib. Document the gaps and what they protect against.

4. ARTIFACT path layout
   - Map ArtifactKind variants (BootIdentity, Memory, RuntimeRootfs, VmState, WorkspaceScratch) to concrete on-disk filenames inside the persistence dir. SnapshotManifest already names them; pin the file basenames here so capture() and restore() agree.

## Output

- docs/behaviors/snapshot/firecracker-rest-contract.md — the REST flow
- Updates to RestoreMetadata schema if compat fields need adding (do this here, before the impl leaves; schema changes are cheap pre-impl)
- A research note on vsock-across-snapshot (likely 'guestd must reconnect; out of scope for this bead — file follow-up')

## Tests

- Schema-roundtrip update if RestoreMetadata gains fields
- No code-runtime tests in this leaf — it's a design output that the IMPL leaves consume.

## Dependencies

Blocks all IMPL leaves under m80-rrp.3.

title: IMPL m80-snapshot: replace Deferred in capture() and restore() with real wiring
description:
Replace the SnapshotError::Deferred stubs in m80-snapshot::capture() and m80-snapshot::restore() with real implementations that call through m80-firecracker-client.

## capture() new signature (proposed; refine in DESIGN leaf)

pub fn capture(running: &mut RunningSandbox, store_root: &Path) -> Result<SnapshotManifest, SnapshotError>

## capture() semantics

1. Pause the VM (InstanceAction::Pause via running's existing Client).
2. Compute the persistence path (use existing persistence_path helper).
3. Resolve destination collision -> SnapshotError::DestinationCollision (do NOT silently overwrite).
4. PUT /snapshot/create with snapshot_path = <dest>/vmstate, mem_file_path = <dest>/memory.
5. Capture/copy the runtime rootfs clone + workspace scratch into the dest dir (these are live ext4 files; consider O_RDONLY copy or fs-level snapshot — DESIGN leaf decides).
6. Compute artifact set sha256s, build SnapshotManifest, write manifest + RestoreMetadata.
7. Resume the VM (InstanceAction::Resume).
8. Return the manifest.

## restore() new signature

pub fn restore(snapshot_dir: &Path, expected_firecracker_version: &str, expected_kernel_sha: Option<&str>) -> Result<RestoreMetadata, SnapshotError>

restore() in m80-snapshot is the manifest-validation + compat-check half. The actual REST orchestration lives in m80-firecracker (next leaf). This split keeps m80-snapshot dependency-free of the orchestrator.

## restore() semantics

1. Read snapshot-manifest.json + restore-metadata.json (existing helpers).
2. Verify all artifact sha256s against on-disk files (NEW — schema is active in v0.1 but verify-on-read is a v0.2 contract per the README).
3. Compat check: expected_firecracker_version + (optional) expected_kernel_sha against RestoreMetadata. Fail-closed with new SnapshotError variants:
   - FirecrackerVersionMismatch { expected, found }
   - KernelShaMismatch { expected, found }
   - Sha256Mismatch { artifact: ArtifactKind, expected, found }
4. Return RestoreMetadata for the orchestrator to consume.

## SnapshotError additions

- FirecrackerVersionMismatch { expected: String, found: String }
- KernelShaMismatch { expected: String, found: String }
- Sha256Mismatch { artifact: ArtifactKind, expected: String, found: String }
- (consider) PauseFailed / ResumeFailed for the capture side; alternatively reclassify firecracker-client errors via #[from]. CLAUDE.md prefers symmetric reclassification — pick one and apply uniformly.

The README explicitly notes Sha256Mismatch + FirecrackerVersionMismatch are NOT v0.1 — this leaf is the v0.2 promotion.

## Tests

- tests/capture_happy_path.rs — fixture firecracker UDS server records the Pause/CreateSnapshot/Resume sequence; asserts artifact files exist + sha256s match.
- tests/restore_compat_check.rs — manifest with mismatched expected_firecracker_version returns FirecrackerVersionMismatch; same for kernel sha.
- tests/restore_artifact_sha_mismatch.rs — tamper with one artifact byte; restore returns Sha256Mismatch carrying the offending ArtifactKind.
- Drop tests/deferred_capture_and_restore.rs (Deferred is going away).

title: IMPL m80-firecracker: Sandbox::launch_from_snapshot alternative path + Sandbox::capture_running
description:
Wire the snapshot capture/restore execution lane through the orchestrator. Two surfaces:

1. RunningSandbox::capture(&mut self, store_root: &Path) -> Result<SnapshotManifest, FcError> — pauses the VM, calls m80-snapshot::capture(), resumes. Thin wrapper; the heavy lifting is in m80-snapshot.

2. Sandbox::launch_from_snapshot(self, snapshot_dir: &Path) -> Result<RunningSandbox, FcError> — alternative to launch() that skips the cold-boot phases.

## launch_from_snapshot phases

Re-uses phases 1 (run-root prep), 2 (lease), 4 (jailer materialize — needs the same kernel + rootfs bind-mounts), 5 (cgroup probe), 8 (api socket path), 9 (jailer exec firecracker), 5b (cgroup create), 10 (open UDS), 12b (ready probe).

REPLACES phase 3 (storage prep) + phase 6/7 (network) + phase 11 (REST PUTs) + phase 12a (InstanceStart):

- Phase 3': storage from snapshot — clone the captured rootfs.ext4 + scratch.ext4 from the snapshot dir into the run-dir (NOT the base rootfs from manifest). Compat check happens in m80-snapshot::restore() before this.
- Phase 11': PUT /snapshot/load (with resume_vm=true, OR resume_vm=false followed by InstanceAction::Resume — DESIGN leaf decides).
- No InstanceStart from snapshot — Firecracker's LoadSnapshot replaces the cold InstanceStart.

## SandboxConfig field

Decision question (resolve in DESIGN leaf): does launch_from_snapshot take snapshot_dir as a separate function arg, or do we add SandboxConfig.from_snapshot: Option<PathBuf> and gate on it inside launch()?

Recommendation: separate function. Cleaner branch-on-config-field pattern is exactly the kind of premature abstraction CLAUDE.md prohibits ('three near-identical lines beat a generic helper'). launch() and launch_from_snapshot() share helpers but are top-level distinct entry points.

title: BENCH: P50/P95 of restore-launched ready latency on idle and loaded host
description:
Quantify the steady-state launch-latency win. Establish the numbers that justify the bead. Document them in docs/behaviors/snapshot/restore-latency.md.

## Bench scope

For a fixed (kernel, rootfs, machine-config) golden snapshot:

1. Idle host
   - Cold boot: m80 launch end-to-end (Phase 1 → ready) — P50/P95 over 50 runs.
   - Restore boot: m80 launch --from-snapshot end-to-end — P50/P95 over 50 runs.
   - Report the gap (target: roughly 5-10x; AWS docs say <200ms restore vs 800-1500ms cold).

2. Loaded host
   - Same two measurements while the host is running 8 concurrent VMs at idle.
   - Watch for restore-time tail latency from disk I/O contention (memory file copy is the long pole).

## What to measure precisely

- 'Ready' = phase_12b_ready_probe returns Ok (vsock channel open, guestd handshake completed).
- Bench timing should NOT include CLI parse + preflight; start the timer at Sandbox::launch / Sandbox::launch_from_snapshot call site.
- Capture the per-phase breakdown for 1-2 representative runs (which phase dominates? Probably phase 9 jailer-exec for cold; phase 11' snapshot-load for restore).

## Tooling

- Use criterion or a hand-rolled bench in crates/m80-firecracker/benches/. Real-KVM only — gated behind the same flag as end_to_end_real_kvm.
- Output: P50, P95, P99, mean, stddev. JSON output committed to docs/behaviors/snapshot/restore-latency.json + a markdown summary in restore-latency.md.

## Compare with SmolVM

If feasible, run the same bench script against SmolVM (snapshot mode) on the same host. Report the comparison. If not feasible (SmolVM not installed / different harness), cite SmolVM's published numbers (~500ms snapshot-restore) and frame m80 as 'expected ~2-3x faster steady-state' from the combined m80-rrp.3 + m80-6a0q (minimal-init) work.

## Dependencies

- m80-rrp.3.4 (the launch_from_snapshot path) — required to bench at all
- m80-rrp.3.5 nice-to-have but not required (bench can call the library directly)

## Acceptance

- restore-latency.md committed with idle + loaded P50/P95 numbers
- restore-latency.json committed with raw run data
- Bench harness committed under crates/m80-firecracker/benches/ (or m80-cli/) — re-runnable
- Numbers validate (or refute) the bead's claim of 'steady-state ~300ms'

## Open question

Should this bead also bench warm-pool steady-state? NO — warm-pool is m80-rrp's other children. This bench measures the snapshot-restore primitive in isolation.

title: DOCS: suitability bounds, compat matrix, and CHANGELOG entry
description:
The wrapper-up doc work. Make the new surface discoverable and document what restore-launched VMs are and aren't suitable for.

## Output 1: docs/behaviors/snapshot/suitability.md

Document the trade-offs:

- Stale clocks: a snapshot-restored VM resumes with the captured wall-clock — guestd, agents, and any process that cares about 'what time is it' will see a clock that jumped. Useful for short-lived agent execs (seconds to minutes); broken for long-running daemons that sync time, schedule cron, or rely on monotonic clock continuity.
- Pre-baked process tree: every restore reuses the captured VM's pid namespace and process state. Side-effects from the captured boot (named-pipe state, in-memory locks, /tmp content) carry through. Document as 'fine for stateless agents, requires reset-evidence-vocabulary discipline (m80-rrp.1) for reuse-after-mutation'.
- DNS / network state: any cached resolver state from the captured VM is restored. For NoEgress this is a non-issue; for OutboundNat (v0.2) callers should plan to flush.
- Filesystem state: the captured rootfs and scratch are cloned into a fresh per-restore copy, so the guest sees a private writable copy.

## Output 2: docs/behaviors/snapshot/compat-matrix.md

Document the compat checks that restore() enforces and which it doesn't:

- ENFORCED at restore: firecracker_version exact match, kernel_sha256 exact match, mem_size_mib match, vcpu_count match.
- NOT ENFORCED: host kernel version, host CPU microcode, /proc/cpuinfo features (CPUID). Note these as 'undefined behavior on mismatch'.
- (Tighten this list per the DESIGN leaf m80-rrp.3.1 outcome.)

## Output 3: CHANGELOG.md entry

Under the v0.2 section (or wherever appropriate):

- Added: SnapshotCreateConfig + SnapshotLoadConfig + REST methods on m80-firecracker-client (m80-rrp.3.2)
- Added: m80-snapshot::capture and ::restore now active (was Deferred); new error variants FirecrackerVersionMismatch / KernelShaMismatch / Sha256Mismatch (m80-rrp.3.3)
- Added: Sandbox::launch_from_snapshot + RunningSandbox::capture (m80-rrp.3.4)
- Added: m80 launch --from-snapshot and m80 snapshot capture (m80-rrp.3.5)
- Bench: P50 ~300ms restore-launched ready (m80-rrp.3.6) — fill in actual number.

## README updates already-in-other-leaves

Each IMPL leaf already updates its own crate's README (CLAUDE.md mandate). This leaf is for the cross-cutting docs that don't belong to one crate.

## Dependencies

title: IMPL m80-firecracker: pre-create vsock UDS at snapshot-load time
description:
When you LoadSnapshot, the host vsock UDS that existed at snapshot-capture time is gone (different run-root, different Sandbox instance). The guest's in-memory vsock state still expects the muxer companion files at <host_sock_path>_<port>. The host has to pre-create the listener BEFORE InstanceStart-from-snapshot, otherwise guest-initiated connects fault.

## Scope

- Sandbox::launch_from_snapshot (m80-rrp.3.4) must allocate the vsock UDS path + bind UnixListener for each known port BEFORE issuing the LoadSnapshot REST call.
- The set of "known ports" is whatever the snapshot manifest captured (guestd control port, plus any reserved ports for ready-probe / m80-7tpy).
- Verify that firecracker's muxer accepts a fresh UDS path on snapshot resume; document any constraints in the snapshot manifest schema (m80-snapshot).

## Acceptance

- launch_from_snapshot survives a guest-initiated vsock connect post-restore (host accept() returns).
- A regression test pins this: snapshot a VM with an active vsock connection, restore, verify the guest can reconnect.
- m80-snapshot README documents the host's pre-create responsibility.

## Sibling

Guestd-side companion bead (post-restore connection-drop detection + redial) tracks separately under m80-rrp.3.
close_reason: superseded by empirical snapshot design and implemented restore path: remove stale vsock.sock, Firecracker rebinds on load, host probes a fresh exec channel; guest listener survives so no guest redial/pre-create leaf remains

title: IMPL m80-guestd: detect post-restore vsock connection drop and redial
description:
After snapshot/restore, any in-flight vsock connection from guestd to host is severed (the host UDS is a fresh inode, even after the host-side pre-create in m80-rrp.3.8). Guestd needs to detect the drop and redial — without panicking, without losing the agent's in-VM state.

## Scope

- Guestd's vsock client: on read/write error indicating peer-closed, attempt redial with bounded backoff.
- Detection mechanism: rely on AF_VSOCK error semantics (likely EPIPE / ECONNRESET); avoid heartbeat-pinging.
- Redial preserves any per-connection state guestd was tracking (request_id correlation, in-flight stream framing).
- Document the edge case: if guestd was streaming exec output when snapshot fired, the partial frame is lost — caller must handle re-exec.

## Acceptance

- A regression test: capture a snapshot mid-execution, restore, verify guestd reconnects and accepts a new request.
- guestd does not exit(1) or panic on vsock peer-close; it retries with bounded backoff and only exits if reconnect fails for >N seconds.
- m80-guestd README documents the post-restore redial contract.

## Sibling

Host-side companion at m80-rrp.3.8.
close_reason: superseded by empirical snapshot design and implemented restore path: remove stale vsock.sock, Firecracker rebinds on load, host probes a fresh exec channel; guest listener survives so no guest redial/pre-create leaf remains

title: DESIGN: warm-pool allocator contract, targets, and sizing model
description:
Design the warm-pool layer that consumes the snapshot-restore primitive and presents a measured clean-VM allocation contract. This bead does not implement pooling; it locks the public shape, state machine, and success criteria before code lands.

## Current evidence

- Persistent sequential exec is measured at roughly 20.6 ms P50/P95 for stateful sessions.
- Snapshot restore is measured at 274.204 ms P50 / 280.132 ms P95 idle, and 444.972 ms P50 / 588.221 ms P95 loaded, with a long loaded tail.
- Cold launch remains seconds-scale; stripped kernel only buys about 100 ms. The warm path must be pool allocation, not more cold-boot trimming.

## Scope

- Define the allocator contract in m80-firecracker terms: a pool owns pre-restored, guestd-ready RunningSandbox slots and hands out one clean slot per allocation.
- Define slot states: Filling, Ready, Leased, Draining, Discarded, with explicit transitions and ownership.
- Define reset evidence required before a leased VM can ever re-enter Ready; if evidence is absent or ambiguous, discard the VM.
- Define pool sizing inputs: target concurrency, restore P50/P95, loaded-tail budget, memory-file footprint, run-root capacity, and refill latency.
- Define hard cutover from direct snapshot restore to warm-pool allocation for clean stateless calls; no compatibility shim or tolerant fallback hidden inside the allocator.
- Document when callers should use persistent VMs instead: stateful sessions with expected filesystem/process continuity.

## Non-goals

- Adapter-level tool semantics, idempotency, workspace policy, or EffectClass handling.
- Kubernetes placement, pod draining, or multi-host scheduling.
- Making Firecracker restore itself sub-200 ms under saturated host load; the pool absorbs restore variance by filling ahead of demand.

## Acceptance

- docs/design/warm-pool.md exists and states the allocator contract, slot state machine, reset/discard rules, and sizing formula.
- m80-firecracker README is updated if the public surface changes are decided here.
- Follow-up implementation and bench beads cite the final target numbers from this design.
- The design explicitly compares persistent VM, direct snapshot restore, and warm-pool allocation using the measured numbers above.

title: IMPL: warm-pool fill, lease, and discard path
description:
Implement the first warm-pool allocator path in m80-firecracker after the design bead lands. The allocator keeps pre-restored, guestd-ready VM slots available so clean stateless calls do not pay snapshot restore latency on the request path.

## Scope

- Add the minimal public surface selected by docs/design/warm-pool.md, likely a WarmPool or WarmSandboxPool owned by m80-firecracker.
- Pool startup fills N slots from a configured snapshot source using Sandbox::launch_from_snapshot.
- Allocation returns a Ready slot as a RunningSandbox-like lease/handoff object with clear ownership.
- Empty pool behavior is explicit and fail-closed: either return PoolEmpty/Unavailable or perform the design-approved synchronous fill. Do not hide a silent cold-boot fallback.
- Refill happens in the background after allocation/discard using bounded concurrency and the existing admission/run-root limits.
- Release path either proves reset evidence and returns to Ready, or discards the VM and schedules replacement. Ambiguous state discards.
- Teardown stops all owned slots without leaking Firecracker, jailer, vsock UDS, overlay, scratch, or snapshot artifacts.

## Non-goals

- Adapter-level routing between persistent VM and warm-pool VM.
- Multi-host placement or Kubernetes pod lifecycle.
- Sophisticated eviction policy beyond the design-approved first rule.

## Acceptance

- Unit/state-machine tests cover Filling -> Ready -> Leased -> Discarded/refilled transitions and empty-pool behavior.
- A real-KVM ignored integration test allocates a pre-restored slot and successfully execs without calling the cold launch path.
- A leak regression test shows pool drop cleans all run-root resources it owns.
- m80-firecracker README documents the new public surface and non-goals.
- No hidden compatibility fallback to cold boot exists inside allocation.

title: BENCH: warm-pool allocation latency idle and loaded
description:
Measure the actual request-path cost of allocating from a pre-filled warm pool. This is the benchmark that proves whether m80 reaches the sub-200 ms clean-VM target in the path callers will actually use.

## Scope

- Add or extend a benchmark under crates/m80-firecracker/benches/ that pre-fills a pool, then measures allocation -> first successful exec -> release/discard.
- Run idle and loaded cells. Loaded should use the existing stress-ng shape so results compare with cold-launch and snapshot-restore data.
- Report P50, P95, max, success count, and pool-refill lag.
- Compare against the current measured baselines: persistent sequential exec ~20.6 ms, direct snapshot restore 274.204 ms P50 idle / 444.972 ms P50 loaded, and cold launch in docs/perf/cold-launch.md.
- Persist machine-readable output next to the existing behavior JSON snapshots, and summarize in docs/perf/cold-launch.md or a dedicated warm-pool perf doc.

## Acceptance

- N >= 50 idle allocations from a pre-filled pool produce P50/P95/max and success count.
- N >= 50 loaded allocations produce the same metrics, or the doc records a diagnostics-first failure with logs/artifacts.
- The benchmark distinguishes request-path allocation latency from background refill latency.
- docs/behaviors/lifecycle or docs/behaviors/snapshot includes a JSON artifact with the exact numbers.
- CHANGELOG records the measured result, including whether sub-200 ms was achieved.

title: m80 quickstart: first-30s constrained-process UX
description:
Split first-touch UX from CI verification. Quickstart targets clean machine -> artifacts/profile -> `m80 run -- echo hello` quickly; smoke targets CI exit codes.

Why:
- The product story is no longer "launch a VM". It is "run a process with a constrained view of the host". Quickstart must teach that from the first command.
- The gap is mostly missing prebuilts, no default image/profile story, and no quickstart path.

Scope:
- scripts/quickstart.sh downloads the latest release tarball, verifies sha256s, places kernel/rootfs/manifest in expected paths, resolves the default image/profile, runs `m80 run -- echo hello`, and prints next-step pointers for `--workspace`, `--egress none`, `--tty`, image/profile selection, and `warm` if available.
- `m80 quickstart` or equivalent in-binary entrypoint may perform the same flow without requiring shell access.
- README top fold points at the quickstart command.

Out of scope:
- CI smoke remains separate.
- No interactive prompts; quickstart is non-interactive end-to-end.
- No agent-specific setup.

Acceptance:
- A clean machine with no m80 checkout can run the documented invocation and see `hello` from `m80 run -- echo hello` in less than 60s wall clock, assuming release artifacts exist.
- README documents quickstart and points at it from the top fold.
- smoke and quickstart have zero overlapping logic.
- Quickstart docs use constrained-process and image/profile vocabulary, not VM lifecycle vocabulary.

Dependency:
- Blocked by m80-6jni.3 or equivalent prebuilt artifact release lane plus the command/profile docs that define the final surface.

title: Marker-file readiness probe to beat SmolVM's polling latency
description:
Replace m80-firecracker's `phase_12b_ready_probe` polling loop with a
stat-based marker probe — IF Firecracker actually creates a host-visible
file when m80-guestd binds its vsock listener. Verification is gating;
see leaf 1.

## Background

Today's `phase_12b_ready_probe`
(crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch.rs:423):
- Calls `Channel::open_uds_only` (UDS connect + write `CONNECT 9001`
  + read `OK` line) every 500ms with a 30s deadline. The 5s
  read timeout caps each attempt.
- Each successful attempt is roughly a UDS handshake's worth of work.
- Under host load the probe occasionally times out before guestd binds.

SmolVM's `wait_for_ssh`:
- `socket.connect()` + 32-byte banner sniff at 100ms intervals,
  then full handshake once the banner appears. 60s budget.

## Marker-file premise — UNVERIFIED

The dossier hypothesis: when m80-guestd does
`VsockListener::bind((VMADDR_CID_ANY, 9001))`, Firecracker creates the
host-side companion file `<vsock_uds>_<port>` (e.g.
`<jail>/vsock.sock_9001`) inside the chroot, and stat'ing that file is
a near-zero-cost readiness signal.

CAUTION — Firecracker's official vsock docs
(https://github.com/firecracker-microvm/firecracker/blob/main/docs/vsock.md)
describe `<uds>_<port>` only in the *opposite* direction: as the file
the **host application** is expected to be listening on so that
**guest-initiated** connections can be forwarded by Firecracker. There
is no documented host filesystem artifact created when the guest binds
a port and waits for host-initiated connects (which is the m80
direction). Firecracker's vsock muxer connects to that path; it does
not create one on guest bind.

Leaf 1 (VERIFY) must close this gap before any other leaf is started.
If verification shows the file is not created, the bead pivots:
- Plan A (file-stat probe) is dropped.
- m80-bgas (100ms / 60s constants) ships as the only `phase_12b`
  improvement, and m80-6gv9 (inotify) folds into a new file-watch
  target — likely the serial console + `GUESTD_READY` marker once
  `PUT /logger` is wired (a v0.2 epic).

## Design (conditional on verification passing)

Replace `phase_12b_ready_probe`'s polling loop with two phases:
1. Stat for `<vsock_uds>_<port>` at 10ms intervals (~1µs/probe vs the
   current full handshake cost). Existence => guest has bound.
2. Once the file appears, do the existing CONNECT/OK handshake one
   shot. The 5s read timeout still catches a guest that bound but
   never called accept().

The fallback-to-CONNECT/OK after stat returns is intentional: it
covers "bind succeeded but accept() not yet ready" without wedging
the probe. It is NOT premature complication.

## Brittleness contract

The companion-file naming is a Firecracker implementation detail, not
a stable API. The probe must:
- Document the exact Firecracker version range under which the naming
  was verified (in m80-vsock README under a new "Readiness contract"
  section).
- Keep CONNECT/OK as a hard fallback so a future Firecracker that
  changes the naming degrades to today's behavior, not failure.
- Re-verify on Firecracker upgrade as an explicit checklist item.

## Quick wins independent of this change

Tracked in m80-bgas (sibling): drop poll interval 500ms -> 100ms,
raise budget 30s -> 60s. m80-bgas should land first as a backstop.

## Acceptance (rolled-up)

- Leaf 1 verifies (or refutes) host-visible companion-file creation
  on a real KVM host under the in-tree Firecracker version.
- If verification passes: `phase_12b` uses the stat probe; CONNECT/OK
  becomes a one-shot post-stat handshake; latency from `InstanceStart`
  PUT to `Channel` returning `Ok` < 1s on idle host.
- m80-vsock README and m80-firecracker README updated to document the
  new readiness contract and its brittleness.
- Smoke test still passes; the simulated-load flake disappears or is
  documented as out-of-scope.

## Sibling beads

- m80-bgas (P2): the polling-constants-only quick win. Lands first.
- m80-6gv9 (P2): inotify upgrade. Stacks on top of m80-tv7i.
close_reason: premise-refuted: Firecracker creates `<uds>_<port>` only when GUEST initiates outbound (see firecracker muxer.rs:619-641). Host-side stat-poll on guest bind() is impossible. Empirical confirmed: 25s lifecycle observation showed only `vsock.sock` exists, no `vsock.sock_9001`. Verification: docs/verifications/m80-tv7i.1-vsock-companion-file.md. Pivot: m80-7tpy becomes primary readiness path (its mechanism is exactly what the source code supports — host pre-listens on `<uds>_<port>`, guest connects out).

description:
Gating leaf for m80-tv7i. Before any implementation work, verify on a
real KVM host that Firecracker creates a host-visible file at
`<vsock_uds>_<port>` when (and only when) m80-guestd executes
`VsockListener::bind((VMADDR_CID_ANY, 9001))`.

## Why this is the first leaf

Firecracker's documented vsock semantics describe `<uds>_<port>` as
the **host-side listener** for **guest-initiated** outbound
connections, not as an artifact of a guest bind. If verification
refutes the premise, the rest of m80-tv7i must be re-planned (likely
collapsing to m80-bgas + a future serial-console-watch leaf under
m80-6gv9 once `PUT /logger` is wired).

Do NOT skip this leaf. Do NOT start IMPL until this leaf is closed.

## Procedure

1. Boot the existing `end_to_end_real_kvm` test to a Running
   sandbox (or run `scripts/smoke.sh` once and pause it before
   `stop()` — easiest way to get a live VM).
2. Locate the host-side jail directory:
   `<run_root>/<vm_id>/firecracker/<vm_id>/root/`
3. Stat the candidate companion path:
   `<jail>/vsock.sock_9001`
4. Record three observations on a real KVM host running the
   in-tree Firecracker version:
   - Does the path exist after `InstanceStart` returns?
   - Does it exist after the guest has bound but before any host
     CONNECT/OK?
   - When in the boot sequence does it first appear (timestamp
     vs `InstanceStart` PUT)?
5. Cross-check against a guest variant that does NOT bind port 9001
   (temporarily comment out the bind in m80-guestd, rebuild rootfs,
   relaunch). If the file appears anyway, the file is unrelated to
   guest bind.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Manual run on KVM host produces a yes/no answer with timestamps,
      captured in a comment on this bead via `br update --notes`.
- [ ] If yes: the exact path format and creation timing are recorded
      (e.g., "appears within 5ms of guestd `bind()`; persists until
      VM stop"). This unblocks the IMPL leaf.
- [ ] If no: this bead is closed with `--reason "premise-refuted"`,
      the parent m80-tv7i is closed with the same reason, and a new
      bead is filed under m80-6gv9 to investigate the
      `PUT /logger`-based serial console watch as the next-best
      latency win.
- [ ] No code changes land from this leaf — observation only.

## Files / paths

- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch.rs` — `phase_12b_ready_probe`,
  `vsock_uds = jail.jail_path.join("vsock.sock")`
- `crates/m80-guestd/src/main.rs:57` — `VsockListener::bind_with_cid_port(VMADDR_CID_ANY, port)`
- `scripts/smoke.sh` — easy harness for getting a Running VM
- Firecracker upstream vsock doc:
  https://github.com/firecracker-microvm/firecracker/blob/main/docs/vsock.md

## Out of scope

- Writing a Rust integration test (see TEST-INT leaf).
- Touching `phase_12b_ready_probe`.
- Documenting the contract in READMEs (see DOCS leaf).
close_reason: premise-refuted: Firecracker creates `<uds>_<port>` only when GUEST initiates outbound (see firecracker muxer.rs:619-641). Host-side stat-poll on guest bind() is impossible. Empirical confirmed: 25s lifecycle observation showed only `vsock.sock` exists, no `vsock.sock_9001`. Verification: docs/verifications/m80-tv7i.1-vsock-companion-file.md. Pivot: m80-7tpy becomes primary readiness path (its mechanism is exactly what the source code supports — host pre-listens on `<uds>_<port>`, guest connects out).

title: IMPL: stat-based two-phase ready probe in phase_12b
description:
Replace the polling loop in `phase_12b_ready_probe` with a two-phase
probe: stat the companion file, then do one CONNECT/OK handshake.

BLOCKED on m80-tv7i.1 (VERIFY) closing with a "yes" outcome.

## Today (crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch.rs:423)

- `READY_POLL_INTERVAL = 500ms`, `READY_TIMEOUT = 30s`
- Each loop iteration calls `Channel::open_uds_only` even when
  Firecracker has not yet seen guestd bind.

## After

- Phase A: stat `<vsock_uds_parent>/vsock.sock_<GUEST_PORT_DEFAULT>`
  at 10ms intervals until it exists, capped at the overall ready
  deadline.
- Phase B: a single `Channel::open_uds_only(vsock_uds, port)` call,
  reusing the existing 5s read timeout to catch a guest that bound
  but didn't `accept()`.
- New constants colocated with the existing ones:
  ```
  const STAT_POLL_INTERVAL: Duration = Duration::from_millis(10);
  ```
  Keep `READY_TIMEOUT` here — the budget is the parent's job; let
  m80-bgas own the 30s -> 60s change. No constants change here that
  m80-bgas also touches.
- The companion-port computation lives next to the probe (don't
  add a public `companion_path()` helper to m80-vsock yet — three
  near-identical lines beat a generic helper per CLAUDE.md).

## Fallback

If Phase A times out without the file appearing, fall back to a
single CONNECT/OK attempt before returning `VsockError::NotReady`.
Rationale: a future Firecracker that drops the companion file should
degrade to today's behavior, not fail outright. Document the
fallback as the brittleness escape hatch.

title: TEST-INT: real-KVM latency benchmark — InstanceStart -> Channel Ok < 1s
description:
Integration test that boots a real Firecracker VM and measures the
elapsed time from `InstanceAction::InstanceStart` PUT returning to
`phase_12b_ready_probe` returning `Ok(Channel)`. Pins the latency
target so a future regression (or a Firecracker version that drops
the companion file and forces fallback) is caught.

sibling `#[ignore]` test rather than touching the existing happy-path
test (the existing one stays a smoke; this one is a perf
characterization).

The test must:
- Run the same `Backend::new` + `admit` + `launch` path as the
  existing test.
- Capture an `Instant` immediately before `client.instance_action`

title: Per-VM rootfs cloning

[CLOSED 2026-05-04 — PREMISE REFUTED]

Original premise: each VM gets a private byte-for-byte copy of the base ext4 under its run-dir. title: Env var schema
description:
Contract: the accepted m80 env schema is exact and case-sensitive. Preflight discovery recognizes M80_FIRECRACKER_BIN, M80_FIRECRACKER_VERSION, M80_JAILER_BIN, M80_KERNEL_IMAGE, M80_ARTIFACT_DIR, M80_ROOTFS_IMAGE, M80_KERNEL_KIND, and M80_RUN_ROOT. Orchestrator config recognizes M80_MAX_CONCURRENT_VMS, M80_RUN_ROOT, M80_JAIL_UID, M80_JAIL_GID, and M80_CGROUP_MODE. Old predecessor-style names such as M80_FIRECRACKER_ROOTFS_IMAGE, M80_FIRECRACKER_RUN_ROOT, M80_FIRECRACKER_MAX_CONCURRENT_VMS, M80_VERSION, and M80_JAILER_MODE are not aliases.
